# Orthognathic surgery and orthodontics associated with orofacial harmonization: Case report

### Alessandra Kuhn Dall'Magro

### Letícia Copatti Dogenski

### Eduardo Dall'Magro

### Nicoly Schmidt Figur

### Micheline Sandini Trentin

### João Paulo De Carli

Corresponding author at: Av. Brasil Leste, 285, Prédia A7, Faculdade de Odontologia, São José, Passo Fundo ZIP Code: 99052-900, RS, Brazil. joaodecarli@upf.br

Received 2021 Apr 26; Revised 2021 May 20; Accepted 2021 May 21; Collection date 2021 Jun.

This is an open access article under the CC BY license (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

## Abstract

### Introduction and importance

Orthognathic surgery aims to restore the functional and esthetic standards of the face and non-surgical or minimally invasive procedures have been optimizing the results of facial orthosurgical treatments. This case report aimed to show the use of minimally invasive techniques that, associated with orthognathic surgery, represent a trend in current oral and maxillofacial rehabilitation.

### Case presentation

A female patient, 28 years old, white, sought care from the Dentistry team of the São Vicente de Paulo Hospital, in Passo Fundo, Brazil, complaining of mandibular prognathism, anteroposterior maxillary deficiency, dental crowding, malocclusion, functional and esthetic changes that negatively affected her psychosocial interactions and stomatognathic function. The treatment involved orthodontics, orthognathic surgery, and orofacial harmonization with dermal fillers.

### Clinical discussion

The multidisciplinarity among the specialties of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery and Traumatology, Orthodontics, and Orofacial Harmonization add and contribute to the process of planning and implementing the treatment proposed, as well as the prognosis toward patient satisfaction.

### Conclusion

The surgical procedure associated with minimally invasive facial harmonization not only corrected the functional complaint of the patient but also played an important role in improving facial harmony, contributing significantly to self-esteem.

**Keywords:** Orthognathic surgery, Orofacial harmonization, Orofacial esthetics, Case report

## Highlights

Minimally invasive facial harmonization refines orthognathic surgery techniques.

The integration of several disciplines helps to improve facial harmony.

Injectable fillers represent important allies in orthosurgical treatments.

## 1. Introduction and importance

Many patients seek dental and maxillofacial surgery not only to improve function but also for esthetic improvements in the smile or face. Therefore, orthognathic surgery has a potential impact on the quality of life, psychosocial well-being, facial esthetics, and oral function [[1](#bb0005)]. It is performed to correct dentoskeletal discrepancies and seek harmony between upper and lower jaws, improving occlusal function. Furthermore, it offers the benefits of improving the self-esteem, satisfaction, self-confidence, social functioning, and interpersonal relationships of patients [[2](#bb0010)].

The management of most orthognathic surgery cases includes preoperative orthodontics to decompose the dentition, followed by surgery and postoperative orthodontics [[1](#bb0005)]. After removing the dental compensations before surgery, this technique allows the optimal surgical repositioning of the mandible. In the search for satisfactory results in both function and post-surgical orofacial esthetics, the facial contouring with injectable fillers such as hyaluronic acid (HA) may serve as a complementary finishing touch to obtain volume correction, improving the shape and facial asymmetries. The main options for using these substances include eyebrow positioning, nasal tip elevation, jawline modeling, chin shape and definition, and lip eversion [[3](#bb0015)].

Thus, orofacial harmonization may integrate treatment plans to combine function, esthetics, and dental health, providing balance to a face that needs symmetry adjustments and balance between facial thirds. When carefully applied, injectable fillers provide an effective solution to several esthetic issues [[4](#bb0020)] and may represent important allies in orthosurgical treatments. Therefore, this study aims to show, through a case report, the multidisciplinary use of orthognathic surgery combined with orthodontics and minimally invasive techniques that, in association, present a trend in current oral and maxillofacial rehabilitation.

## 2. Case presentation

Written informed consent was obtained from the patient for publication of this case report and accompanying images. A copy of the written consent is available for review by the Editor-in-Chief of this journal on request. All applicable rules regarding the ethics of experimentation and research integrity were followed. This work has been reported in line with the SCARE 2020 [[5](#bb0025)] criteria.

Female patient, 28 years old, white, with good health, no history of drug use or any relevant family or genetic disease information, sought assistance from the Dentistry team at the São Vicente de Paulo Hospital, in Passo Fundo, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, for orofacial rehabilitation, complaining of mandibular prognathism, anteroposterior maxillary deficiency, dental crowding, malocclusion, and functional and esthetic changes (Angle Class III). The patient reported being disturbed by the lack of harmony on her face and the occlusal and functional problems developed over time due to the skeletal discrepancy that negatively affected her psychosocial interactions.

After an interdisciplinary evaluation, the treatment was planned according to the following sequence:

Phase 1 - Photos and initial documentation, followed by orthosurgical preparation with leveling, alignment, and coordination of the dental arches ([Figs. 1](#f0005) and [2](#f0010)).

### Fig. 1.

[![Fig. 1](https://cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/blobs/2e50/8178104/c52bee17fcd2/gr1.jpg)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/core/lw/2.0/html/tileshop_pmc/tileshop_pmc_inline.html?title=Click%20on%20image%20to%20zoom&p=PMC3&id=8178104_gr1.jpg)

![Fig. 1](https://cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/blobs/2e50/8178104/c52bee17fcd2/gr1.jpg)

Initial frontal photos at rest (1a), smiling (1b), profile (1c), and profile teleradiography (1d). Initial intraoral photos of the right side (1e), left side (1f), upper arch (1g), and lower arch (1h).

### Fig. 2.

[![Fig. 2](https://cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/blobs/2e50/8178104/26474339b3fb/gr2.jpg)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/core/lw/2.0/html/tileshop_pmc/tileshop_pmc_inline.html?title=Click%20on%20image%20to%20zoom&p=PMC3&id=8178104_gr2.jpg)

![Fig. 2](https://cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/blobs/2e50/8178104/26474339b3fb/gr2.jpg)

Photos after orthodontic preparation - leveling, dental alignment, and coordination of upper and lower arches in frontal view at rest (2a), smiling (2b), profile (2c), and profile teleradiography (2d). Intraoral photos after orthodontic preparation on the right side (2e), left side (2f), upper arch (2g), and lower arch (2h).

Phase 2 - Bimaxillary orthognathic surgery, lip filling with hyaluronic acid, and bichectomy at the same surgical time, aided by the Nemoceph™ software for surgical planning ([Fig. 3](#f0015)). After orthognathic surgery, the patient was instructed to remain at rest for 15 days, leaving only to attend the postoperative return visits once a week for six weeks. The patient was also instructed not to make any physical effort or to expose herself to the sun for 30 days, and to maintain a pasty diet for 40 days.

### Fig. 3.

[![Fig. 3](https://cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/blobs/2e50/8178104/c5ccb98f78fb/gr3.jpg)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/core/lw/2.0/html/tileshop_pmc/tileshop_pmc_inline.html?title=Click%20on%20image%20to%20zoom&p=PMC3&id=8178104_gr3.jpg)

![Fig. 3](https://cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/blobs/2e50/8178104/c5ccb98f78fb/gr3.jpg)

Virtual planning for predictive analysis through preoperative cephalometric evaluation of the Nemoceph™ software. An initial cephalometric analysis (3a) and cephalometric tracing for surgical planning (3b) were performed. Below, images of the operation with Le Fort I osteotomy in the maxilla (3c), sagittal mandible osteotomy (3d), and bichectomy (3e).

Phase 3 - Integrated dentolabial harmonization process and gingival plastic surgery with surgical laser 60 days after removing the orthodontic appliance and in-office tooth bleaching ([Figs. 4](#f0020) and [5](#f0025)).

### Fig. 4.

[![Fig. 4](https://cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/blobs/2e50/8178104/ef63d1ff60f2/gr4.jpg)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/core/lw/2.0/html/tileshop_pmc/tileshop_pmc_inline.html?title=Click%20on%20image%20to%20zoom&p=PMC3&id=8178104_gr4.jpg)

![Fig. 4](https://cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/blobs/2e50/8178104/ef63d1ff60f2/gr4.jpg)

Follow-up 60 days after orthognathic surgery (4a) and gingival plastic surgery in teeth 11, 12, 13, 22, and 23 (4b). Filling of the upper lip with hyaluronic acid (4c and 4d). Initial photo before (4e) and after (4f) tooth bleaching.

### Fig. 5.

[![Fig. 5](https://cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/blobs/2e50/8178104/f68f6832ebca/gr5.jpg)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/core/lw/2.0/html/tileshop_pmc/tileshop_pmc_inline.html?title=Click%20on%20image%20to%20zoom&p=PMC3&id=8178104_gr5.jpg)

![Fig. 5](https://cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/blobs/2e50/8178104/f68f6832ebca/gr5.jpg)

Final photos of the case.

This case was conducted by an orthodontist and by the Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery and Traumatology team of the dentist staff at São Vicente de Paulo Hospital. Throughout the process, the patient demonstrated good adherence and tolerability to treatment.

## 3. Clinical discussion

The expected benefits of orthognathic surgery range from optimizing physiological functions to improving the functions involved in social interactions [[6](#bb0030)]. In fact, esthetics represents one of the main motivations of the patient for surgery [[6](#bb0030)], and also minimally invasive cosmetic treatments have been increasingly after, with the aim of reshaping facial proportions and symmetry [[3](#bb0015)]. In this sense, the literature meets the objective of the present case report, which was to demonstrate the use of minimally invasive techniques associated with orthognathic surgery and orthodontics, a strong tendency in a current maxillofacial rehabilitation.

In fact, orthognathic surgery alone has already shown excellent results in terms of improving overall patient satisfaction. Aiming to assess oral health-related quality of life before and after orthognathic surgery, Rezaei et al. [[7](#bb0035)] examined 112 adult patients with class III skeletal malocclusion using the Short Form Oral Health Impact Profile (OHIP-14) and Orthognathic Quality of Life (OQLQ) questionnaires. Their results showed that orthognathic surgery improved the quality of life of these patients, as well as their satisfaction, self-confidence, and oral function. Such findings corroborate those of the present case report, considering the patient was extremely satisfied with the functional and esthetic findings obtained after the multidisciplinary treatment.

Orthognathic surgery often involves orthodontic treatment before and after surgical skeletal repositioning, and this three-stage sequence is the most popular method due to the greater likelihood of achieving occlusal stability after surgery [[8](#bb0040)]. However, an alternative method called “Surgery First” involving skeletal repositioning before the orthodontic treatment has been described more recently, showing potential advantages in reducing treatment time and improving facial esthetics at the beginning of the treatment [[9](#bb0045)].

Pelo et al. [[10](#bb0050)] conducted a study to evaluate the differences perceived by patients of the “traditional orthognathic approach” and “surgery first.” The post-surgical facial and masticatory improvement led to a better quality of life in both groups. However, the traditional approach group showed greater initial frustration related to the progressive worsening of the facial profile and masticatory function due to initial dental decompensation. The level of patient satisfaction may decrease before surgery due to the lack of knowledge of patients about the phases of orthodontic treatment. Thus, as occurred in the present case, it is up to the multidisciplinary team to raise patient awareness about the therapeutic phases to potentially increase the level of satisfaction with the treatmen [[7](#bb0035)].

Minimally invasive cosmetic improvements have been increasingly sought for reshaping facial proportions and increasing symmetry [[3](#bb0015)]. In the search for ideal esthetic results, it is essential that specialists have knowledge of facial anatomy, and treatment should be focused on the needs of the patient so that a specific esthetic approach for each case is properly selected [[11](#bb0055)]. The planning and execution of the treatment at the present case involved a stage of tooth-lip harmonization with the application of HA in order to improve the patient's esthetic results. Basically, this material is injected subcutaneously to add volume, change the conformation of the surface, thicken the skin or tissues or fill a rhytid. All of these points are a form of sculpture, which results in a significant change in facial appearance [[4](#bb0020)].

Wollina & Goldman [[12](#bb0060)] described the case of a 17-year-old patient subjected to orthognathic surgery 4 years earlier. Due to this procedure, the nasolabial angle was wide and the upper lip vermilion was thin and seemed flat. The patient received 0.6 mL of HA filling to volumize the upper and lower lips, obtaining an improvement in the quality of life and self-esteem. Thus, despite the various advantages offered by orthognathic surgery, unwanted esthetic changes may occur, which can be corrected by minimally invasive techniques.

As a multidisciplinary approach is often necessary to achieve esthetic harmony between face, teeth, lips and gums, interaction with various specialties of Dentistry must be used to solve the complexity of each patient's case [[13](#bb0065)]. Considering that a harmonious smile is influenced by several factors such as minimal gingival exposure, presence of healthy gingival tissue in interproximal spaces, symmetry between the upper gingival margin and upper lip, harmony between anterior and posterior segments, and correct proportions and anatomy [[14](#bb0070)], this case also involved a stage of gingival repair and tooth whitening, important steps in the search for an excellent result.

## 4. Conclusion

Currently, a closer look at Dentistry has been expanding and modifying rehabilitation standards, with the integration of several disciplines, new multidisciplinarity concepts, and more comprehensive views offering possibilities for additional procedures that may help to restore function, health, and esthetics of patients. The present case report reaffirms the benefits of orthognathic surgery associated with minimally invasive facial harmonization procedures used to refine the technique. The surgical procedure not only corrected the functional complaint of the patient but also played an important role in improving facial harmony, contributing significantly to self-esteem.

## Consent and ethics

Written informed consent was obtained from the patient for publication of this case report and accompanying images. A copy of the written consent is available for review by the Editor-in-Chief of this journal on request.

1. Phase 1: Orthodontic preparation (leveling, alignment, dental arch coordination)

## Bridging Dentistry and Facial Artistry for Natural Beauty

A beautiful smile does not exist in isolation. Teeth, lips, gums, and the underlying facial structure form an interconnected system where a change in one area inevitably influences the others. This fundamental insight drives the modern practice of dental aesthetic integration, a patient-centered approach that prioritizes balance, precision, and long-term well-being.

### The Science of Facial Harmony

Facial harmony is rooted in the balance and proportion of features such as the jawline, cheekbones, nose, chin alignment, and overall symmetry. The smile must complement these elements, not compete with them. For example, teeth whitening can brighten the complexion, while porcelain veneers may redefine lip support and alter the perceived shape of the lower face. Cosmetic dentists now use detailed facial analysis to ensure that any dental enhancement works with the patient‘s unique anatomy.

Studies using mathematical modeling of facial images have defined four main facial types—strong, dynamic, delicate, and calm—each requiring a tailored approach to tooth design. Notably, over 60% of individuals exhibit features from two or more facial types, underscoring the need for highly personalized treatment rather than a one-size-fits-all solution. Advanced algorithms can predict facial type with over 84% accuracy, giving clinicians a reliable tool for planning restorations that align with the patient‘s natural appearance.

### The Role of Technology in Integrated Planning

Digital technology has transformed how dentists and facial aestheticians collaborate. Digital Smile Design (DSD) uses high-resolution photography and specialized software to simulate dental outcomes before any clinical work begins. The process includes comprehensive facial analysis, virtual smile simulation, and creation of a 3D model preview of potential results. This not only improves communication between practitioner and patient but also increases predictability and confidence in the final outcome.

CEREC technology takes integration a step further by allowing dentists to design, manufacture, and place ceramic restorations in a single visit. These precision-fitted restorations blend seamlessly with natural teeth and enable comprehensive transformation plans tailored to the individual‘s needs.

### Choosing the Right Procedures

Porcelain veneers are thin custom-made shells that correct chips, cracks, and discoloration. Beyond repairing individual teeth, they reshape the smile line and can create a more youthful appearance by restoring volume in the mid-face and lifting the lips. The shape of the veneer must be guided by facial structure: a shorter, rounder face may benefit from slightly longer veneers, while a longer, narrow face often suits wider veneers to add fullness.

Professional teeth whitening removes stains caused by age, food, and beverages, brightening teeth by several shades. This simple procedure can make the face appear fresher and more vibrant, enhancing overall attractiveness.

Facial treatments such as Botox and dermal fillers refine the contours around the mouth, ensuring dental work complements rather than competes with the rest of the face. Botox relaxes overactive muscles that deepen laugh lines and marionette lines, creating a smoother complexion alongside dental enhancements. Dermal fillers restore volume lost to aging in the lips, cheeks, and nasolabial folds, plumping these areas to create a more youthful framework for the smile.

### Sequencing for Optimal Results

The order in which treatments are performed significantly affects the final outcome. A well-established sequence begins with orthodontic alignment (such as Invisalign) to correct bite function, midline shifts, and dental arch shape. Straightening teeth first sets a stable foundation, allows more conservative enamel removal for veneers, and improves smile symmetry.

After alignment, gumline adjustments may be needed to improve the tooth-to-gum ratio. Then, veneers or bonding are placed, followed by whitening to ensure color consistency across the arch. This step-by-step approach prevents issues like bulky veneers, uneven shade, or unnatural contours, culminating in a result that feels both comfortable and authentic.

### The Consultation and Personalization

Every integrated treatment begins with an in-depth evaluation considering oral health, facial structure, and aesthetic aspirations. Factors such as bite alignment, gum health, bone density, skin tone, and lifestyle habits are all assessed. Digital imaging allows patients to visualize potential outcomes before any procedures begin, ensuring they feel confident in their decisions.

Personalization is a defining element—there is no universal ideal smile. Cultural preferences, professional image, and personality influence smile design. Skilled cosmetic dentists tailor results to enhance without redefining, creating smiles that feel completely authentic to the individual.

### Longevity and Maintenance

Results vary by procedure: porcelain veneers and crowns can last 10-20 years with proper care; teeth whitening may need maintenance every 6 to 12 months; Botox typically lasts 3-4 months; dermal fillers last 6-12 months depending on the type and area treated. Preserving these outcomes requires regular touch-ups, good oral hygiene, routine dental check-ups, sun protection for the skin, and a healthy lifestyle.

### The Interdisciplinary Team

Achieving harmony between dentistry and facial artistry requires a team approach. Cosmetic dentists collaborate with periodontists, orthodontists, oral surgeons, and facial aesthetic practitioners such as dermatologists or plastic surgeons. Dentists‘ specialized knowledge of facial anatomy—including muscles, nerves, and bone—makes them particularly well-suited to perform precise injections like Botox, which smooth wrinkles while maintaining natural expressions and offering therapeutic benefits for TMJ disorders and jaw pain.

### Psychological and Functional Benefits

A harmonious smile boosts self-esteem and social interactions. Patients often report feeling more confident in personal and professional settings after comprehensive treatment. Functionally, proper bite alignment not only ensures comfort but also supports long-term oral health and facial balance.

### A Holistic Standard of Care

Dental aesthetic integration reflects a broader movement in healthcare toward holistic, patient-centered thinking. By bridging dentistry and facial artistry, practitioners deliver results that feel balanced, natural, and aligned with each patient’s unique presentation—enhancing not just teeth, but the entire face.

## The Interconnected Canvas of Your Smile

### How does the smile act as an interconnected system rather than an isolated feature of the face?

A beautiful smile does not exist in isolation; it is an integral part of a larger facial ecosystem. The teeth, lips, gums, and underlying facial structure are deeply interconnected, meaning adjustments in one area will naturally influence others. For instance, [how teeth whitening can brighten the complexion](https://vaccaroaesthetic.com/articles/18482/harmonizing-dental-aesthetics-with-facial-treatments/) can visually brighten the entire complexion, while how porcelain veneers may redefine the shape of the lips may redefine the shape of the lips and alter lip support. Facial treatments such as Botox and dermal fillers further refining contours around the mouth with Botox and dermal fillers refine the contours around the mouth, ensuring that dental work complements rather than competes with the rest of the face. This principle highlights the importance of a meticulous, holistic strategy where achieving harmony with technical skill and an artist’s eye requires technical skill combined with an artist’s eye for proportion and an intuitive grasp of individual anatomy. Factors such as skin tone, bone structure, and lifestyle habits all play a role in determining the most effective combination of procedures. A truly harmonious smile results when the teeth, lips, and facial structure are interconnected work together seamlessly, creating a refreshed and balanced appearance.

### What role does digital imaging and smile design analysis play in assessing the connection between teeth, lips, and facial structure?

Advanced technology like digital imaging and smile design analysis is essential for evaluating how a smile interacts with the face before any clinical work begins. [Digital Smile Design (DSD) workflow and clinical applications](https://www.smiledesignmanhattan.com/) uses high-resolution photography and specialized software to simulate dental outcomes, allowing both the patient and the clinician to visualize potential results in advance. This process includes [Comprehensive digital imaging for smile planning](https://veytsmandds.com/procedures/cosmetic-dentistry/smile-design-manhattan-ny/) from multiple angles, collaborative facial analysis that uses software to examine structural balance, and Virtual smile simulation preview that creates a 3D model preview of the proposed treatment. Digital imaging allows dentists to analyze facial features, measure proportions, and assess how the smile line aligns with the lower lip curve. It also helps evaluate important details such as the buccal corridor—the dark spaces at the corners of a smile—and the position of the midline relative to the face. By mapping proposed changes directly onto photographs, digital tools provide measurable precision, improve communication between patient and dentist, and increase predictability and confidence in the final results. This technology ensures that the smile design is tailored to the individual’s unique facial structure rather than following a generic template.

### Why are the lip line and facial form critical considerations in smile design?

The [lip line and smile aesthetics](https://dynamicsmiledesign.com/smile-aesthetics-facial-harmony-why-teeth-are-only-part-of-the-picture/)—how the upper lip rests at rest and moves when smiling— is a critical factor in smile aesthetics. A high lip line reveals more gum tissue, making the gum contour a prominent part of planning. If the gingival display is uneven or does not frame the teeth symmetrically, the asymmetry becomes very noticeable. Conversely, a low lip line partially hides the upper teeth at rest, shifting focus toward the incisal edge position and how the lower teeth interact with the smile line. The smile line itself is the curve formed by the upper incisal edges, and ideally it mirrors the curve of the lower lip. When these two curves align well, the smile looks natural and proportionate. Facial structure also guides the shape of the teeth themselves. A shorter, rounder face often benefits from slightly longer, squared veneers to elongate the face, while a longer, narrow face typically suits slightly shorter or wider veneers to create fullness. Heart-shaped faces often look best with soft, rounded veneers that follow the natural curve of the smile line. Square or strong jawlines pair well with more defined veneers that match the strength of the facial structure. These are not rigid rules but are grounded in how the eye perceives proportion and balance.

### How do changes in dental aesthetics impact the surrounding facial features?

Changes to the teeth have a direct effect on the lower third of the face. Porcelain veneers, for example, are thin custom-made shells that cover the front surface of teeth, capable of altering tooth dimensions and positioning. This can lead to broader changes in the lower third of the face, reshaping lip support and influencing the balance of facial features. Well-designed veneers can help restore volume in the mid-face, lift the lips, and soften deeper lines around the mouth, making smile design part of overall facial aesthetic. Similarly, missing teeth can cause bone loss that reduces cheek fullness; restoring lost teeth with dental implants can indirectly support midface structures. Orthodontic treatments such as clear aligners correct misalignment that disrupts facial harmony, affecting jawline prominence and facial profile balance. A complete smile makeover—combining orthodontics, whitening, veneers, and facial treatments—creates a cohesive result that photographs well and feels natural. As people age, teeth wear down, gums recede, and facial skin loses elasticity. Restorative work like crowns or porcelain veneers, when planned with facial structure in mind, can restore vertical dimension and improve soft-tissue support, potentially reversing some visible effects of aging on the lower face. This integrated approach ensures that dental enhancements do not just improve the smile but enhance the entire face, boosting self-confidence and contributing to a more positive self-image. The goal is refinement, not reinvention—creating a smile that looks natural, elegant, and tailored to the individual. For prospective clients seeking a balanced and rejuvenated appearance, understanding this interconnected canvas is the first step toward a truly harmonious outcome. Consulting with a cosmetic dentist skilled in digital smile design and facial analysis allows patients to explore how targeted dental procedures can complement their unique facial features and deliver lasting, natural-looking results. The consultation process typically includes a review of medical history, a dental exam and facial assessment, digital imaging to visualize potential outcomes, and the development of a customized treatment plan that outlines expected results, recovery time, and maintenance options. Whether considering teeth whitening, porcelain veneers, or a full smile makeover paired with facial rejuvenation, a comprehensive evaluation ensures that every detail works together to create a balanced, confident smile. For those curious about how their own facial structure influences smile design, scheduling a detailed consultation provides the opportunity to see a preview of the possibilities and take the first step toward achieving facial harmony through expert cosmetic dentistry. Regular follow-ups and good oral hygiene, along with lifestyle habits such as sun protection, help preserve these results over time, allowing patients to enjoy their enhanced smile and its positive impact on their overall appearance for years to come.

## Facial Harmony: A Real, Achievable Goal

### How Digital Facial Mapping Defines Your Unique Facial Type

Modern technology now provides objective, data-driven methods to identify a person's facial type with remarkable accuracy. A study involving [computer analysis of 91 facial images](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31994538/) used mathematical modeling to generate digital facial maps consisting of 27 landmark points and 12 basic lines, defining four main facial types: strong, dynamic, delicate, and calm. The resulting algorithm (C5.1 classification tree) achieved a general prediction accuracy of 84.3% for determining facial type by digital facial map. This research highlights that 61.5% of people have features of two facial types, and 38.5% have features of three facial types, underscoring the need for truly customized aesthetic treatment rather than a one-size-fits-all approach. Digital facial maps and 3D modeling allow patients and providers to visualize potential outcomes before any clinical work begins, enhancing communication and confidence in the treatment plan.

### Practical Guidelines: How Facial Harmony Guides Treatment Planning

Facial harmony guides dental treatment planning by providing clear reference points for natural-looking results. Key considerations include:

| Facial Feature | What Cosmetic Dentists Assess | How It Guides Treatment Planning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jawline and Face Shape | Round, long, heart-shaped, or square | Veneer shape and length are selected to balance the face; round faces may benefit from slightly longer veneers, while long faces often suit wider veneers to add fullness |
| Lip Line Position | High, low, or average; how much gum is visible | High lip lines require careful gum contouring; low lip lines shift focus to incisal edge position and lower tooth interaction |
| Smile Line Curve | Whether the upper incisal edges mirror the lower lip curve | Alignment aims for a curve that looks natural and proportionate, avoiding a flat or uneven appearance |
| Buccal Corridor | The dark spaces at the corners of a smile | Filling or preserving these spaces depends on individual facial proportions; a broader smile suits some faces while a slightly narrower one flatters others |
| Midline Alignment | Position relative to the nose, philtrum, and interpupillary line | A midline that is significantly off-center reads as asymmetric; treatment plans work with natural asymmetries rather than forcing perfect symmetry |
| Tooth Width-to-Length Ratio | Proportion of visible crown width to length | Ideal ratios vary per person; a tooth that is too wide flattens a smile, while one too long can appear cartoonish |
| Skin Tone and Lip Color | Underlying warmth or coolness of complexion | Veneer and whitening shades are selected to look natural against the patient's skin tone, avoiding overly bright or dull results |

### Why Balance and Proportion Over Feature Isolation

The goal of facial harmony is refinement, not reinvention. Real beauty is often found in balanced asymmetry, where slight variations in features combine to create an attractive, harmonious face. Skilled cosmetic dentists embrace small asymmetries—such as a naturally tilted smile midline—rather than forcing mathematical perfection, because overly symmetrical smiles can make the face look stiff or expressionless. For example, a shorter, rounder face may benefit from slightly longer veneers to create visual elongation, while a longer, narrower face may suit wider veneers to add volume and presence. Similarly, square or strong jawlines pair well with slightly more defined veneers that match the strength of the facial structure, while heart-shaped faces often look best with soft, rounded veneers that follow the natural curve of the smile line. These guidelines are not rigid rules but are grounded in how the eye perceives proportion and balance, ensuring that dental enhancements feel effortless and authentic.

### Avoiding Common Pitfalls in Smile Design

One-size-fits-all veneer designs often look unnatural—too flat, too white, or awkwardly positioned. When facial structure is ignored during planning, the results can feel out of place even if the dental work is technically flawless. Common pitfalls include:

* **Overly symmetrical smiles** that make the face look stiff or expressionless
* **Veneers designed too white** that clash with skin tone or look obviously cosmetic
* **Incorrect tooth length** that disrupts the lip line or creates a "gummy" or artificial appearance
* **Ignoring bite mechanics**, which can cause discomfort or uneven wear over time

A facially driven smile design approach avoids these issues by letting the entire face guide the shape, size, placement, and tone of each veneer. Dentists who approach cosmetic treatment planning with facial structure in mind typically assess the width of the face, the position of the midline, how the lips rest at neutral, and where the gum line sits. This level of detail ensures that results appear natural now and continue to look appropriate as the face ages.

## Why a Smile Makeover Is a Worthy Investment

### Is Smile Design Worth It?

A smile makeover is more than a cosmetic upgrade; it is a comprehensive approach that blends aesthetic refinement with functional improvement. By customizing treatments to your unique facial features, modern smile design delivers results that feel natural, balanced, and long-lasting. The investment pays off not only through a brighter, more youthful smile but also through better bite function, improved oral health, and a measurable boost in self-esteem.

A thoughtfully planned smile makeover addresses both form and function. For example, aligning teeth with clear aligners or porcelain veneers can correct bite discrepancies that cause [jaw pain](https://www.ddsgroupnyc.com/where-your-smile-meets-the-science-of-facial-harmony/) or uneven wear. Restoring proper occlusion stabilizes the jaw, enhances comfort, and protects dental work from premature failure. This functional dimension ensures that your smile remains comfortable and durable for years to come.

The aesthetic benefits are equally compelling. By considering your face shape, lip line, gum display, and skin tone, a cosmetic dentist can design a smile that complements your entire face. Digital imaging and 3D modeling allow you to preview outcomes before treatment begins, giving you confidence in the final result. Whether you choose whitening, veneers, orthodontics, or gum contouring, each procedure is tailored to your individual anatomy and goals.

### Customized Treatments for Lasting Results

A smile makeover is not a one-size-fits-all solution. The most effective plans combine multiple procedures in a logical sequence, starting with alignment and progressing to shaping, whitening, and finishing touches. This systematic approach ensures each step supports the next, preventing mismatched colors, bulky restorations, or unbalanced proportions.

**Teeth whitening** is often the first step. Professional whitening removes years of stains from coffee, tea, and age, creating a radiant base that makes your smile look fresh and vibrant. It can be done in-office or with take-home trays, and results typically last six months to a year with touch-ups.

**Porcelain veneers** are ultra-thin shells that correct chips, cracks, gaps, and discoloration. They also reshape the smile line and support lip fullness, contributing to a more youthful lower face. Veneers are custom-made using digital scans and are bonded permanently to the front of teeth. With proper care, they can last 10 to 20 years—making them a long-term investment in your appearance.

**Orthodontic treatment** with clear aligners (such as Invisalign) straightens teeth without visible braces. Aligners improve bite function, close gaps, and create a balanced foundation for veneers or bonding. By correcting midline shifts and arch symmetry, orthodontics enhances facial proportions and ensures that subsequent cosmetic work looks natural and stable.

**Gum contouring** may be recommended after alignment to even out an irregular gum line. Using a laser, the dentist reshapes excess gum tissue to create a symmetrical frame around the teeth. This step is especially important for patients with a high lip line or a “gummy” smile, as it prevents the teeth from appearing too short or uneven.

Each of these treatments is selected based on your facial structure, bite, and aesthetic goals. The result is a smile that looks like it was always meant to be there—not an artificial addition.

### Longevity and Psychological Impact

One of the most compelling reasons to invest in a smile makeover is the longevity of restorative work. High-quality porcelain veneers and crowns can last a decade or more with routine dental care, such as six-month checkups, good oral hygiene, and avoiding habits like nail-biting or chewing ice. Teeth whitening and gum contouring require periodic touch-ups, but the core structural changes remain stable.

The psychological benefits are equally significant. People who are happy with their smile tend to smile more often, which signals confidence and approachability in social and professional interactions. Research shows that individuals content with their dental appearance report higher self-esteem, greater career success, and stronger personal relationships. A smile makeover does not just change your teeth; it changes how you present yourself to the world.

Moreover, the process itself is designed to be comfortable and minimally invasive. Modern techniques, such as digital smile design and same-day CEREC restorations, reduce the number of visits and ensure precision. Patients often report feeling relaxed and well-informed throughout their journey, thanks to clear communication and virtual previews.

In summary, a smile makeover is a worthwhile investment because it delivers both tangible and intangible returns. You gain a functional bite, a harmonious smile that complements your face, and the confidence to express yourself fully. When performed by an experienced team that prioritizes facial harmony and long-term stability, the results can enhance your quality of life for many years.

## Enhancing Harmony with Complementary Facial Treatments

### How do Botox and dermal fillers refine the contours around the mouth and complement dental work?

A beautiful smile does not exist in isolation—it is framed by the lips, supported by the cheeks, and influenced by the dynamic movement of facial muscles. While dental procedures like porcelain veneers or teeth whitening directly enhance the teeth, injectable treatments such as Botox and dermal fillers refine the surrounding soft tissues, creating a seamless and natural-looking result.

Botox primarily targets dynamic wrinkles caused by repetitive muscle activity. Around the mouth, it relaxes the overactive muscles that deepen laugh lines and marionette lines. By softening these expressions, the complexion appears smoother and more relaxed, allowing dental work to take center stage without competition from deep furrows or tension lines around the lips.

Dermal fillers restore volume that naturally diminishes with age. When injected into the lips, nasolabial folds, or cheeks, they plump and support the surrounding structures. This restoration can complement dental enhancements by creating a fuller, more youthful smile line. For example, when porcelain veneers are designed to add subtle length and width to the teeth, adding volume to the lips with fillers ensures the two features balance each other, rather than the teeth appearing disproportionately prominent.

Dentists with specialized knowledge of facial anatomy are uniquely positioned to perform these injections. Their understanding of muscle, nerve, and bone relationships allows them to place injectables precisely, ensuring that facial expressions remain natural and unforced. The result is a harmonious integration where dental work and facial treatments work together, not against each other.

### What therapeutic benefits does Botox offer for TMJ disorders and teeth grinding?

Beyond its cosmetic applications, Botox provides significant therapeutic benefits for temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders and bruxism (teeth grinding). By injecting Botox into the masseter and temporalis muscles—the primary muscles responsible for chewing and clenching—the muscle activity is temporarily reduced.

This relaxation alleviates several symptoms:

* **Chronic jaw pain and tension**: Patients often experience relief from persistent aching in the jaw, temples, and face.
* **Teeth grinding (bruxism)**: By reducing the force of clenching, Botox helps prevent excessive wear on dental restorations and natural teeth, preserving the results of cosmetic work like veneers.
* **Headaches associated with TMJ**: Tension headaches originating from the jaw muscles frequently diminish after treatment.
* **Improved jaw function**: With reduced muscle spasticity, patients may find it easier to open and close the mouth comfortably.

Integrating Botox for TMJ management into a comprehensive dental aesthetic plan is particularly valuable. A patient receiving porcelain veneers or extensive restorative work benefits from a stable bite environment. If bruxism is unaddressed, the constant grinding force can chip or fracture restorations, shorten their lifespan, and cause discomfort. Botox offers a non-invasive, reversible way to protect both natural teeth and cosmetic enhancements while improving overall quality of life.

### How do injectables create a unified appearance when combined with dental procedures?

The goal of combining injectables with dental work is not simply to perform multiple treatments, but to create a cohesive facial aesthetic. A [patient-centered approach](https://www.450aesthetics.com/) examines how teeth, lips, gums, cheeks, and jawline interact at rest and during expression.

Digital imaging and 3D modeling allow clinicians to visualize how proposed changes will look before any procedure begins. For example, if a patient desires a broader, more symmetrical smile, the dentist may plan to lengthen or widen the visible teeth with porcelain veneers. However, if the lips are thin or asymmetrical, the veneers may appear overwhelming. By adding dermal filler to the upper lip, the lip volume increases, providing a proportional frame for the larger teeth. The result is a balanced, natural-looking smile that photographs well and feels authentic.

Similarly, Botox can be used to soften a gummy smile—a condition where excessive gum tissue is visible when smiling. By injecting a small amount of Botox into the muscles that elevate the upper lip, the lip drops slightly, reducing gum display. This simple adjustment can make a dramatic difference in smile harmony without any dental intervention.

| Treatment | Primary Role in Dental Aesthetics | Typical Duration | Complementary Benefit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Botox | Relaxes overactive muscles around the mouth, reduces gummy smile, softens laugh lines | 3–4 months | Protects dental restorations from grinding forces; ensures natural expressions |
| Dermal fillers | Restores volume to lips, cheeks, nasolabial folds | 6–12 months | Provides structural support for smile line; balances tooth proportions |
| Porcelain veneers | Corrects tooth shape, size, color, and alignment | 10–20 years | Creates the dental foundation for facial harmony |
| Teeth whitening | Brightens enamel shade | 6 months–1 year (touch-ups) | Enhances overall radiance; sets a clear baseline for restoration color |

### Why should patients consider sequencing these treatments with dental work?

Treatment sequencing is critical for achieving lasting, harmonious results. When Botox or fillers are performed before dental restorations, the facial soft tissues settle into their new position. This allows the dentist to design veneers or crowns that align precisely with the updated lip line and facial contours. Conversely, if dental work is completed first, subsequent injectable treatments must adapt to the existing tooth positions, which may limit the aesthetic options.

A typical sequencing plan for a combined smile makeover might follow this order:

1. **Initial consultation and digital planning**: Facial analysis, bite evaluation, and simulation of potential outcomes.
2. **Orthodontic alignment if needed**: Clear aligners or braces correct tooth position and bite discrepancies.
3. **Botox for TMJ or gummy smile**: If indicated, Botox is administered to relax muscles and stabilize the bite environment.
4. **Gum contouring**: Laser or surgical reshaping of the gumline to create symmetry.
5. **Porcelain veneers or crowns**: Custom restorations are bonded to the prepared teeth.
6. **Dermal fillers and final Botox touch-ups**: Fillers add volume to lips and cheeks, while Botox ensures the muscles around the mouth remain relaxed during healing.

This structured approach ensures that each step builds upon the previous one, reducing the need for adjustments later and maximizing the longevity and natural appearance of the results. The integrated strategy reflects a shift in modern aesthetic dentistry—from isolated interventions toward a cohesive, patient-centered vision that enhances both oral health and overall facial beauty. For patients in fast-paced urban settings, this efficiency is particularly appealing, as it minimizes chair time and accelerates the path to a confident smile. Moreover, by addressing functional issues like bruxism and TMJ pain alongside cosmetic goals, the holistic treatment plan supports long-term well-being, ensuring that the investment in aesthetics is protected by a foundation of oral health stability.

## An Integrated Approach for Lasting Confidence

### The Psychological Impact of a Harmonious Smile

A genuinely harmonious smile does more than improve appearance—it reshapes how people feel about themselves. Research consistently shows that individuals satisfied with their smile are more socially active, experience higher self-esteem, and report better mental well-being. This psychological lift extends into professional and personal spheres, where confidence in one's smile often translates into more assertive communication and a greater willingness to engage with others.

When dental work and facial treatments work together, the result feels natural rather than artificial. Patients no longer worry about drawing attention to their teeth or feeling that their smile looks "done." Instead, they report feeling more comfortable in social situations, smiling more freely, and experiencing a renewed sense of vitality. This is not simply cosmetic vanity—it reflects a genuine improvement in quality of life, supported by studies linking smile satisfaction to lower anxiety and higher overall happiness.

The psychological benefits are particularly pronounced when treatments are customized to the individual's unique facial structure and personality. A one-size-fits-all approach can leave patients feeling that their smile doesn't belong to them. By contrast, a carefully planned integration of dental and facial enhancements produces a smile that feels authentic, boosting self-image in a way that generic whitening or off-the-shelf veneers never could.

Clinicians increasingly recognize that the emotional outcome of aesthetic treatment is as important as the technical result. A smile that looks perfect but feels out of sync with the patient's face or expressions can cause discomfort rather than confidence. True success comes when the smile becomes a seamless extension of the person—something that enhances, rather than overrides, their natural features. This holistic understanding drives the modern approach to dental aesthetics.

### Comprehensive Treatment Planning Through Collaboration

Creating a smile that enhances facial harmony demands more than a single dentist's expertise. It requires a multidisciplinary team working in concert: cosmetic dentists, periodontists, orthodontists, oral surgeons, dermatologists, and plastic surgeons each contribute specialized knowledge. For example, Botox and dermal fillers can refine the contours around the mouth, but they must be timed and placed to complement restorations like porcelain veneers or crowns. Likewise, clear aligners may be needed to correct bite alignment before veneers are fabricated.

A comprehensive treatment plan begins with a thorough evaluation. The team reviews medical history, performs a full dental exam and facial assessment, and uses digital imaging to create a simulation of potential outcomes. This allows patients to see how changes to tooth shape, gum line, and lip support will affect their overall face. The goal is not to impose a standard ideal but to work with each individual's facial proportions, bone structure, and personal aesthetic goals.

Sequencing is critical. For instance, Invisalign is often performed first to straighten teeth and correct the bite. Gum contouring may follow to create an even gum line. Veneers or bonding are then designed with a precise understanding of the now-aligned teeth. Teeth whitening is usually done last to ensure consistent color across natural enamel and restorations. Each step builds on the previous one, leading to a stable, natural-looking result.

Facial treatments like Botox and fillers are integrated into this sequence. Botox can relax overactive muscles around the mouth, preventing deepening of laugh lines and ensuring that facial expressions remain smooth. Dermal fillers restore volume to lips, cheeks, and nasolabial folds, supporting the new smile line created by veneers. When dental and facial procedures are planned together, they produce a cohesive enhancement that neither could achieve alone.

Interdisciplinary collaboration extends to the design phase. A cosmetic dentist and a ceramist may work side by side, with the ceramist studying the patient's face in person to sculpt veneers that match natural tooth anatomy and harmonize with facial features. This level of coordination ensures that the final result looks effortless—as though the smile was always meant to be that way.

### The Future of Aesthetic Dentistry: AI and Digital Innovation

Artificial intelligence is poised to transform how dentists plan and execute smile makeovers. AI‑driven smile prediction software can analyze a patient's facial structure, skin tone, and existing dental proportions to recommend ideal tooth shapes, sizes, and shades. These tools learn from thousands of successful cases, offering evidence-based suggestions that reduce guesswork and improve consistency.

Digital smile design (DSD) is already widely used, but future systems will integrate real-time facial tracking. AI will be able to simulate how a smile will appear across a range of expressions—speaking, laughing, resting—not just a static photograph. This allows clinicians to anticipate how restorative work will interact with dynamic facial movements, ensuring that the smile remains harmonious in motion as well as at rest.

Biocompatible materials are also advancing. Newer ceramics and composite resins are designed to mimic the light-reflecting properties of natural enamel more closely, while being stronger and more durable. Combined with AI-assisted manufacturing, these materials will enable restorations that are virtually indistinguishable from natural teeth, even under close inspection.

Another emerging trend is the use of 3D facial scanning and augmented reality (AR). Patients will be able to preview proposed changes on their own faces in real time, using a smartphone or tablet. This interactive process not only builds trust but also helps patients articulate preferences more clearly, leading to treatments that are truly personalized.

These technologies do not replace clinical judgment—they augment it. The human eye and artistry remain essential for evaluating subtle aesthetic nuances. But AI and digital tools make the planning process more efficient, predictable, and transparent. For patients, this means less uncertainty, fewer surprises, and a clearer understanding of what their future smile will look like.

As the field evolves, the emphasis remains on creating smiles that enhance overall facial harmony and boost lasting confidence. The integration of psychological understanding, collaborative treatment planning, and cutting-edge technology ensures that each patient receives care that is as thoughtful as it is effective. The result is not just a beautiful smile, but one that supports a more confident, engaged life.

## Building a Foundation for Natural Beauty

### A Holistic View of Facial Beauty

A radiant smile does not exist in isolation. Teeth, lips, gums, and the underlying facial structure are deeply interconnected, meaning adjustments in one area can profoundly influence the others. For instance, teeth whitening can brighten the overall complexion, while porcelain veneers may subtly redefine the shape and support of the lips. This interconnectedness underscores a fundamental shift in aesthetic medicine: true beauty arises not from isolated interventions but from a comprehensive, patient-centered approach that prioritizes balance, proportion, and long-term well-being across the entire face.

### The Science of Facial Harmony

Facial harmony is rooted in the balance and proportion between features such as the jawline, cheekbones, lip shape, and chin alignment. A smile designed without considering these structural elements can feel out of place, even if the dental work is technically flawless. Cosmetic dentists now employ advanced smile design analysis, using digital imaging and 3D scans to study facial structure thoroughly. This process ensures that the size, shape, and spacing of teeth enhance, rather than compete with, the patient's unique facial proportions. The goal is to create a cohesive look where the smile appears as a natural, effortless extension of the individual's identity.

### Personalized, Minimally Invasive Care

Modern aesthetic dentistry emphasizes personalized, minimally invasive techniques that respect the patient's natural anatomy. Rather than applying a one-size-fits-all solution, skilled practitioners develop tailored treatment plans that consider factors like skin tone, lifestyle habits, and individual aesthetic aspirations. Procedures such as porcelain veneers and custom whitening are designed to be conservative, preserving healthy tooth structure while delivering dramatic results. This philosophy extends to integrating facial treatments like Botox and dermal fillers, which can refine contours around the mouth, soften laugh lines, and restore volume, ensuring that dental work complements rather than dominates the face.

### The Role of Digital Technology

Digital technologies have revolutionized the predictability and precision of combined aesthetic treatments. Digital Smile Design (DSD) and 3D modeling allow patients to visualize potential outcomes before any clinical work begins, improving communication between the patient and the care team. This digital roadmap enables clinicians to coordinate procedures seamlessly—from orthodontic alignment with clear aligners to the fabrication of ceramic veneers using CAD/CAM technology. The result is a treatment sequence that builds each step on the previous one, leading to stable, harmonious, and sustainable outcomes.

### Integrating Dental and Facial Treatments

Integrating dental aesthetics with facial rejuvenation treatments offers advantages over isolated interventions. Botox, for example, is not just for smoothing wrinkles; it can also relax overactive muscles around the mouth, preventing the deepening of marionette lines and ensuring facial expressions remain smooth and natural. Dermal fillers can restore volume to the lips, cheeks, and nasolabial folds, creating a more youthful complexion that complements dental enhancements. When porcelain veneers are combined with dermal filler augmentation, the result is a fuller, more youthful smile line that addresses both tooth appearance and perioral volume loss. This holistic strategy creates transformations that appear effortless and enduring.

### The Consultation and Planning Process

A comprehensive consultation is the cornerstone of integrated care. The process typically begins with an in-depth evaluation of oral health, facial structure, and aesthetic goals. Clinicians assess bite alignment, gum health, bone density, and the dynamics of the lip line. High-resolution photography and digital facial mapping are used to classify facial types and identify the most effective combination of procedures. This thorough assessment ensures that the treatment plan is not only aesthetically pleasing but also functionally sound, supporting long-term comfort and stability. The consultation also provides an opportunity to review longevity expectations: porcelain veneers and crowns can last 10–20 years with proper care, while Botox requires touch-ups every few months, and dermal fillers typically last 6–12 months.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Porcelain Veneers | Corrects chips, gaps, discoloration; reshapes smile line | 10–20 years | Provides foundational tooth shape and color |
| Teeth Whitening | Brightens teeth; refreshes complexion | 6 months – 1 year | Enhances overall radiance before restorative work |
| Botox | Reduces wrinkles; relaxes perioral muscles | 3–4 months | Smooths expressions; prevents line deepening |
| Dermal Fillers | Restores volume to lips, cheeks, nasolabial folds | 6–12 months | Complements dental work; rejuvenates lower face |

### Sustainable Results and Self-Confidence

The ultimate aim of combining dental aesthetics with facial treatments is to enhance both oral health and overall attractiveness, leading to increased self-confidence. Patients often report feeling more assured in social and professional settings after comprehensive treatment. Maintaining these results requires a partnership between the patient and the care team: regular dental check-ups, good oral hygiene, sun protection, and occasional touch-ups preserve the harmony achieved. By embracing a holistic, technology-driven approach, modern aesthetic practices deliver results that are balanced, natural, and beautifully aligned with each patient's unique presentation.

# Dental Aesthetic Integration: Enhancing Facial Harmony Through Smile Alignment

This article from drmmacdonald.com explores the integrated approach of dental aesthetics, emphasizing that a beautiful smile exists as part of a larger facial ecosystem. The core premise is that teeth, lips, gums, and facial structure form an interconnected system requiring holistic, personalized treatment planning.

## Key Scientific Foundations

- **Facial types**: Research using computer analysis of 91 facial images identified four main facial types—strong, dynamic, delicate, and calm—with a C5.1 classification tree algorithm achieving 84.3% accuracy in prediction. Notably, 61.5% of people have features of two facial types, and 38.5% have features of three, underscoring the need for highly customized treatment.

- **Digital technology**: Digital Smile Design (DSD) uses high-resolution photography and specialized software to simulate dental outcomes before clinical work begins. 3D modeling and facial mapping allow clinicians to analyze facial features, measure proportions, and assess how the smile line aligns with the lower lip curve.

## Treatment Options and Sequencing

The article details a comprehensive range of procedures with expected longevity:
- **Porcelain veneers** (10-20 years): Thin custom shells that correct chips, cracks, discoloration, and reshape the smile line
- **Teeth whitening** (6-12 months): Professional brightening that enhances overall complexion
- **Botox** (3-4 months): Relaxes overactive muscles; also treats TMJ disorders and bruxism
- **Dermal fillers** (6-12 months): Restore volume to lips, cheeks, and nasolabial folds
- **Invisalign** (varies): Corrects bite and alignment as foundation for cosmetic work
- **Gum contouring** (permanent): Reshapes gumline for even symmetry

**Recommended treatment sequence**: Orthodontic alignment → Botox for TMJ/gummy smile → Gum contouring → Porcelain veneers/crowns → Dermal fillers and final Botox touch-ups → Teeth whitening last for color consistency.

## Facial Harmony Principles

- **Lip line**: High lip lines require careful gum contouring; low lip lines shift focus to incisal edge position
- **Face shape guides tooth design**: Round faces benefit from longer veneers; long faces suit wider veneers; heart-shaped faces pair with soft, rounded veneers; square jawlines match more defined veneers
- **Buccal corridor** and **midline alignment** are critical assessment factors
- **Overly symmetrical smiles** can look stiff—skilled dentists embrace balanced asymmetry

## Psychological and Functional Benefits

A harmonious smile boosts self-esteem, social confidence, and professional success. Functionally, proper bite alignment ensures comfort and supports long-term oral health. The article emphasizes that the emotional outcome of aesthetic treatment is as important as the technical result.

## Future Directions

AI-driven smile prediction software, 3D facial scanning, augmented reality previews, and advanced biocompatible materials are transforming the field, making planning more efficient, predictable, and transparent.

# The Benefits of Combining Botox with Orthodontic Treatment

When most people think about Botox, they imagine wrinkle reduction, crow’s feet fading, or smooth foreheads. But in recent years, Botox has gained surprising ground in dental and orthodontic practices—where its benefits go far beyond aesthetics. For patients undergoing orthodontic treatment, Botox can actually improve outcomes, reduce discomfort, and support long-term results.

At Dental & Facial Aesthetics of South Florida, we specialize in harmonizing smile alignment with facial balance. In this blog, we explore how Botox can work hand-in-hand with orthodontics to enhance both function and facial aesthetics—and why this combination may be the key to your most confident smile yet.

## **Why Botox Belongs in an Orthodontic Office**

Botox (botulinum toxin type A) works by temporarily relaxing targeted muscles. While its cosmetic benefits are well known, its therapeutic uses in dentistry and orthodontics are just as powerful.

In orthodontics, muscle tension around the jaw, lips, or cheeks can interfere with tooth movement, jaw alignment, and overall bite function. Injecting small doses of Botox into overactive muscles can help reduce strain, correct habits like clenching or lip-pulling, and support the success of your braces or aligners.

## **Functional Benefits of Botox During Orthodontic Treatment**

### **1. Reduces Jaw Clenching and TMJ Pain**

One of the most common issues during or after orthodontic treatment is temporomandibular joint (TMJ) discomfort. As your bite adjusts, the muscles around your jaw may respond with tension, inflammation, or even painful spasms.

Botox can relax the overactive masseter and temporalis muscles—helping to reduce clenching, nighttime grinding (bruxism), and the headaches or jaw pain that often follow. This not only improves comfort but allows your orthodontic appliance to work more efficiently.

### **2. Controls Hyperactive Lip Muscles**

Some patients have strong or imbalanced lip muscles that interfere with tooth positioning. For example, a hyperactive upper lip may pull up excessively when smiling, revealing too much gum—a condition known as a “gummy smile.”

Botox injections can gently relax the elevator muscles of the upper lip, softening the smile arc and allowing orthodontic adjustments to settle more naturally. In some cases, Botox may be a less invasive alternative to gum surgery.

### **3. Supports Retention and Relapse Prevention**

After braces or aligners are removed, there’s always a risk that teeth may begin shifting back—especially if muscle memory and tension remain unchanged. Strategic Botox applications during the retention phase can help “retrain” the facial and jaw muscles, making relapse less likely.

This is especially useful for adult orthodontic patients or those with prior treatment failure due to muscular interference.

## **Aesthetic Synergy: Why Botox + Braces Means a Better Smile**

Orthodontic treatment isn’t just about moving teeth—it’s about designing a smile that complements your face. While aligners and braces reshape your bite, Botox can fine-tune your overall expression. The result? A smoother, more harmonious transformation.

At DFAesthetics, we often use Botox in coordination with orthodontic plans to:

* Reduce frown lines or crow’s feet that may feel exaggerated during treatment
* Soften forehead tension from jaw-related headaches
* Balance facial asymmetry caused by one-sided clenching or muscle overuse

Because we take a holistic approach, our team considers both the functional mechanics and the artistic outcome—ensuring your new smile looks as good as it feels.

## **Who’s a Good Candidate for Botox During Orthodontics?**

Botox may be appropriate for orthodontic patients who:

* Experience jaw tension, clenching, or bruxism
* Suffer from TMJ-related pain or limited jaw mobility
* Have a hyperactive upper lip or gummy smile
* Are undergoing re-treatment due to relapse
* Want facial symmetry and relaxation during smile correction

Your provider will perform a full facial and oral evaluation before recommending Botox. The dosage and injection sites are customized to your anatomy and treatment goals.

## **What to Expect from the Procedure**

Botox injections are minimally invasive and take just minutes to administer. Most patients feel only a slight pinch. Results typically begin within 3–5 days and last 3–4 months, though some therapeutic effects—like jaw tension relief—can be felt sooner.

In the context of orthodontics, Botox may be administered at key milestones:

* Before starting treatment to reduce jaw strain
* During active alignment for muscle control
* Post-treatment to assist in retention and stability

There’s no downtime, and you can return to your normal routine immediately. Patients are advised to avoid rubbing the area and to stay upright for a few hours after the injection.

## **Safety and Side Effects**

Botox has a long track record of safe use when performed by trained professionals. At DFAesthetics, our providers are certified in both dental and aesthetic medicine—so you can trust your treatment is precise, conservative, and tailored to your needs.

Side effects are rare but may include:

* Mild bruising or swelling at the injection site
* Temporary muscle weakness in the treated area
* Slight headache or tightness (usually brief)

Proper placement and dosage help minimize these risks, which is why experience matters when choosing your provider.

## **Why Choose DFAesthetics for Botox + Orthodontic Treatment?**

We’re not just a dental office—we’re a full-service facial aesthetics practice. That means we don’t treat smiles in isolation. We look at the entire face, head, and neck as an integrated system, combining cosmetic insight with clinical precision.

Our team includes board-certified professionals who specialize in:

* Orthodontics and aligner therapy
* TMJ and bite disorders
* Facial muscle dynamics
* Botox and dermal fillers

Whether you’re undergoing clear aligners, braces, or orthodontic relapse correction, our Botox-enhanced protocols are designed to maximize your comfort and your results.

## **Conclusion: A New Era in Smile Design**

Orthodontics isn’t just about straight teeth anymore. It’s about total facial harmony—and Botox is an essential tool in that vision.

By reducing tension, supporting muscle rebalancing, and enhancing aesthetics, Botox can elevate your orthodontic journey from routine correction to transformative change.

At Dental & Facial Aesthetics of South Florida, we believe in creating smiles that work—and wow. If you’re curious about how Botox can support your treatment, we invite you to schedule a personalized consultation.

**Don’t settle for just straight teeth. Choose a confident, comfortable, and complete smile transformation. Call us today or book your appointment online to explore the power of combining Botox with orthodontics.**

This webpage from Dental & Facial Aesthetics of South Florida (DFAesthetics) discusses the benefits of combining Botox with orthodontic treatment. The article explains that Botox (botulinum toxin type A) is increasingly used in dental and orthodontic practices for therapeutic purposes beyond cosmetic wrinkle reduction.

**Functional Benefits of Botox During Orthodontic Treatment:**
1. Reduces jaw clenching and TMJ pain by relaxing overactive masseter and temporalis muscles
2. Controls hyperactive lip muscles, including treating "gummy smile" by relaxing upper lip elevator muscles
3. Supports retention and relapse prevention by retraining facial and jaw muscles after braces/aligners are removed

**Aesthetic Synergy:** Botox can fine-tune facial expression alongside orthodontic work, reducing frown lines, softening forehead tension, and balancing facial asymmetry.

**Good Candidates:** Patients with jaw tension/clenching/bruxism, TMJ-related pain, hyperactive upper lip/gummy smile, relapse issues, or those wanting facial symmetry during smile correction.

**Procedure Details:** Minimally invasive injections taking minutes, results begin within 3-5 days, last 3-4 months, no downtime. Botox may be administered before treatment, during active alignment, or post-treatment for retention.

**Safety:** Performed by certified professionals with rare side effects including mild bruising, temporary muscle weakness, or slight headache.

The practice is located at 9 Plaza Real, Suite 101 & 102, Boca Raton, FL 33432 and 3325 N University Dr, Coral Springs, FL 33065, with hours Monday to Thursday 10am-6pm and Friday 10am-3pm.

# How Surgical Orthodontics Can Enhance Facial Aesthetics

October 30, 2023

Orthodontist

In today’s society, appearance plays a significant role in how we perceive ourselves and are perceived by others. We all strive for that perfect smile and a face that radiates confidence and beauty. That’s where surgical orthodontics comes into play. By combining the power of orthodontic treatment with specialized surgery, individuals can achieve not only straight teeth but also an improved facial profile. Get ready to delve into this fascinating topic as we explore the role of facial aesthetics in modern society and uncover the incredible benefits of surgical orthodontics. Let’s begin!

## The Role of Facial Aesthetics in Modern Society

Our society has become increasingly obsessed with appearance, and facial aesthetics play a significant role in shaping our perception of beauty. From flawless skin to symmetrical features, there is immense pressure to conform to societal standards.

Facial aesthetics not only impact personal confidence but also influence how others perceive us. Whether it’s for professional success or personal relationships, a well-proportioned face is often considered attractive and desirable.

In today’s world, where social media dominates our lives, the emphasis on facial aesthetics has heightened even further. Filters and editing tools have made it easier than ever to alter one’s appearance digitally, leading many individuals to aspire towards unrealistic ideals.

However, [surgical orthodontics offers a tangible solution](https://www.toombsorthodontics.com/treatment/surgical-orthodontics/) for those seeking an improved facial aesthetic. By combining orthodontic treatment with surgery when necessary, patients can achieve balanced proportions and enhanced harmony between their teeth and facial structures.

Moreover, surgical orthodontics goes beyond just cosmetic benefits. It can correct functional issues such as misaligned bites or breathing difficulties caused by jaw discrepancies. This comprehensive approach ensures that both the form and function of the face are improved simultaneously.

As we continue to navigate through modern society’s obsession with appearances, it is essential to remember that true beauty comes in all forms. Surgical orthodontics offers individuals an opportunity to enhance their natural features while maintaining individuality – ultimately boosting self-esteem and overall quality of life.

So why succumb to societal pressures when you can choose surgical orthodontics as a means of achieving your desired facial aesthetic? With advancements in technology and highly skilled professionals available today, embracing your unique beauty has never been more accessible!

## The Benefits of Combining Orthodontics and Surgery

Combining orthodontics and surgery can offer a range of benefits when it comes to enhancing facial aesthetics. This approach is often used in cases where there are significant skeletal discrepancies or severe malocclusions that cannot be corrected with orthodontic treatment alone.

One major benefit of surgical orthodontics is the ability to achieve not only straighter teeth but also a more balanced and harmonious facial profile. By addressing underlying jaw misalignments, such as an overbite or underbite, surgical orthodontics can help improve the overall appearance of the face.

Another advantage is that surgical orthodontics can correct functional issues related to bite problems. This can lead to improved chewing and speech abilities, as well as alleviate any discomfort or pain caused by jaw misalignments.

Additionally, combining surgery with orthodontic treatment allows for more precise control over tooth movement. Surgical intervention can help reposition the jaws and create a solid foundation for optimal dental alignment. This means that once the braces are removed, patients are left with not only straight teeth but also a properly aligned bite that will promote long-term oral health.

It’s important to note that while surgical orthodontics may require longer treatment times compared to traditional braces alone, the results achieved through this combined approach are often more comprehensive and durable.

Combining orthodontics with surgery offers numerous advantages in terms of both aesthetic enhancement and functional improvement. It provides an opportunity for individuals with complex dental issues to achieve a harmonious facial balance while also addressing underlying structural concerns. By working together, surgeons and orthodontists can create beautiful smiles that positively impact not only how individuals look but also how they feel about themselves.

## The Bottom Line

In today’s modern society, facial aesthetics play a significant role in how we perceive ourselves and how others perceive us. With the advancements in orthodontic and surgical techniques, it is now possible to enhance not only the functionality of our teeth but also improve our overall facial appearance.

Surgical orthodontics offers a unique solution for individuals with complex dental issues that cannot be corrected through traditional orthodontic treatments alone. By combining orthodontics with surgery, patients can achieve remarkable results that go beyond just straightening their teeth.

The benefits of surgical orthodontics are numerous. Not only does it address functional problems such as misaligned jaws or severe bite discrepancies, but it also improves facial harmony by repositioning the jawbones and achieving proper alignment. This leads to an enhanced overall aesthetic appeal, boosting self-confidence and transforming smiles.
