* [Orthodontic Dentistry](https://ohmdentalpiscataway.com/category/orthodontic-dentistry/)

Cosmetic treatments such as lip filler and Botox are extremely popular. But once someone has updated their face, many people also want their smile to match their new look. That is why [Invisalign](https://ohmdentalpiscataway.com/) has become the number one cosmetic upgrade following facial treatments. Here at OHM Dental Piscataway, we will comfortably and safely help our patients improve their smiles.  
If you need help, call us anytime at (908) 205-8585.

**Why People Choose Invisalign After Cosmetic Treatments**

After getting fillers or Botox, patients want their smile to be in balance. Additionally, Invisalign helps straighten the teeth without using any metal wires or brackets. It fits perfectly with facial aesthetics.

**How Invisalign Complements Facial Enhancements**

There are many reasons people choose **clear aligners**:

* They enhance the results of lip fillers by improving tooth alignment.
* Moreover, they make the smiles in photos look smoother.
* They enhance confidence in conducting daily activities.
* Furthermore, they help the face look more balanced and youthful.
* In addition, they support long-term dental health.

**How Invisalign Works: Quietly and Naturally**

Major reasons adults choose **Invisalign** are that the trays are almost invisible. Therefore, you can smile freely and never feel self-conscious. This makes [teeth straightening](https://ohmdentalpiscataway.com/) a perfect match with treatments like lip filler and Botox.

**Why Invisalign Is Better Than Braces for Cosmetic-Minded Patients**

Here are a few reasons:

* No visible metal that affects your photos.
* Easy to remove for eating or makeup touch-ups.
* More comfortable, especially after lip filler.
* Additionally, it’s faster for mild and moderate spacing issues.
* Matches other **cosmetic dentistry** goals well.

**What About Dental Implants?**

Some patients may also consider **dental implants** if they have missing teeth. Straightening teeth with **clear aligners** can create better spacing, making future **dental implant** placement easier and more accurate.

**Invisalign Helps Complete Your Smile Makeover**

It is not just about white teeth; it is about balance, symmetry, and confidence. As a result, **Invisalign** gives you a natural and beautiful smile that fits your facial features, helping complete your **smile makeover**.

**Why Choose OHM Dental Piscataway?**

At OHM Dental Piscataway, we offer:

* Gentle and modern **cosmetic dentistry**
* Personalized **clear aligner** treatment plans
* Digital scans for accuracy
* Comfortable and safe procedures
* Expert care for long-lasting results.

Additionally, our team helps you choose the best option for your smile and confidence.

**Schedule Your Appointment**

If you want to complete your **smile makeover** or learn if **Invisalign** is right for you, we’re here to help.  
Call us today at (908) 205-8585 to schedule your appointment. We truly look forward to giving you a confident and beautiful smile.

## [](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070)Abstract

### Background

To evaluate the facial aesthetic effects of orthodontic treatment performed with clear aligners and to compare it to an untreated control group, on lower third facial ageing in adult patients through the use of the Wrinkle Severity Rating Scale (WSRS) at the beginning (T0) and at the end (T1) of the study period.

### Material and Methods

A clear aligners treated group (TG) of 68 patients was compared to a control group of 33 untreated patients (UG). Each group was divided in 2 subgroups according to age: subgroup 1 if under 40 years of age and subgroup 2 if over. Facial aesthetics of the lower third was evaluated at T0 and T1 by a panel of five aesthetic experts with WSRS.

### Results

Statistically significant changes were found in all subgroups comparing WSRS scores at T0 and T1. The between group comparisons revealed that wearing clear aligners produces a statistically relevant improvement in lower third facial aesthetics both in younger (_p_< 0.05) and older (_p_< 0.001) patients.

### Conclusions

The present retrospective cohort study has successfully shown that malocclusion therapy conducted through the use of clear aligners in a population of adults affected by dental crowding has beneficial effects on lower third facial ageing.

**Key words:**Orthodontics, clear aligners, facial aesthetics, facial wrinkles, compliance.

## [](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070)Introduction

Ageing is an inevitable life process: from birth human genes lead the body through a series of changes ranging from growth and development to maturation, ageing and finally death. Facial ageing is a complex physiological process, involving hard and soft tissues, essentially characterized by loss of soft tissue muscle tone and of hard tissue volume.

In the dentate patient the facial ageing is believed to be totally due to soft tissue changes. Ageing of the skin is associated with progressive atrophy of the dermis as well as changes in the dermal tissues. This leads to thinning, wrinkling, sagging and laxity of the facial skin. Moreover the muscles of the head and neck show a significant reduction in cross-sectional area and density with age ([1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#B1)).

The increased interest in aesthetics procedures has required the development of scales to measure the degree of ageing, the severity of facial wrinkles and the level of improvement resulting from such procedures. Numerous different instruments have been proposed with the aim of creating a standardized tool for the measurement of ageing such as questionnaires or the 3-Dimensional photogrammetry ([2](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#B2)). Validated scales could be also useful for assessing patient-reported outcomes, such as quality of life and satisfaction with treatment. One of the above mentioned scales is a photograph-based five-point scale, named Wrinkle Severity Rating Scale (WSRS), that is designed for quantifying facial folds from 1 = absent to 5 = extreme ([3](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#B3)).

Orthodontics and orthognathic surgery, with only a moderately increased risk rate of complications ([4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#B4)) and a more positive effect on patient’s compliance ([5](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#B5)), can help give facial harmony, where malocclusions created a situation of abnormalities in bone bases, teeth position, muscle function and posture of lips and tongue. The consequence of a correct orthodontic treatment is the finding of a face harmony, highlighted with the face aesthetic analysis ([6](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#B6)).

Clear aligners consist in a series of transparent aligners that are able to perform orthodontic movements without compromising the aesthetic of the smile. A recent systematic review demonstrated that clear aligner treatment is effective in aligning and levelling the arches in non-growing subjects ([7](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#B7)).

The aim of this retrospective cohort study was to evaluate the effects of orthodontic treatment performed with clear aligners on lower third facial ageing in adult patients through the use of WSRS by a panel of five aesthetic experts.

## [](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070)Material and Methods

-Subjects

The examined sample consisted of subjects enrolled in a retrospective observational study at the dental clinic of “A. Gemelli” Foundation – Teaching Hospital in Rome. The study project was approved by the Ethical Committee at the Catholic University of Sacred Heart in Rome. The following inclusion criteria had to be fulfilled by the subjects enrolled in the study:

• Skeletal class I (ANB: 2°+/- 2°);

• Overjet between 0 and 4 mm;

• Overbite between 0 and 4 mm;

• Molar and canine class I;

• Moderate upper and lower crowding (with dento-basal discrepancy from 4.1 to 7.0 mm);

• Presence of all permanent teeth except for third molars.

The following exclusion criteria were established:

• Previous orthodontic treatment;

• Surgical interventions or aesthetic treatments in head and neck district;

• Loss or gain more than 2 kg during the study period.

A sample of 101 patients with moderate crowding was enrolled for the study, and informed consent was obtained. The following records were collected in the study sample at the initial observation (T0) and after an average period of 12 months (T1): intraoral and extraoral photographs, orthodontic casts, latero-lateral teleradiography and orthopanoramic radiography.

All subjects, homogeneous for dental and skeletal relationship, were assigned to one of the following two groups:

• Treatment of dental crowding with a set of clear aligners (TG);

• Patients that, for certain personal motivations, decided to defer orthodontic treatment (UG).

Each group was further divided according to age into subgroups: subgroup 1 if under 40 years of age and subgroup 2 if over.

Participants enrolled in this study showed the following distribution:

• TG1: 39 subjects, mean age of 33.31 years at T0, 20 female and 19 male;

• TG2: 29 subjects, mean age of 45.52 years at T0, 15 female and 14 male;

• UG1: 20 subjects, mean age of 31.42 years at T0, 10 female and 10 male;

• UG2: 13 subjects, mean age of 46.54 years at T0, 7 female and 6 male.

Demographics of the above mentioned group and statistical comparisons regarding age at T0 and study period are shown in [Table 1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#T1) and [Table 2](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#T2).

Table 1Demographics of the groups TG1 and UG1, study period duration and statistical comparisons.

Table 2Demographics of the groups TG2 and UG2, study period duration and statistical comparisons.

-Treatment protocol

In the TG a set of clear aligners (Invisalign®, Align Technology, San José, CA, USA) was used as the sole appliance. Each aligner has a thickness of about 0.75 mm. Patients were instructed to wear the aligners for 22 hours/day, to remove them only for meals and dental cleaning and to regularly change them every 14 days. Patients belonging to the UG did not receive any form of orthodontic treatment during the study period.

Extraoral frontal projections photographs at T0 and T1 were taken in the same room with steady light conditions with the same camera parameters (distance, focus and flash). Photographs were taken on a wide screen with cutaneous Frankfurt plane parallel to the floor; male patients were kindly asked to have their face shaved and female patients to have their make-up removed before taking pictures. All patients belonging to the treated groups had their clear aligner removed before taking the photographs.

-Facial ageing assessment

The evaluation of facial folds of the lower third was done through the WSRS.

A panel of five aesthetic experts (a plastic surgeon, a dermatologist, an aesthetic physician and two orthodontists) previously calibrated (Cohen’s Kappa = 0.893) were asked to express a judgement regarding the lower third facial ageing of patients from 1 = absent to 5 = extreme. Pictures from T0 and T1 were randomly allocated through the use of a computer generated code and shown to the aesthetic experts in a portable document format (pdf) file.

The evaluations and statistical analysis were carried out double blind since each photograph was matched with a code, known by an author not involved in the clinical and statistical evaluations.

-Statistical methods

Due to the lack of scientific reports regarding the evaluation of the impact of orthodontic therapy on facial ageing, the sample size calculation of each group was conducted by performing a power analysis based on the results of a previous pilot study, to detect at least a 1 grade difference between groups, with a standard deviation of 0.9 grade, an alpha value of 0.05 and a power of 0.8 and was calculated to be 13 subjects.

To determine the reliability of the method, WSRS measurements on half of the subjects were performed by one trained examiner and repeated after an interval of approximately two weeks. A paired t-test was used to compare the two measurements (systematic error). The magnitude of the random error was calculated by using the method of moment’s estimator (MME). Exploratory statistics revealed that all variables were normally distributed (Kolmogorov-Smirnov test) with equality of variances (Levene’s test). Lower third facial wrinkle changes during study period (T1-T0) were evaluated and paired t-tests were used to assess statistical significance within each group. A comparison of changes between the two groups was also carried out using unpaired t-tests. All comparisons were considered significant at _p_< 0.05. All statistical analyses were performed using the Statistical Package for Social Sciences version 15.0 (SPSS Inc., Chicago, Illinois, USA).

## [](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070)Results

The present investigation reached an adequate power (> 0.85) because of the number of subjects enrolled in the examined groups.

The study period lasted 1.23 years (SD: 0.43 years). No systematic error was found between the WSRS repeated measurements. For the lower third facial wrinkle changes the random error was 0.01 marks. No significant between-group differences were found for age of the participants at T0 and for the study period duration ([Table 1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#T1),[Table 2](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#T2)).

Skeletal, molar and canine class, overjet and overbite did not register any significant change during the study period.

Regarding subgroups 1 the overall aesthetics of the lower third of the face showed a statistically significant change of -0.21 (_p_< 0.05) in the TG and of 0.27 (_p_< 0.05) in the UG. Consequently the difference between TG1 and UG1 was -0.29 (_p_< 0.05).

Regarding subgroups 2 the overall aesthetics of the lower third of the face showed a statistically significant change of -0.28 (_p_< 0.01) in the TG and of 0.30 (_p_< 0.05) for the UG. Thus the difference between TG2 and UG2 was -0.65 (_p_< 0.001) ([Table 3](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#T3),[Table 4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#T4)).

Table 3Descriptive statistics and statistical comparisons of the WSRS marks at T0 and T1 in subgroups TG1 and UG1.

Table 4Descriptive statistics and statistical comparisons of the WSRS marks at T0 and T1 in subgroups TG2 and UG2.

## [](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070)Discussion

This retrospective cohort-study, whose aim was to evaluate the effects of orthodontic treatment on lower third facial ageing in adult patients, has successfully shown that wearing clear aligners during orthodontic treatment has beneficial effects on face soft tissues when compared to the aesthetic impact of patients of an untreated group.

The results found in the present study show the presence of an additional effect on the lower third facial aesthetics in patients undergoing orthodontic therapy with clear aligners. To the best of our knowledge no other report had previously highlighted this particular effect of orthodontic therapy; for this reason any comparison with the previous scientific literature is fairly inaccurate to do.

A possible explanation of this finding is that the mechanism of dental aligners could be compared to the effects of splints that interact with the vertical intraoral dimension. In fact wearing two aligners (one for each arch), with a thickness of about 0.75 mm each, could lead to an increasing of the intraoral vertical dimension, though it is limited to the time of the aligners application. Constantly wearing the aligners, a slight modification of the vertical dimension could have beneficial effect also in the intra-articular compression, even with a repositioning of the joint ([8](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#B8)). Positive effects are also reported in patients affected by obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome whose diagnosis is even more complex in the event of a decrease of the vertical dimension ([9](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#B9)).

Such beneficial effects are also reported by Okeson that demostrated that occlusal splints can improve occlusal conditions, reducing muscular activity ([10](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#B10)).

The result of this splint effect, due to the wearing of the aligners for 22/24 hours a day for at least one year, has been evaluated on the lower third face soft tissues and considered as an anti-aging effect. Such consideration is shown by the statistical analysis resulting from the evaluations of 5 facial aesthetics experts.

The second possible mechanism of action of anti-aging effect of clear aligners could be linked to the fact that wearing the aligners involves a number of changes in the cellular and molecular metabolism of bone and muscle structures. In particular, authors reported an improvement related to the whole range of facial features, not just the lower face, using appliances (acrylic pivots), for six months. The mechanisms by which patients’ signs of facial aging are reversed are based on the fact that both muscles and bone respond to mechanical signals. Stretch of the muscle fibres leads to an increase in the bone density due to the activity of the osteocytes and induces release of mechano-growth-factor (MGF) and insulin growth factor 1 (IGF-1) ([11](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#B11)).

These two mechanisms of action, mentioned as possible explanations of this anti-aging effect during orthodontic therapy conducted with Invisalign® on adults, could be considered as phenomena that can take place in combination rather than individually.

A statistically significant improvement in facial aesthetics was found in both subgroups of patients but such finding is much more significant in older patients (subgroup 2) (_p_<0.001).

This finding can be explained by suggesting that at older ages, aging mechanisms become more apparent and any aesthetic improvement, although of a minimal clinical significance, can be better noticed as compared to those that may occur at a younger age in which to show the same aesthetic improvement it is required to make a substantial change in the facial soft tissues architecture.

The findings of this study, however, should be interpreted with caution because it has some limitations. Firstly: although the results were statistically significant the size of the sample is quite small. Another limitation is that the judgements given by the experts were expressed looking at photographs: this could unavoidably lead to a partial perception of the whole patient’s facial expressions. In fact it is important to consider that in most cases the facial beauty and self perception is linked to a global face evaluation rather than the appraisal of the depth of wrinkles of a specific part of it. This statement finds support in the fact that in pictures taken at T1 phase patients very often showed a change of their hairstyle or make-up, even in cases where experts’ judgments had revealed a decrease in facial aesthetics, so that patients were asked to remove their make-up before taking all the photographs not to influence the aesthetic evaluations. Probably the biggest limitation of this study is the lack of a control group treated with traditional orthodontic therapy. Such a lack is justified by the fact that the second photograph records (T1) were taken at an average period of 12 months after the beginning of therapy with clear aligners. This moment does not always correspond to the end of therapy. Therefore photographing subjects wearing brackets would have inevitably caused a methodological bias as the circum-oral soft tissues around brackets could simulate a lifting effect on the wrinkles of the lower third of the face and thus invalidate the judgment of evaluators.

The anti-aging additional effect demonstrated, even if modest when compared with the results of aesthetic medicine procedures, could be partially considered by the clinicians, who nowadays are forced to face with ever increasing aesthetic demands without surgical and invasive procedures or procedures that provide the use of anesthesia and needles that have always been subjectively considered painful and looked with suspicious eyes in all medical fields ([12](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070#B12)).

## [](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070)Conclusions

The properties and functional capacity of dental aligners may influence patients’ and aesthetics experts’ perception of facial beauty causing an additional anti-aging process.

In addition, the effect of wearing clear aligners can be interpreted as a complex and multiple phenomenon involving blood vessels, cells, growth factors, derma and muscle.

Such phenomenon has lead to a positive aesthetic impact of the face even if its results should be considered partial and interpreted with caution because of the need of further research.

args.key_excerpts: Clear aligner treatment is effective in aligning and levelling the arches in non-growing subjects; Wearing clear aligners during orthodontic treatment has beneficial effects on face soft tissues when compared to the aesthetic impact of patients of an untreated group; The anti-aging additional effect demonstrated, even if modest when compared with the results of aesthetic medicine procedures, could be partially considered by the clinicians; The effect of wearing clear aligners can be interpreted as a complex and multiple phenomenon involving blood vessels, cells, growth factors, derma and muscle; The properties and functional capacity of dental aligners may influence patients' and aesthetics experts' perception of facial beauty causing an additional anti-aging process
args.summary:
This retrospective cohort study published in the Journal of Clinical and Experimental Dentistry (2018) by Romeo Patini et al. evaluated the effects of clear aligner orthodontic treatment on lower third facial ageing in adult patients. The study compared a treated group (TG) of 68 patients using Invisalign clear aligners to a control group (UG) of 33 untreated patients. Each group was divided into subgroups based on age: under 40 (subgroup 1) and over 40 (subgroup 2). Facial aesthetics were assessed using the Wrinkle Severity Rating Scale (WSRS) at baseline (T0) and after an average of 12 months (T1) by a panel of five calibrated aesthetic experts.

Key results: In the younger subgroups, TG1 showed a statistically significant WSRS improvement of -0.21 (p<0.05) while UG1 worsened by 0.27 (p<0.05), with a between-group difference of -0.29 (p<0.05). In the older subgroups, TG2 improved by -0.28 (p<0.01) and UG2 worsened by 0.30 (p<0.05), yielding a highly significant between-group difference of -0.65 (p<0.001). The anti-aging effect was more pronounced in older patients.

The authors propose two mechanisms for this effect: (1) a "splint effect" from wearing two 0.75mm aligners for 22 hours/day, which slightly increases vertical intraoral dimension, reducing muscular activity and intra-articular compression; (2) cellular and molecular changes in bone and muscle structures from mechanical signals, potentially involving mechano-growth-factor (MGF) and insulin growth factor 1 (IGF-1) release.

Study limitations include a relatively small sample size, reliance on photograph-based evaluations, and lack of a traditional braces control group (excluded because brackets could create a confounding lifting effect on wrinkles). The authors conclude that clear aligner therapy provides a modest but beneficial anti-aging effect on the lower third of the face, particularly in older patients.

# How Can Invisalign And Cosmetic Dentistry Help Restore Your Smile?

Do you want your smile to be unique like you? Minor dental issues like crooked teeth or stains might prevent you from sharing your attractive grin. Many people look for ways to improve their smile, and two popular options are invisalign and cosmetic dentistry. Both these options can transform your smile and boost overall confidence. 

Learn how modern invisible aligners and cosmetic dental treatments can reshape, rejuvenate, and brighten your grin to match your inner spirit.

## **Invisalign Treatment, What Are Its Benefits, And How Does It Work?**

Invisalign is one of the most popular procedures for straightening teeth. The treatment involves using a clear plastic aligner that fits over your teeth. Unlike metal aligners, these do not include brackets or wires. These invisible teeth straighteners are custom-made for your dental set and gradually shift your teeth to the correct position. 

Since these aligners are discreet, no one will able to notice while you are wearing them. Consult your dentist for invisalign in Peachtree City and straighten your teeth professionally.  

### **How Does Transparent Aligner Work?**

If you choose this transparent aligner, the dental professional will carry out a 3D scan of your teeth and make a personalized treatment plan per your oral needs. This plan will help predict how your teeth will progress during the entire process. 

When the aligners are ready, you can quickly wear them throughout the day. To get the best results, switch to a new pair of aligners every 1-2 weeks. The treatment will generally take 12-18 months, depending on how many teeth need to be shifted. 

Transparent aligners are effective in treating-

* Crooked teeth
* Gaps between teeth
* Crowded teeth
* Mild overbites and underbites

### **Advantages Of Using Invisible Aligners**

There are different benefits to transparent teeth straighteners involve-

* **Comfort**– Getting invisalign involves using smooth, plastic aligners that provide the utmost ease. There are no wires or brackets that will cause sores inside the mouth.
* **Appearance-** these aligners are invisible; they will not affect the appearance during the treatment.

* **Convenience**—You can remove them while you eat, brush, and floss, making them perfect for maintaining good oral health.

* **Less Dental Visits**– These alignment treatments do not require regular orthodontist visits as you do with the metal braces.

## **What Is Cosmetic Dentistry?**

Cosmetic dental treatment is a type of oral care that enhances the aesthetics of your teeth, smile, and gums. Here are some of the issues that cosmetic dentistry solves-

* Discolored teeth
* Spaces between teeth
* Chipped or cracked teeth
* Missed tooth or teeth
* Misaligned, uneven, or irregularly shaped teeth

Some widespread procedures among patients include teeth whitening, crowns, bondings, veneers, etc. Consult with your [cosmetic Dentist in Peachtree](https://vasseydentalpartners.com/cosmetic-dentistry/) to treat misalignment, spots on enamel, or uneven teeth. 

Invisalign and cosmetic dental procedures work together to get the perfect smile you want. They provide total smile makeovers, give long-lasting results, and come with personalized treatment plans.

Our dentist in Peachtree City, Dr. Amish N., and our team recommend the best treatments for achieving a confident smile. Consult us today to get a complete smile makeover.

This is the official Invisalign website homepage, promoting Invisalign clear aligners as the #1 doctor-recommended clear aligner brand. Key claims include: Invisalign aligners are faster and more comfortable than braces, use SmartTrack Material for more predictable results, are designed using 25 years of insights from 23 million smiles, and are described as the world's most advanced clear aligners.

**Cost & Affordability:** Invisalign can be paid for using FSA, HSA, financing plans, or insurance. Insurance may cover up to $3,000 of orthodontic care.

**Treatment Duration:** Patients may see results in as little as 6 months, with changes visible in just a few weeks. Treatment times vary based on case complexity.

**Who Can Use Invisalign:**
- **Kids (ages 6+):** Phase I aligners and Invisalign Palatal Expander System available.
- **Teens:** Removable for sports/eating; results as good as braces but faster and more comfortable.
- **Adults:** Discreet alternative to braces with predictable results in as little as 6 months.

**How Treatment Works (3 Steps):**
1. Meet with your doctor for a precise 3D scan.
2. Begin the transformation with customized aligners.
3. Maintain your new smile with customized Vivera retainers.

**Press Mentions:** 90% of customers say it's worth it (RealSelf); dentists love Invisalign for safe, effective tooth movement (Forbes); recommended for wedding prep (Brides); noted for discreet appearance during Zoom calls (Cosmopolitan).

**Clinical References:** The page includes multiple footnoted citations supporting claims of speed, comfort, effectiveness, and patient satisfaction.

## 01丨牙齿矫正究竟能起到什么作用

用最接地气的话讲：**牙齿矫正，就是给牙齿“搬家 + 排队 + 调整上下牙咬合关系”**。

🦷 很多人以为矫正只是“好看一点”，其实远不止：

牙齿整齐了，更容易刷干净，**蛀牙、牙周病风险会下降**；

咬合关系变好，**咀嚼更省力，有些人的头痛、下颌关节不适也会缓解**；

最现实的一条：**笑起来更自信**，照片、社交、工作场合都能感受到差别。

所以它不是简单的“美容项目”，更接近一套“口腔功能 + 外观”的综合改善方案。

表 1：牙齿矫正能带来的主要改善作用

| 改善方向 | 具体作用说明 |
| --- | --- |
| 牙齿健康 | 牙齿更整齐、清洁更容易，蛀牙与牙周病风险下降 |
| 咬合功能 | 咬合关系改善，咀嚼更省力、效率更高 |
| 下颌关节 | 能缓解部分人群的头痛、咬合疲劳、关节弹响等不适 |
| 发音影响 | 对部分漏风、含糊等发音问题有改善作用 |
| 外观与自信 | 笑容更协调，提升社交与职场自信度 |

## 02丨常见几种矫正方式，怎么选不踩坑？



别急，我们一个一个聊，**用各自的特点来帮你记住它们**。👇

### 1⃣ 传统金属牙套：老实又能干的“工地师傅”

力量稳定、可控，**各种复杂咬合问题都能搞**；

价格在几种方式里通常是**最亲民**的；

吃东西要稍微注意，**特别硬、特别黏的食物要少吃**，避免托槽脱落。

👉 一句话总结：**实用、可靠、不花哨。**

### 2⃣ 陶瓷牙套：低调一点的“白领选手”

**长什么样？**

跟金属牙套结构类似，也是托槽 + 弓丝的组合；

托槽换成了**牙色或透明的陶瓷材质**，

再配合比较不显眼的弓丝，看起来比金属“温柔很多”。

**优点：**

比金属牙套更不显眼，说话、拍照时不会那么“钢铁风”；

一般佩戴舒适度不错。

**需要注意的地方：**

有些人如果经常喝咖啡、红酒、浓茶，橡皮圈可能会染色，需要更勤快地复诊更换；

费用通常比金属托槽**略贵一档**；

陶瓷托槽本身相对比较“脆”，极个别情况下可能会碎裂，但只要认真护理，这种情况并不常见。

**适合哪类人？**

在意形象、但又不一定要“完全隐形”的上班族；

不太想别人一眼就看出自己在戴牙套的人。

👉 一句话总结：**比金属更“好看一点”，性价比和美观度之间的平衡选择。**

### 3⃣ 舌侧矫正：外面完全看不见的“隐身侠”

**长什么样？**

托槽不是粘在牙齿外面，而是**贴在牙齿内侧（靠舌头那一面）**；

外人几乎完全看不出来你在矫正，属于真正意义上的“隐形牙套”。

![舌侧隐形托槽牙套的示意图](https://brightraydental.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/aesthetic-invisible-self-aligning-lingual-locks-2024-10-22-14-16-11-utc-scaled.jpg)

舌侧矫正把托槽放在牙齿内侧，实现“真正从外面看不见”的隐形效果。

**优点：**

从正面看几乎看不到牙套，对镜头敏感、人群曝光度高的人特别友好；

矫正原理依然是托槽 + 弓丝，力量控制上比较成熟。

**现实中的感受：**

一开始会比较“别扭”，

舌头总觉得有东西，

说话可能会轻微大舌、喷口水，

吃饭时也需要一点适应期；

清洁难度比传统牙套略高，需要更用心刷牙、使用牙线或冲牙器；

费用通常是几种方案里**最贵**的之一。

**适合哪类人？**

特别在意美观度的职业：比如演员、主持人、经常要开会演讲的职场人；

预算充足，对清洁和复诊比较有耐心的人。

👉 一句话总结：**真正的“隐身高手”，但价格与耐心也要跟上。**

### 4⃣ 隐形矫正（如 Invisalign 等）：能摘能戴的“自由派”

**长什么样？**

一副一副透明塑料牙套（矫正器），

戴上之后从正常社交距离看几乎不明显，

吃东西、刷牙时可以拿下来。

![男性手持一副透明隐形矫正器](https://brightraydental.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/man-holding-one-transparent-aligner-invisalign-or-2024-11-26-16-55-57-utc-scaled.jpg)

隐形矫正器外观低调，从日常社交距离几乎难以被察觉。

**使用方式简单说就是：**

> 每天乖乖戴够 20–22 小时，
>
> 每隔一段时间（例如 7–14 天）换一副新的，
>
> 一副一副“推进”牙齿慢慢移动。

**优点：**

外观自然，非常适合不想被看出戴牙套的成人；

可以摘下来吃饭、刷牙，口腔清洁相对更容易；

金属托槽磨嘴的问题明显少很多。

![透明隐形牙套细节特写](https://brightraydental.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/invisalign-braces-2024-10-18-09-15-39-utc-scaled.jpg)

隐形牙套通过一副一副更换，逐步把牙齿推向预期位置。

**潜在问题：**

**自律要求极高**——戴不满时间、老摘老忘，会直接拖慢、甚至影响疗效；

对极复杂的咬合问题，有时候需要配合橡皮筋、微种植钉等才能达到理想效果，有些情况干脆不建议只用隐形矫正；

费用通常不算低，具体要看病例复杂程度和所用品牌。

**适合哪类人？**

成年人、上班族、经常要见客户的人；

轻中度牙列不齐、咬合问题不是特别严重的患者；

对自己自律有信心的人（要是你连一天喝水都懒得拿杯子，那要慎重考虑）。

👉 一句话总结：**舒适、隐蔽、自由，但“不听话戴”的话，效果会打折扣。**

表 2：四大矫正方式对比（按特点分类）

| 矫正方式 | 优点 | 不足 / 注意点 | 适合人群 | 核心特点总结 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 传统金属牙套 | 力量强、效果稳定、适用范围广、价格亲民 | 显眼；初期可能磨嘴；饮食限制较多 | 学生、预算有限、咬合复杂者 | 实用可靠，不讲究外观 |
| 陶瓷牙套 | 美观度更高、不易被察觉、舒适度佳 | 橡皮圈易染色；费用略高；托槽较脆 | 上班族、注重形象者 | 美观与性价比的中间方案 |
| 舌侧牙套 | 从外面看完全隐形；专业度高 | 说话适应期；清洁难；费用昂贵 | 公众人物、经常露脸的职业人士 | 真正的“隐身矫正” |
| 隐形矫正 | 舒适、隐蔽、易清洁、可摘戴 | 需高度自律；复杂病例需联合治疗；费用较高 | 成人、上班族、轻中度不齐者 | 自由度高，不明显，但自律重要 |

## 03丨牙齿矫正的大概步骤和时间

很多人以为：

> “是不是我今天去，医生给我装个牙套，过几个月就拆了？”

现实要细致一点，不过也没那么可怕，我们拟一个比较典型的流程给你参考：

### 第 1 步：初诊咨询 & 全面检查

一般会包括：

医生肉眼检查牙齿排列、咬合情况；

拍牙片、全景片，必要时会做头影测量、CBCT（类似 3D X 光）了解骨头和牙根情况；

记录照片、取牙齿模型或做口内扫描。

**这一阶段你可以大胆问：**

我这种情况严不严重？

大概有哪些矫正方案？优缺点是什么？

预计需要多久？大概费用范围？

⚠️ 小提醒：

> 如果一上来什么都不看，就直接给你报价格、催你交定金，这种一定要多留个心眼。

### 第 2 步：先把“地基”弄好——口腔基础治疗

矫正前要确保牙齿和牙周（牙龈和牙槽骨）**状态尽量健康**，否则等于在“烂地基上盖楼”。

可能需要：

先把蛀牙补好；

牙龈炎、牙周炎先做洁牙、牙周治疗；

有些人需要拔除阻生智齿、严重拥挤的牙；

必要时先做简单的咬合调整。

这一步看起来“磨叽”，但非常关键，**做得越扎实，后面越顺利。**

![医生为患者进行专业洁牙与口腔基础治疗](https://brightraydental.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/doctor-doing-professional-teeth-cleaning-in-dental-2025-01-16-23-24-17-utc-scaled.jpg)

在进入矫正前，先把牙齿和牙周照顾好，是所有后续治疗顺利进行的前提。

### 第 3 步：正式上场——安装矫正器

取决于你选的是哪一种：

传统牙套/陶瓷牙套：

医生会在牙面上一个个粘托槽，

再上弓丝、橡皮圈，

整个过程大概 1–2 小时左右。

隐形矫正：

前期扫描数据会送去制作矫正器，

回来之后医生教你怎么戴、怎么摘，

有时会在牙面粘一些小小的“附件”（看起来像小突起），帮助牙齿更好受力。

刚装上的那几天，大部分人都会感觉到：

> 酸酸的、咬东西有点使不上劲儿，
>
> 有的部位还会轻微磨嘴。

别担心，这是牙齿在“适应新工作”，一般几天就会好很多。

### 第 4 步：定期复诊 & 调整

常见频率是 **每 4–8 周** 复诊一次（具体看个人情况和方案）：

传统牙套：更换不同硬度的弓丝、调整橡皮筋的方向；

隐形矫正：检查佩戴情况、发下一阶段的牙套、必要时微调方案；

同时会检查口腔清洁情况、是否有托槽脱落等问题。

⏱️ 总疗程：

轻度不齐：可能 1 年左右；

中度情况：普遍在 1.5–2 年；

复杂咬合：两年以上也不稀奇。

这里也顺便提醒一句：

> 老催医生“能不能快点”的同时，别忘了——**很多时候，耽误时间的是“自己没按时来复诊”或“没好好戴橡皮筋/隐形牙套”**。🤐

### 第 5 步：拆牙套？不，是进入“保持期”

很多人以为：

> “拆牙套那一刻，一切结束了！”

真相是：

> **拆牙套，只是从“矫正期”进入“保持期”。**

刚刚移动完的牙齿，就像刚搬完家的家具，需要一段时间“固定形态”。

医生会给你做**保持器**：

有透明的活动保持器、

也有粘在牙齿内侧的小钢丝（固定保持器）。

刚开始通常需要**每天长时间佩戴**，

后期可以逐渐改为只在晚上戴，但完全不戴一般是不建议的。

![女性双手托着两副透明保持器](https://brightraydental.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/hands-of-a-woman-holding-invisible-retainers-2024-12-10-03-23-55-utc-scaled.jpg)

保持器是防止牙齿“各回各家”的关键一环，拆牙套后同样不能偷懒。

不戴保持器会怎样？

> 牙齿很可能会“各回各家”，出现不同程度的复位，有人甚至需要第二次矫正。

所以，**保持器这一步千万别偷懒**。很多人后悔的根源就两个字：

> 「不戴」。

表 3：牙齿矫正步骤与时间概览

| 步骤 | 主要内容 | 时间范围 | 重点提示 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 初诊咨询 & 检查 | 拍片、检查咬合、口扫、方案沟通 | 1 次就诊 | 多问方案、费用、时长，避免“看都不看就报价” |
| 口腔基础治疗 | 补蛀牙、洁牙、牙周治疗、处理智齿等 | 数周 – 数月 | 地基越稳，后期越顺利 |
| 安装矫正器 | 粘托槽、上弓丝；隐形矫正则教学佩戴 | 1–2 小时 | 初期酸软正常，几天会适应 |
| 定期复诊 & 调整 | 换弓丝、调橡皮筋；隐形矫正更换托盘 | 每 4–8 周 | 不按时复诊会拖慢进度 |
| 保持期 | 配戴保持器（透明或固定钢丝） | 数年甚至长期 | 不戴 = 复位风险上升 |

## 04丨牙齿矫正到底疼不疼？

这个问题基本上每个准备戴牙套的人都会问。我们直接说结论：

矫正过程中的不适，**大多数人都能接受**，

不属于“剧痛”“受不了那种”。

主要有哪些感觉？

1. **刚上牙套/换更紧的弓丝/换新一副隐形牙套的前几天：**

牙齿会酸软，咬东西有点难受，

有人形容“像牙齿酸到不太敢咬排骨那种”；

2. **嘴唇、脸颊内侧的磨擦：**

比如刚戴金属托槽那段时间，

可以用医生给的保护蜡贴在托槽上，会舒服很多；

3. **隐形矫正：**

刚换新牙套时会紧一些，但通常较少出现“磨破嘴”的情况。

一般来说：

不适 **前 3 天最明显**，

1 周左右，大部分人都能适应，

有特别难受的情况，可以在医生指导下适当用一些止痛药。

👉 如果你本身比较怕疼，可以在矫正前就和医生说清楚，医生在调力量、安排节奏时会更照顾你的感受。

表 4：矫正过程中常见不适类型

| 不适类型 | 具体表现 | 缓解方式 | 持续时间 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 牙齿酸软 | 咬东西使不上力、酸胀感 | 软食、少咀嚼、必要时止痛药 | 前 3 天明显，1 周内适应 |
| 口腔磨擦 | 嘴唇/脸颊被托槽磨到 | 使用牙科保护蜡 | 通常 1–2 周习惯 |
| 隐形牙套紧张感 | 换新托盘时感觉“紧紧的” | 持续佩戴，一般无需特殊处理 | 约 1–3 天 |

## 05丨矫正之前，你最好先知道这些“坑”

这里帮你列几个**真心建议**，少走弯路：

### 1️⃣ 只看价格，不看医生资质和经验

便宜不是不行，但如果：

没有正畸专长；

没有详细检查就随便给方案；

用“现在交钱就打折”“今天做就送什么”这种方式逼你做决定；

那就要非常警惕。

**矫正是一场“长期合作”**，你要选的是：

愿意跟你沟通、

讲理、

肯认真做随访的医生，而不只是“价格最低”的那一家。

### 2️⃣ 口腔清洁敷衍了事

戴牙套后，食物残渣更容易卡在托槽、钢丝周围，如果刷牙还是沿用原来的“随缘模式”，基本可以预见：

蛀牙、牙龈出血、口臭、白垩斑（牙面一块块白白的斑）都会找上门。

建议养成：

每天至少 **早晚认认真真刷牙**，

配合 **牙线、牙缝刷或冲牙器**，

隐形矫正还要注意：**每次吃完饭刷完牙再戴回去**。

### 3️⃣ 对“保持期”掉以轻心

很多人是这样翻车的：

> 戴牙套的时候可积极了，拆完之后保持器几乎不戴。

结果就是——几年以后又默默长歪一点，然后心里默默后悔。

记一句：

> **矫正是短期的，保持是长期的。**

### 4️⃣ 想用最轻松的方式，解决最复杂的问题

有的人情况比较复杂（例如严重的骨性错颌、上下颌发育问题），

可能需要配合拔牙、种植钉，

甚至需要考虑正颌手术。

如果医生认真评估后建议你：

> “仅靠隐形矫正可能达不到特别好的效果。”

这通常不是为了多收钱，而是真实情况的限制。**不要把“听劝”当成“被套路”。**

表 5：做矫正前常见“避坑点”

| 避坑点 | 可能出现的问题 | 如何避免 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 只看低价，不看资质 | 方案草率、疗程延长、效果不佳 | 选择专业医生，先评估后决定 |
| 清洁不到位 | 蛀牙、牙龈炎、白斑、口臭 | 每日认真刷牙 + 牙线/冲牙器 |
| 忽视保持期 | 牙齿复位、重新变歪 | 按医嘱戴保持器，不能偷懒 |
| 复杂问题只想用最简单方案 | 效果不佳、疗程拉长 | 尊重医生判断，必要时联合治疗 |

## 06丨关于价格：范围、影响因素、怎么不被“忽悠”

以纽约为例，给你一个**大致参考范围**（具体费用还是要以面诊为准）：

金属托槽：大约 **$3,000 – $6,000**；

陶瓷托槽：大约 **$4,000 – $7,000**；

舌侧牙套：大约 **$8,000 – $12,000**；

隐形矫正（以常见品牌为例）：大约 **$4,000 – $8,000 或以上**，看复杂程度。

影响价格的因素主要有：

病例难度（简单排齐 vs. 复杂咬合、骨性问题）；

是否需要拔牙、种植钉、正颌联合治疗；

医生的资历、诊所所在地区；

使用的材料和矫正系统。

小建议：

1. **不要只问“总价多少”，也要问清楚：**

是否包含所有 X 光、复诊、保持器费用；

有没有额外隐形费用；

2. **问清楚付款方式：**

是否可以分期；

是否可以配合保险报销；

3. 如果你跑了好几家，方案和价格差很多，**可以把检查资料带着，再找一家可信的医生做个“第二意见”。**

## 07丨几岁做矫正最合适？成年了还能不能做？

### 👶 孩子 & 青少年

一般来说：

**6–7 岁左右**：建议至少做一次正畸评估，主要是看看颌骨发育、咬合有没有明显问题；

**11–14 岁左右**：大部分恒牙已经萌出，是做矫正的黄金阶段之一，

骨头还比较“软”，

牙齿移动相对更快，

有些骨性问题可以通过功能矫治、早期干预来改善。

![牙医手持由隐形矫正器摆成的爱心形状](https://brightraydental.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/smiling-doctor-holding-heart-made-of-clear-aligner-2024-11-25-12-39-18-utc-scaled.jpg)

孩子的牙齿发育期，是部分矫正问题最容易解决的黄金窗口。

当然，这并不是说“错过这个年龄就永远晚了”，只是说：

> **在发育期，有些问题能更容易、也更温和地处理。**

### 🧑‍💼 成年人：20/30/40 岁还能做吗？

答案很简单：

> **只要牙周条件允许（牙槽骨和牙龈情况还可以），绝大多数成年人是可以做矫正的。**

区别只是：

成年人的骨头发育已基本稳定，牙齿移动速度可能比青少年稍慢；

有些人已经有牙周问题、缺牙、修复体，这些都需要在矫正方案里一并考虑；

成年人对外观、工作、社交的要求更高，因此更青睐 **陶瓷牙套、隐形矫正** 等方式。

我们也见过不少 30 多岁、40 多岁的患者：

有的是为了改善咬合、咀嚼；

有的是长期对自己笑容不满意，想在事业和生活进入新阶段前，给自己一个“整牙礼物”。

![成年人手持隐形矫正器特写](https://brightraydental.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/man-holding-one-transparent-aligner-invisalign-or-2024-11-26-16-55-57-utc-scaled.jpg)

只要牙周条件允许，成年后依然可以安全有效地进行牙齿矫正。

👉 只要检查后医生评估你的牙周状况可以承受矫正的力量，成年矫正完全不是问题。

## 常见问答 – 牙齿矫正

不只是“好看”，更像是给牙齿和咬合系统做一场“综合升级”。

可以从三个层面看：

**1）健康层面：**

* 牙齿整齐以后，刷牙更容易刷干净，蛀牙、牙周病的风险会下降；
* 咬合关系改善后，咀嚼效率变好，有些人原来吃东西总是一边用力，久了关节酸、头痛，矫正后能缓解不少；
* 有些发音问题（漏风、含糊不清）也和牙齿位置、咬合有关，矫正后会改善。

**2）功能层面：**

* 上下牙咬合关系好，咬东西更省力，不会老觉得“咬不烂、总塞牙”；
* 对以后要做烤牙、种植等修复，也是一种“打基础”。

**3）外观与自信：**

* 牙弓形态变好、牙齿排列整齐，人一笑，脸部气质直接上一个台阶；
* 工作、社交、拍照都更自在，不再刻意抿嘴。

简单说：不是纯颜值消费，而是“功能 + 美观”的长期投资。

大多数人对矫正的感受是：“酸、紧、胀，有点不自在，但没到‘受不了’的程度”。

**常见感受：**

* **刚上牙套 / 换紧一点的弓丝 / 换新隐形牙套：**牙齿会酸软，咬东西有点难受，有人形容“像吃多了酸的东西，牙根有点发酸，不太敢啃排骨那种”。
* **嘴唇、脸颊磨擦：**金属或陶瓷托槽一开始可能磨到口腔内侧，一般用医生给的保护蜡贴在托槽上，可以明显缓解。
* **隐形矫正：**更像“紧紧的压迫感”，通常不太会磨破嘴。

通常前 3 天不适感最明显，1 周左右绝大多数人都适应了。

**怕疼的人可以：**

* 提前跟医生说自己比较敏感，医生在加力时会温和一些；
* 用冷敷、软食度过前几天，必要时按照医生建议短期用止痛药。

结论：怕疼也可以做，大多数人“能忍，而且比想象中轻”。

可以从这几方面来比较：

* **显眼程度：**金属托槽一张嘴就能看到，存在感很强；陶瓷托槽接近牙色或透明，整体更柔和。
* **坚固性：**金属比较结实，很难碎；陶瓷略脆，极少数情况可能碎托槽（正常使用问题不大）。
* **染色问题：**金属托槽本身不太会染；陶瓷托槽本身不易染，但橡皮圈容易被咖啡、茶、红酒染色，需要更勤快复诊更换。
* **费用：**陶瓷一般比金属贵一档。

**适合人群大致是：**

* 金属牙套：学生党、预算有限但咬合问题复杂的人；
* 陶瓷牙套：上班族、见客户较多、介意“钢牙”的人。

如果预算有限，对外观没那么敏感，金属很合适；如果在意“开口不要那么显眼”，陶瓷牙套更友好。

舌侧矫正最大的卖点是：从外面几乎完全看不到托槽。

**现实中需要考虑：**

* **适应成本：**舌头会一直碰到托槽，说话初期可能有点大舌、漏风，需要时间适应发音。
* **清洁难度：**托槽在里面，刷牙比传统牙套难度大，必须更认真使用牙线、冲牙器。
* **费用：**通常是几种方式里最贵的一档，医生操作难度、技术要求也更高。
* **适用性：**很多错颌可以做舌侧，但方案设计复杂度高，最适合那些对外观极致在意的人，比如公众人物、经常上镜的职业。

总结：舌侧矫正适合愿意为“完全隐形”多花钱、多花精力的人，不太适合追求省事、省力的人。

隐形矫正的优点很明显，但也不是“零存在感”。

**优点：**

* 透明、低调，拍照、开会不太看得出来；
* 可摘戴，吃饭可以正常吃，刷牙清洁更方便；
* 舒适度一般比金属托槽好，不太磨嘴。

**但你要知道：**

* 必须每天戴够 20–22 小时，不然效果会打折甚至乱跑；
* 换新牙套的前两天，照样会紧、会酸；
* 严重咬合问题（骨性、严重深覆合等）可能需要别的手段配合，甚至不适合单靠隐形矫正。

隐形矫正适合“自律 + 在意美观 + 病例不算太复杂”的人；如果连“睡前刷牙”都经常忘，就要慎重。

原则非常明确：有蛀牙先补，有牙周问题先治，再谈矫正。

**原因：**

* 矫正让清洁难度增加，如果本来就蛀牙多、牙龈发炎，再戴托槽和钢丝，只会火上浇油；
* 牙周本来就不稳，硬拉着移动牙齿，风险是牙齿变松，甚至丢牙。

正规的做法是：

* 先全面检查：X 光、牙周探诊、口腔检查；
* 先打“地基”：补蛀牙、做洁牙、控制牙周炎；
* 再开始矫正计划。

如果有人说“这些先别管，先戴牙套再说”，那你要认真考虑这位医生是否值得长期合作。

时间和三个因素相关：

* **问题的复杂程度：**轻度拥挤大约 1 年左右，中度通常 1.5–2 年，复杂咬合（深覆合、开合、骨性问题）2 年以上很正常。
* **配合程度：**是否按时复诊？橡皮筋/隐形牙套有没有老实戴？托槽掉了、钢丝扎嘴有没有拖很久才去修？
* **治疗目标：**只是“看起来差不多齐了就行”，还是尽量做到咬合平衡良好？认真打磨咬合细节，时间一般会稍长一些，但更稳定。

一年能否搞定要看起点，不是看你着不着急。想“快又好”，最关键是：听话、配合、不缺诊。

最常见的坑有：

* **刷牙随便刷：**后果是牙龈出血、口臭、白斑、蛀牙。解决办法是：每天早晚认真刷，加牙线/冲牙器。
* **保持器不戴：**拆完牙套觉得“大功告成”，保持器束之高阁，几年后又歪一点，然后后悔当初没坚持戴。
* **矫正期间乱减肥、营养不良：**长期吃得太软、太少，整个人状态都会受影响，尤其是青少年，更要注意营养均衡。
* **频繁更换医生、换诊所：**每个医生的设计理念和操作习惯不同，中途频繁折腾，容易让疗程混乱。

真正的坑不在牙套上，而在态度和习惯上。

矫正过程中，牙齿“有点松动”的感觉是正常的，因为牙齿是通过牙周膜悬吊在骨头里，不是死死钉死。

**在矫正时：**

* 小力量让牙齿缓慢移动，牙周组织会一边吸收、一边重建；
* 只要力量控制得当、牙周健康，最终牙齿会在新位置重新稳定。

会出问题的情况是：

* 本来就有严重牙周病，还不治疗就硬要做矫正；
* 口腔清洁做得很差，矫正中牙周状况进一步恶化。

重点不是“矫正会不会让牙齿变松”，而是你是不是在一个牙周健康、医生规划合理、清洁到位的前提下做矫正。

客观差别确实有：

* 骨头不再生长，移动速度一般比青少年慢一点；
* 成年人可能有旧补牙、烤牙、缺牙、牙周问题，这些都要纳入整体计划考虑；
* 对外观、时间、舒适度要求更高。

但优势也很明显：

* 成年人目标更明确，知道自己要什么；
* 配合度往往更好，不太会“说不戴就不戴”。

只要牙周条件允许，成年人的矫正效果完全可以非常好，关键是有没有遇到愿意花时间做整体规划的医生。

可以，但要提前跟医生沟通好你的作息模式。

**建议：**

* 隐形矫正会更灵活一些，复诊间隔可以稍微拉长（视方案而定），出差时也不会太影响外观；
* 传统牙套也不是不行，重点是能否大致按时复诊，托槽掉了、钢丝扎嘴要尽量及时处理；
* 可以请医生尽量把复诊安排在你相对固定在本地的时间，并问好遇到急症时的应对方式。

忙不是矫正的阻碍，不配合才是。

常见处理方式（最终以主治医生意见为准）：

* 刚戴没几天就丢：通常会让你退回上一副，戴稳一段时间，再决定是否重做这一副；
* 快要换下一副时丢：有时可以直接提前换下一副，但要评估牙齿有没有完全到位。

建议：

* 把已完成阶段的旧牙套保留一两副备用；
* 准备一个固定收纳盒，养成随取随收的习惯，减少丢失风险。

要看矫正方式和阶段：

* 传统托槽矫正期间：不建议做强力冷光美白，因为牙面被托槽遮住，美白会不均匀，可以通过认真清洁和护理来改善观感；
* 隐形矫正期间：部分居家美白方案可以在医生指导下搭配使用，但不建议自己乱买“美白牙贴”折腾。

更稳妥的做法是：矫正结束、牙齿位置稳定后，再系统做美白，效果更均匀也更安全。

拔不拔牙不是患者拍板，而是正畸方案设计的问题。

**拔牙常见用于：**

* 牙弓特别拥挤，空间明显不够；
* 嘴突厉害，需要后退前牙让侧面轮廓更协调。

* 医生没详细检查、没分析头影 X 光，就轻描淡写说“拔几颗就好了”；
* 患者自己执念“我听说不拔就没效果”。

* 为什么要拔？
* 不拔的话会有什么妥协？
* 对脸型影响有多大？

理论上前 1–2 年是“高危复位期”，但实际上很多人如果完全不戴，终身都存在不同程度复位风险。

* 刚拆完牙套前 6–12 个月：每天长时间佩戴（除吃饭、刷牙外尽量戴着）；
* 之后几年：可改成只在晚上戴，但不建议完全停戴。

* 如果原来牙齿严重前突、嘴巴鼓，尤其是需要拔牙后退前牙的情况，矫正后侧面轮廓会变柔和，嘴不会那么顶；
* 如果只是轻微拥挤、小问题，脸型变化不会像整容那样明显，更多是笑起来更自然、牙弓形态更协调。

它不能代替削骨、脂肪调整，也不是所有人“矫正后都会小 V 脸”。

* 找正规、有正畸经验的医生，比所谓“神奇低价”更重要；
* 把检查做全：X 光、全景片、必要的头影测量，没检查就报价、就戴牙套的要谨慎；
* 问清楚费用包含哪些：是否包括片子、复诊、保持器，有没有中途加价；
* 不要被各种“升级套餐”洗脑，材料有档次之分，但不是越贵越神奇；

* 近距离交谈别人会看见，但现在大家接受度很高；
* 真正看重你的人，不会因为你戴牙套就否定你的专业。

隐形矫正：

* 一般社交距离几乎看不出，适合经常要开会、谈判、上镜的人。

* 我现在的牙齿和咬合，是否已经影响到自卑、咀嚼或清洁困难？
* 如果 5 年后回头看，会不会后悔“这几年其实完全可以做，却一直拖”？
* 我能不能接受在未来 1–2 年里，稍微为这件事挤一点时间和耐心出来？

**👁️ 角膜因长期戴镜而变得不规则**，会让：LASIK / 全飞秒评估变困难；度数测不准；手术效果打折。

因此术前要求：软镜停戴 1–2 周；RGP 停戴 1–4 周（甚至更久）。

This is a comprehensive Chinese-language blog post from BrightRay Dental (精典牙科), a dental clinic located in Flushing, New York (131-07 40th Rd., Level E, Unit E36, Flushing, NY 11354, phone: 718-888-1817). The article serves as an educational guide about dental orthodontics (teeth straightening), covering:

**Purpose of Orthodontics**: Teeth straightening is described as "moving + queuing + adjusting bite relationships." Benefits include improved oral hygiene (reducing cavities and periodontal disease), better chewing function, relief from jaw pain/headaches for some patients, and enhanced confidence in social and professional settings.

**Four Types of Orthodontic Treatment**:
1. **Traditional Metal Braces** ($3,000-$6,000): Strong, reliable, affordable, suitable for complex cases. Visible and may cause initial discomfort.
2. **Ceramic Braces** ($4,000-$7,000): Less visible than metal, good balance of aesthetics and cost. Ceramic brackets can be more brittle; rubber bands may stain.
3. **Lingual Braces** ($8,000-$12,000): Fully hidden (placed behind teeth), most expensive. Requires adaptation period for speech and cleaning.
4. **Clear Aligners (Invisalign)** ($4,000-$8,000+): Removable, discreet, comfortable. Requires high patient compliance (20-22 hours/day wear). Not suitable for the most complex cases.

**Treatment Process** (5 steps):
1. Initial consultation and examination (X-rays, photos, scans)
2. Pre-treatment dental work (fill cavities, treat gum disease, extract wisdom teeth if needed)
3. Installation of braces or aligners (1-2 hours)
4. Regular follow-up appointments (every 4-8 weeks, total duration 1-2+ years)
5. Retention phase (wearing retainers long-term to prevent relapse)

**Key Advice**: 
- Don't shop solely on price; prioritize qualified orthodontists
- Maintain excellent oral hygiene during treatment
- Do not neglect the retention phase (most common reason for relapse)
- Complex cases may require extractions, temporary anchorage devices, or even orthognathic surgery

**Age Considerations**: 
- Children: First orthodontic evaluation recommended around age 6-7; golden period for treatment is around 11-14 years old
- Adults: Can be treated at any age as long as periodontal health is adequate. 30-40+ year-old patients are common.

**Pain/Discomfort**: Most patients experience soreness (especially first 3 days after adjustment), which is manageable with soft foods and, if needed, pain relievers. The article emphasizes that discomfort is tolerable for most people.

The article includes a disclaimer stating it does not constitute medical advice and that individual consultation is required.

# 健康教育

## 矫正=整形？想变美的你必须知道的事！

2017-01-30

随着正畸治疗在社会中的普及，越来越多的人们听说正畸治疗可以改变脸型。这是真的么？

      其实，牙齿矫正对脸型改变的效果因人而异。在临床案例中，确实有很多因为牙齿、颌骨和颅面缺陷，通过矫正以后，脸型和比例都变得更漂亮。说堪比整容，绝对不是耸人听闻。但是能通过正畸改变脸型也是分具体情况的:

上下唇凸出

上下唇凸出的患者。比如通过拔牙获得空间让前牙往回收。前牙的位置向后移动，骨组织也会向后移动，从而减小嘴唇的突度，下巴颏的线条更加流畅。视觉上会突显鼻梁更加高挺，侧貌看起来更加立体，更加精致。

下巴后缩

这样的患者面形上往往显示侧貌凸出，下巴后缩，颏部短小，肌肉紧张，看上去很没精神。正畸医生通过正畸治疗使患者的下巴产生前移的效果，改善下巴后缩的侧貌，纠正凸面型。但是，有些严重的下巴后缩则无法通过移动牙齿来矫正面型，须等到成年后进行正畸-正颌联合治疗或颏部成型术达到改善面形的目的。

“地包天”

反颌，俗称“地包天”。患者侧面面型呈月牙状，大下巴。“地包天”会严重地影响口腔、颜面、颌骨的生长发育。医生可以通过矫正治疗纠正患者牙齿的位置关系适量改善前凸的下巴。“地包天”的治疗则是越早越好，过于严重的“地包天”畸形则无法通过正畸达到满意的效果，须等到成年后进行正畸-正颌手术联合治疗。

深覆合

“咬合深”—深覆合。正常的前牙关系应该是上前牙盖住下前牙大约2毫米，如果遮盖过多，甚至下牙完全被上前牙挡住看不见，则称之为深覆合。深覆合的患者从侧面看面部下1/3过短以及下巴后缩，从而影响面容美观。这种畸形还会导致前牙的牙周疾病及面部关节疾病。通过矫正可以重新建立正常的前牙及后牙咬合关系，改善脸部偏短的问题。

通过对以上几种面型正畸前后的描述，相信很多人对正畸治疗的神奇之处充满了感叹。随着正畸技术的不断进步，正畸治疗早已不单单是把牙齿排列整齐，更加追求患者的整体面部协调美观。其实，通过正规的正畸治疗后，你也是潜力股呦~~

args.summary:
This is a health education article from Hangzhou Stomatology Hospital (杭州口腔医院), published on January 30, 2017, addressing whether orthodontic treatment (tooth correction) can change facial shape. The article explains that orthodontic treatment can indeed improve facial aesthetics in certain cases, comparable to cosmetic surgery, but the effects vary by individual. It describes four specific facial conditions that can be improved through orthodontics:

1. **Protruding lips (上下唇凸出)** - Extraction of teeth allows front teeth to retract, reducing lip protrusion, making the nose appear more prominent and the side profile more defined.
2. **Receding chin (下巴后缩)** - Orthodontic treatment can create a forward chin effect, improving side profile and convex facial shape. Severe cases may require combined orthodontic-orthognathic surgery.
3. **Underbite/Crossbite (地包天)** - A moon-shaped face with prominent chin. Early treatment is recommended; severe cases require orthodontic-surgical combined treatment.
4. **Deep overbite (深覆合)** - Lower third of the face appears shortened, chin receding. Orthodontics can re-establish proper bite and improve facial proportions.

The article emphasizes that modern orthodontics aims not only to straighten teeth but also to achieve overall facial harmony and aesthetics.

--- SOURCE 1: Self-Perceived Dental Esthetics and Orthodontic Treatment Need ---
URL: https://www.jrmds.in/articles/selfperceived-dental-esthetics-and-orthodontic-treatment-need-88601.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a scientific research article published in the Journal of Research in Medical and Dental Science (2021, Volume 9, Issue 12) titled "Self-Perceived Dental Esthetics and Orthodontic Treatment Need." The study was conducted by researchers from Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Health and Umm Al-Qura University, led by Amjad Alotaibi.

**Objective:** To explore self-perceived dental esthetics of adults and evaluate their subjective orthodontic treatment needs on esthetic grounds.

**Methodology:** A descriptive, cross-sectional study using a self-administered questionnaire distributed randomly to the general population in the Makkah region of Saudi Arabia. A total of 1,014 participants (737 female, 277 male, aged 18-60) completed the questionnaire, which included the Aesthetic Component of the Index of Orthodontic Treatment Need (AC-IOTN) and the Oral Aesthetics Subjective Impact Score (OASIS).

**Key Findings:**
- 66.5% of participants had positive self-perceived dental esthetics (mean OASIS score: 12.53 ± 7.34, range 5-35).
- According to AC-IOTN self-evaluation: 90.1% had "no need" for orthodontic treatment, 5.1% had "borderline need," and 4.7% had "definite need."
- A statistically significant positive correlation was found between OASIS and AC-IOTN scores (r=0.37, p=0.005), indicating that as concern about dental esthetics increased, perceived orthodontic treatment need also increased.
- Gender significantly influenced the demand for orthodontic treatment, with females more concerned about appearance.
- Prior studies cited in the article note that professional assessments identify much higher orthodontic treatment needs (71.6% severe need) compared to self-perceived needs.

**Conclusion:** The study found a weak association suggesting that when esthetic self-satisfaction decreases, the subjective need for orthodontic treatment increases. The authors recommend that patients' perceptions of their own dental esthetics and gender differences should be considered in orthodontic treatment planning.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"The positive association indicated that as the individual's OASIS score increased, suggesting a greater concern about dental esthetics, his or her orthodontic treatment needs also increased on the AC-IOTN."; "The demand for orthodontic treatment was significantly influenced by gender."; "A comparison of these estimates to professional assessment indicates that only 15.2% have little or no need for treatment, 13.2% have a moderate/borderline need, and 71.6% have a definite need for treatment."; "The present study suggests that the majority of adult individuals have positive self-perceived dental esthetics, and that the demand for orthodontic treatment is significantly influenced by gender."; "It is important to consider the patient's perception of his or her own dental esthetics along with gender differences in orthodontic treatment planning."
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 2: Is Orthodontics Only About Aesthetics? ---
URL: https://www.theorthodontists.com.au/blog/is-orthodontics-only-about-aesthetics

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage from The Orthodontists (Australia) addresses the question of whether orthodontics is purely about aesthetics or serves medical purposes. The article argues that while aesthetics is a significant component of orthodontic treatment, there are also important medical benefits. It discusses how appearance impacts self-image, confidence, career prospects, and social interactions, citing the "halo effect" where attractive people are perceived as having other positive qualities. SUMMARY:
<summary>
This retrospective cohort study published in the Journal of Clinical and Experimental Dentistry (2018) by Romeo Patini et al. evaluated the effects of clear aligner orthodontic treatment on lower third facial ageing in adult patients. The study compared a treated group (TG) of 68 patients using Invisalign clear aligners to a control group (UG) of 33 untreated patients. Each group was divided into subgroups based on age: under 40 (subgroup 1) and over 40 (subgroup 2). Facial aesthetics were assessed using the Wrinkle Severity Rating Scale (WSRS) at baseline (T0) and after an average of 12 months (T1) by a panel of five calibrated aesthetic experts.

Key results: In the younger subgroups, TG1 showed a statistically significant WSRS improvement of -0.21 (p<0.05) while UG1 worsened by 0.27 (p<0.05), with a between-group difference of -0.29 (p<0.05). In the older subgroups, TG2 improved by -0.28 (p<0.01) and UG2 worsened by 0.30 (p<0.05), yielding a highly significant between-group difference of -0.65 (p<0.001). The anti-aging effect was more pronounced in older patients.

The authors propose two mechanisms for this effect: (1) a "splint effect" from wearing two 0.75mm aligners for 22 hours/day, which slightly increases vertical intraoral dimension, reducing muscular activity and intra-articular compression; (2) cellular and molecular changes in bone and muscle structures from mechanical signals, potentially involving mechano-growth-factor (MGF) and insulin growth factor 1 (IGF-1) release.

Study limitations include a relatively small sample size, reliance on photograph-based evaluations, and lack of a traditional braces control group (excluded because brackets could create a confounding lifting effect on wrinkles). The authors conclude that clear aligner therapy provides a modest but beneficial anti-aging effect on the lower third of the face, particularly in older patients.

--- SOURCE 14: Orthodontic treatment demand for fixed treatment and aligners among young adults in middle Europe and South America – a questionnaire study ---
URL: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10908024

SUMMARY:
<summary>
## Orthodontic Treatment Demand for Fixed Treatment and Aligners Among Young Adults in Middle Europe and South America

This 2024 study published in *BMC Oral Health* (PMCID: PMC10908024) assessed orthodontic treatment demand, prior experience, and knowledge about fixed and aligner treatments among young adults (aged 18–30) in Poland and Chile.

### Methodology
- Cross-sectional questionnaire study (25 questions) delivered via social media over 3 months (July–September 2022)
- Target sample: >400 per country; 1,092 responses obtained (670 from Chile, 422 from Poland)
- Response rate: 1.99%
- The survey was exempted from bioethical committee approval (ref: RWP/6546/2022P)

### Key Findings on Treatment Demand
- **Prior orthodontic treatment**: 42.9% in Poland vs. 25.0% in Chile had been treated
- **Planning treatment within a year**: 11.8% in Poland vs. 5.3% in Chile
- **Overall**: 51.6% of all respondents did not want orthodontic treatment; 16.5% were unsure
- 20.6% of all respondents would rely on doctor's recommendation for appliance type; 14.7% were interested solely in aligners
- 58% of respondents had heard about aligners

### Patient Preferences
- **Direct-to-consumer services (without doctor)**: Not acceptable to 85.1% (Poland) and 64.8% (Chile)
- **Treatment without doctor supervision**: Unacceptable to 85% (Poland) and 65% (Chile)
- **Consultation by a general dentist vs. orthodontist**: Opinions were divided (about 38% said no in both countries)
- Most important treatment features: acceptable price (69.4%), expected excellent result (66.3%), treatment time (57.5%), aesthetics (45%)

### Knowledge Gaps
- Most young adults provided incorrect answers about various aspects of aligner treatment
- Only ~23% knew the correct daily wear time for aligners (22–24 hours)
- Only ~20% knew teenagers with mixed dentition could be treated with aligners
- 46.5% correctly believed aligners are indicated only for non-complex malocclusions
- In Chile, top recognized brands: Invisalign (43.9%); in Poland: Dr. Smile (52.8%)
- Main information sources: Chile relied on orthodontists/dentists/associates; Poland relied on social media

### Conclusions
- Patients in both countries demand treatment and monitoring by orthodontists
- A high percentage of patients want treatment exclusively with aligners
- Direct-to-consumer orthodontics is not attractive to patients
- Young adults lack adequate knowledge about aligner treatment
- Many people want treatment despite having undergone prior orthodontic treatment
- Poland and Chile show similar socioeconomic/developmental indices but cultural differences influence treatment demand and knowledge
</summary>

--- SOURCE 1: Self-Perceived Dental Esthetics and Orthodontic Treatment Need ---
URL: https://www.jrmds.in/articles/selfperceived-dental-esthetics-and-orthodontic-treatment-need-88601.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a scientific research article published in the Journal of Research in Medical and Dental Science (2021, Volume 9, Issue 12) titled "Self-Perceived Dental Esthetics and Orthodontic Treatment Need." The study was conducted by researchers from Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Health and Umm Al-Qura University, led by Amjad Alotaibi.

**Objective:** To explore self-perceived dental esthetics of adults and evaluate their subjective orthodontic treatment needs on esthetic grounds.

**Methodology:** A descriptive, cross-sectional study using a self-administered questionnaire distributed randomly to the general population in the Makkah region of Saudi Arabia. A total of 1,014 participants (737 female, 277 male, aged 18-60) completed the questionnaire, which included the Aesthetic Component of the Index of Orthodontic Treatment Need (AC-IOTN) and the Oral Aesthetics Subjective Impact Score (OASIS).

**Key Findings:**
- 66.5% of participants had positive self-perceived dental esthetics (mean OASIS score: 12.53 ± 7.34, range 5-35).
- According to AC-IOTN self-evaluation: 90.1% had "no need" for orthodontic treatment, 5.1% had "borderline need," and 4.7% had "definite need."
- A statistically significant positive correlation was found between OASIS and AC-IOTN scores (r=0.37, p=0.005), indicating that as concern about dental esthetics increased, perceived orthodontic treatment need also increased.
- Gender significantly influenced the demand for orthodontic treatment, with females more concerned about appearance.
- Prior studies cited in the article note that professional assessments identify much higher orthodontic treatment needs (71.6% severe need) compared to self-perceived needs.

**Conclusion:** The study found a weak association suggesting that when esthetic self-satisfaction decreases, the subjective need for orthodontic treatment increases. The authors recommend that patients' perceptions of their own dental esthetics and gender differences should be considered in orthodontic treatment planning.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 3: Profiles of facial soft tissue changes during and after orthodontic treatment in female adults ---
URL: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9233845

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This study, published in BMC Oral Health (2022), used 3dMD stereo photography technology to investigate facial soft tissue changes during and after orthodontic treatment in 52 adult Chinese females (24 extraction, 28 non-extraction cases). The research aimed to determine whether "braces face" (thinner faces, protruding cheekbones, sunken temples) is a real orthodontic effect or due to excessive patient attention, and to identify factors associated with these changes.

**Key Findings:**
- Overall facial soft tissue protrusions reduced by about 2 mm on average during orthodontic treatment, regardless of extraction status. Negative changes (~1 mm reduction) occurred in infraorbital, cheekbone, zygomatic, sub-zygomatic, lower cheilion, buccal, mandibular angle, and temporal regions.
- Extraction was **not** a major factor for facial soft tissue changes. Changes were consistent between extraction and non-extraction groups, with only the temporal region (R11) showing statistically significant differences between the two groups.
- Negative changes in the buccal region (R9) moderately correlated with shorter distances of nasion-menton and subnasale-menton, and larger ratios of face height to face width, indicating that adult females with **wide and short faces** may be more prone to negative soft tissue changes.
- An increase in posterior facial height (N-Go distance) was identified as a risk factor for negative changes in the zygomatic arch area (R3).
- A moderate positive correlation was found between maxillary first molar width changes and negative changes in the lower cheek region (R9) (rs = 0.41, P < 0.05), suggesting that narrower dental arch width correlates with more obvious lower cheek depression.
- Soft tissue changes were detectable as early as 3 months after treatment initiation but did not necessarily worsen thereafter.

**Conclusions:** Short face height, long mid/lower face width, and large face height-to-width ratios are major factors for aesthetic risks. Changes in posterior facial height and first molar arch width are also risk factors. Extraction is not a primary cause of facial soft tissue changes.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 4: The impact of orthodontic treatment on face and smile attractiveness: A cross-sectional study of longitudinal data ---
URL: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0889540626001563

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a scientific article published in the American Journal of Orthodontics and Dentofacial Orthopedics (Volume 170, Issue 2, August 2026, Pages 262-273) titled "The impact of orthodontic treatment on face and smile attractiveness: A cross-sectional study of longitudinal data."

**Objective:** To assess the effect of orthodontic treatment on facial and smile attractiveness as perceived by laypeople.

**Methods:** The study included 37 adults (aged 21-35 years): 29 treated patients and 8 untreated controls. A total of 132 photographs (full-face smiles and close-up smiles) were collected pre- and post-treatment for treated patients and once for controls. Laypeople (n=297) rated the images using a visual analog scale (VAS). Statistical analyses included univariate regression models, analysis of covariance, t-tests, and Spearman correlation.

**Key Results:**
- Orthodontic treatment significantly improved facial attractiveness by 15.6% (P<0.001) and smile attractiveness by 24.3% (P<0.001) on VAS scores.
- Post-treatment ratings were higher than untreated controls (P_face=0.029; P_smile=0.010), with no significant differences at baseline.
- Higher Aesthetic Component of the Index of Orthodontic Treatment Need (IOTN-AC) scores correlated with lower initial VAS ratings (r=0.67; P<0.001).
- Age and treatment duration had no significant effect on attractiveness ratings.
- Evaluator demographics (including history of orthodontic treatment) did not significantly influence ratings.

**Conclusions:** Orthodontic treatment improves facial and smile attractiveness as perceived by laypeople, supporting its esthetic benefits for patient communication and treatment planning.
</summary>

SUMMARY:

This is a scientific case report published in the International Journal of Surgery Case Reports (2021) describing a multidisciplinary approach to orofacial rehabilitation combining orthognathic surgery, orthodontics, and minimally invasive orofacial harmonization procedures.

**Case:** A 28-year-old female patient presented with mandibular prognathism, anteroposterior maxillary deficiency, dental crowding, malocclusion (Angle Class III), and functional/esthetic changes negatively affecting psychosocial interactions.

2. Phase 2: Bimaxillary orthognathic surgery + lip filling with hyaluronic acid + bichectomy (simultaneously), aided by Nemoceph™ software for surgical planning

**Conclusion:** The case reaffirms that orthognathic surgery combined with minimally invasive facial harmonization procedures represents a current trend in oral and maxillofacial rehabilitation, addressing both functional and esthetic needs.

--- SOURCE 12: Clear aligners’ effects on aesthetics: evaluation of facial wrinkles ---
URL: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6057070

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This retrospective cohort study published in the Journal of Clinical and Experimental Dentistry (2018) by Romeo Patini et al. evaluated the effects of clear aligner orthodontic treatment on lower third facial ageing in adult patients. The study compared a treated group (TG) of 68 patients using Invisalign clear aligners to a control group (UG) of 33 untreated patients. Each group was divided into subgroups based on age: under 40 (subgroup 1) and over 40 (subgroup 2). Facial aesthetics were assessed using the Wrinkle Severity Rating Scale (WSRS) at baseline (T0) and after an average of 12 months (T1) by a panel of five calibrated aesthetic experts.

Key results: In the younger subgroups, TG1 showed a statistically significant WSRS improvement of -0.21 (p<0.05) while UG1 worsened by 0.27 (p<0.05), with a between-group difference of -0.29 (p<0.05). In the older subgroups, TG2 improved by -0.28 (p<0.01) and UG2 worsened by 0.30 (p<0.05), yielding a highly significant between-group difference of -0.65 (p<0.001). The anti-aging effect was more pronounced in older patients.

The authors propose two mechanisms for this effect: (1) a "splint effect" from wearing two 0.75mm aligners for 22 hours/day, which slightly increases vertical intraoral dimension, reducing muscular activity and intra-articular compression; (2) cellular and molecular changes in bone and muscle structures from mechanical signals, potentially involving mechano-growth-factor (MGF) and insulin growth factor 1 (IGF-1) release.

Study limitations include a relatively small sample size, reliance on photograph-based evaluations, and lack of a traditional braces control group (excluded because brackets could create a confounding lifting effect on wrinkles). The authors conclude that clear aligner therapy provides a modest but beneficial anti-aging effect on the lower third of the face, particularly in older patients.
</summary>

Dublin, Nov. 20, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The ["United States Orthodontics Market - Treatment Trends & Forecast 2025-2033"](https://www.researchandmarkets.com/reports/6101936/united-states-orthodontics-market-treatment?utm_source=GNE&utm_medium=PressRelease&utm_code=2q9wcj&utm_campaign=2108602+-+United+States+Orthodontics+Market+Research%2c+Treatment+Trends+%26+Forecast+Report+2025-2033&utm_exec=chdomspi) report has been added to **ResearchAndMarkets.com's** offering.  
  
The United States Orthodontics Market in 2024 was valued at US$ 2.04 billion and is expected to reach US$ 5.02 billion during the forecast period from 2025 to 2033, with a CAGR of 10.5%. The reason behind the growth is growing awareness of the aesthetics of teeth, advancements in clear aligners, and increased demand for early treatment of orthodontics for children and adolescents, which is propelling the overall market.

[![](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///ywAAAAAAQABAAACAUwAOw==)](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/DF8E914373CF3CB9E1CCBADC056E3235D0E6480DCBBD558C2EA2FD2AF35694BB/subgraphmysterio/resizefit_w960;quality_80;format_webp/https:%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fglobenewswire.com%2F62be0bec48f4142fc5e4f7d4ec58be36)

In the U.S., orthodontic care is particularly coveted by adolescents and adults because of the increasing focus on dental appearance and oral health. Parents particularly endeavor to have their children treated in the early years to avoid more serious dental issues later in life. Adults are now choosing discreet aligner solutions for aesthetic purposes as well as enhanced self-esteem. With teledentistry and improved orthodontic technologies, care has become more accessible, efficient, comfortable, and readily available for diverse populations in the U.S.  
  
**Growth Drivers in the United States Orthodontics Market**

**Increased Demand for Aesthetic Dental Treatments**  
  
Increased attention to personal appearance and the need for flawless smiles have greatly impacted the U.S. orthodontics market. Numerous people are opting for cosmetic dental treatments, including clear aligners, to secretly enhance the alignment of their teeth. This is especially true among working adults and professionals who want non-invasive, cosmetic solutions. Advances in aligners, combined with the growing power of social media, are promoting the use of orthodontic therapy for aesthetic reasons, further propelling the market.

In February 2025, LuxCreo introduced the 4D Bright Aligner, a revolutionary dental appliance that brings together the functionality of the 4D Aligner with the cosmetic look of whiter teeth. Driven by LuxCreo's end-to-end 4D Aligner system and ActiveMemory polymer, this aligner provides accurate orthodontic correction and delivers consistent elastic forces over treatment duration, enabling patients to keep their natural smile.  
  
**Technological Advancements and Digital Orthodontics**  
  
Digital orthodontics with 3D imaging, computer-aided design (CAD), and intraoral scanners has changed the way treatment planning and execution is done. The technologies provide quicker diagnosis, improved patient comfort, and more tailored treatment options. Added benefits include accuracy and outcomes improvement through the use of artificial intelligence in treatment simulations.

These innovations render orthodontic treatments more desirable and convenient, particularly to technology-oriented people, thus driving the market in the U.S. to increase. In August 2023, Angelalign Technology Inc. introduced its tailor-made clear aligners to the U.S. market. The firm is a global leader in clear aligner dental technology and provides evidence-based clinical knowledge.  
  
**Expanding Adult and Teen Patient Base**  
  
There has been a steep rise in orthodontic treatment amongst adolescents and adults alike within the U.S. In the past, adolescents traditionally formed the backbone of the orthodontic patient pool, but increasingly adults form an expanding portion of the market, largely because of clear and removable aligners. Increased orthodontic awareness, affordable financing options, and increased insurance benefits are motivating more patients to seek corrective dental treatments, leading to increased demand for orthodontic treatment.

In December of 2023, Align Technology, Inc., a leading global medical device company, reported that the FDA has given its approval for its Invisalign Palatal Expander System to use commercially in the U.S. This approval makes for wider patient use, encompassing children, adolescents, and adults (who might also need surgery or other methods).  
  
**United States Orthodontics Market Challenges**

**Excessive Treatment Prices and Limited Insurance Coverage**  
  
Orthodontic treatments can be quite expensive, especially when it relates to enhanced options like clear aligners which guarantee an invisible and efficient method for straightening teeth. Sadly, most insurance companies provide partial or no coverage for orthodontic treatment, posing a great hindrance to access for families attempting to afford these services.

This is most severe among low- and middle-income families, where the cost of high out-of-pocket spending can deter patients from initiating their treatment process or make them drop their plans along the way. Consequently, even with increasing demand for orthodontic treatment, the market is unable to expand because it has many limitations placed upon it, leaving many people without access to smile-improving treatments they would like.  
  
**Lack of Trained Orthodontists in Rural Areas**  
  
Urban areas of the United States abound with an abundance of orthodontic practitioners and state-of-the-art facilities, offering a location where patients can readily have access to prompt and superior dental treatment. In contrast, rural communities greatly lack skilled orthodontists, depriving many of its population of basic services.

This geographic inequality not only limits immediate access to care, but also seriously jeopardizes the dental health of children. Delayed early treatment results in more complicated and expensive orthodontic problems in the future, as issues are not treated in the early stages. Thus, addressing the uneven dispersal of dental practitioners is key to nurturing balanced market development and guaranteeing that every patient, irrespective of where they are located, has access to what they require.

## Cosmetic Dentistry Market Outlook 2025-2034

The global cosmetic dentistry market was valued at **$45.42 billion** in 2025 and is projected to reach **$92.44 billion** by 2034, expanding at a compound annual growth rate of **8.2%**. This robust expansion is driven by multiple converging factors spanning consumer behavior, technological innovation, and demographic shifts. Rising disposable incomes across developed and emerging economies have fundamentally reshaped patient expectations, with cosmetic procedures transitioning from luxury services to mainstream dental treatments. The proliferation of **clear aligner systems** pioneered by Align Technology has democratized orthodontic correction, while **CAD-CAM technology** has made custom veneers and crowns faster and more affordable. Additionally, the integration of **[digital smile design software](/report/digital-smile-design-software-market)** and **intraoral scanning** into routine practice has enhanced treatment predictability and patient acceptance. Consumer spending on elective dental procedures accelerated significantly during 2023-2025 as confidence in discretionary spending rebounded post-pandemic. The market also benefits from the aging Baby Boomer demographic in North America and Europe, where teeth replacement through implants and crowns represents a major spending category. Furthermore, social media influence has created powerful demand pull, particularly among teenagers and young adults seeking Instagram-ready smiles through whitening, veneers, and orthodontic correction. Personalized aesthetic procedures are gaining traction as consumers increasingly view smile enhancement as part of broader cosmetic wellness spending. Geographic expansion into Asia-Pacific has unlocked millions of middle-class consumers pursuing cosmetic improvements previously unavailable in their home markets. This analysis is based on primary and secondary research conducted through Q4 2025, with data verified as of May 2026.

## Cosmetic Dentistry Market Regional Outlook 2025-2034

North America retained the dominant position with **$17.33 billion** in market size during 2025, representing **38.2%** of global revenue. Medical automation advances have streamlined practice operations, enabling practitioners to handle higher patient volumes efficiently.

India's emerging cosmetic dentistry sector benefits from lower procedure costs relative to Western markets, attracting medical tourism while simultaneously building domestic patient bases in major cities. The region's growth rate is projected to outpace mature markets throughout the 2026-2034 period as disposable incomes rise and treatment accessibility expands.
