# The Selfie Effect: How Social Media Is Reshaping Cosmetic Dentistry

* Dr. Sep Pouresa DMD
* Jul 29
* 8 min read

Quick answer: Social media has fundamentally changed who seeks cosmetic dental treatment and why. According to industry data, 90.7% of cosmetic dental practitioners attribute rising aesthetic demand directly to social media, while 72% report patients specifically requesting procedures to look better in selfies—a pattern now recognized in clinical literature as "Snapchat dysmorphia."

Take a scroll through Instagram or TikTok. Within minutes, you'll encounter teeth that are impossibly white, perfectly straight, and flawlessly symmetrical—sometimes real, sometimes filtered, often a combination of both. For millions of people, that scroll ends with a creeping dissatisfaction about their own smiles. And increasingly, it ends with a call to a cosmetic dentist.

Social media has reshaped virtually every corner of the beauty industry. Cosmetic dentistry is no exception. The global cosmetic dentistry market crossed $31 billion in 2026 (Towards Healthcare, 2025)—and behind much of that growth is a force that didn't exist two decades ago: the selfie.

This post examines how platforms like Instagram, TikTok, and Snapchat are driving demand for cosmetic dental procedures, what the clinical community is saying about it, and how to make smart decisions about your smile when your feed is full of filtered ones.

**Why Are So Many People Suddenly Unhappy with Their Smiles?**

Social media didn't invent insecurity about appearance. But it did give it a 24/7 platform.

According to a systematic review of 15 studies covering over 10,000 participants globally, 72% of patients reported being motivated by influencer posts when choosing a cosmetic dental treatment (URBN Dental, 2026). Nearly half of all Americans report that social media has damaged their smile confidence. That's not a niche phenomenon—that's a population-scale shift in self-perception.

The mechanism is straightforward. Social comparison is a deeply human tendency. Platforms like Instagram are engineered to maximize engagement, which in practice means surfacing aspirational content: idealized bodies, perfect skin, and—increasingly—flawless teeth. Every time users compare themselves to a curated highlight reel, their own reflection becomes a little harder to feel good about.

What's changed in recent years is the addition of photo-editing tools that don't just showcase other people's appearance—they show users a modified version of their own. Apps like Facetune and Snapchat's beauty filters reshape faces, smooth skin, and whiten teeth in real time. The result is a live preview of a version of yourself that doesn't exist, which researchers at Boston Medical Center warn can trigger body dysmorphic disorder in vulnerable individuals.

**What Is Snapchat Dysmorphia, and Why Are Dentists Taking It Seriously?**

"Snapchat dysmorphia" is a term coined to describe a specific pattern: patients seeking cosmetic procedures not to look like a celebrity or an ideal, but to look like the filtered version of themselves. It was first flagged in plastic surgery contexts, but cosmetic dentistry has seen the same trend emerge.

Dr. Susan McMahon, an accredited member of the American Academy of Cosmetic Dentistry, documented cases in which patients with clinically attractive smiles were presenting for treatment because social media standards had shifted around them. As she noted in a clinical case series published in Dentistry Today, patients who had completed orthodontic treatment and received professional whitening were no longer satisfied—not because anything had gone wrong, but because the benchmark had moved.

The data backs this up. According to URBN Dental's 2026 industry report, 72% of aesthetic dental professionals report patients requesting procedures specifically to look better in selfies. That figure has remained consistent across multiple surveys and reflects a genuine change in patient motivation—one that the profession is actively working to understand and respond to responsibly.

This doesn't mean these motivations are illegitimate. Many patients with real clinical concerns—gaps, discoloration, chips, asymmetry—find the confidence to seek treatment because social media showed them what was possible. The challenge lies in distinguishing patients with genuine cosmetic concerns from those whose expectations have been distorted by filters that no real procedure can replicate.

**Who Is Driving This Demand?**

The social media effect is most pronounced among younger adults, though its reach extends further than many expect.

Millennials aged 25–40 are currently the primary consumers of cosmetic dental treatments, driven by a combination of aesthetic goals, social media presence, and career-related appearance investment (URBN Dental, 2026). Adults aged 40–51 are the most common demographic specifically seeking veneers, often for age-related wear and discoloration rather than selfie optimization.

Self-esteem plays a measurable role. Research published in peer-reviewed journals in 2025 and 2026 found that 82.2% of people with low self-esteem express interest in cosmetic dental procedures, compared to 66.6% of those with high self-esteem. Social media amplifies this gap—nearly half of Americans who report confidence damage from social media are also more likely to explore cosmetic options.

The influencer effect is particularly powerful. Across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, 68% of social media users report being more inclined toward cosmetic procedures after exposure to influencer content. When a trusted creator documents their smile makeover journey in real time—before, during, and after—it normalizes the process and lowers the perceived barrier to action. That normalization is part of what has contributed to a 250% increase in veneer procedures in recent years, with around 600,000 Americans now receiving veneers annually (URBN Dental, 2026).

**Which Procedures Are Most Influenced by Social Media?**

Not all cosmetic dental procedures are equally driven by social media, but a few have clear viral momentum.

Teeth whitening remains the most widely adopted cosmetic dental procedure, with 19% of US adults having undergone professional treatment. It's the first procedure most social-media-motivated patients consider—relatively affordable, non-invasive, and immediately visible in photos.

Veneers have become the centerpiece of smile transformation content online. The before-and-after format is native to social media, and veneer results are among the most dramatic. Porcelain veneers now cost between $900 and $2,500 per tooth in the US (URBN Dental, 2026), which drives many patients to research alternatives, including composite veneers and dental tourism options.

Clear aligners have also benefited from social media visibility, with 18 million patients worldwide having used Invisalign as of Q1 2025. Adults now account for 70% of all new clear aligner cases—a major demographic shift from the system's teen-focused origins. The appeal is partly aesthetic, partly practical: discreet orthodontics that work in the background of an active social life.

Dental bonding and contouring are gaining traction as fast, affordable entry points for patients who want visible improvement without committing to veneers. These procedures address chips, gaps, and minor misalignment—exactly the kinds of imperfections that high-resolution selfies make more apparent.

**Is the Selfie Effect a Problem?**

This is where the clinical community is genuinely divided—and where nuance matters.

On the positive side, social media has democratized access to information about cosmetic dentistry. Patients arrive at consultations better informed, more specific about what they want, and more willing to have honest conversations about their concerns. For those who have lived with real cosmetic issues—significant discoloration, prominent gaps, or worn teeth—seeing others transformed by treatment can be the catalyst they needed.

The concern, raised consistently by dental professionals, is about conservation of tooth structure—particularly in younger patients. The most ethical approach to cosmetic dentistry prioritizes minimal intervention: doing the least invasive procedure that achieves the desired result. When patients arrive expecting to replicate a filtered image or a celebrity smile that required significant dental work, managing those expectations requires both clinical skill and thoughtful communication.

The data suggests that once patients begin cosmetic treatment, demand tends to compound. Some 84.3% of people who have had at least one cosmetic dental procedure express interest in further treatment, compared to 47.7% of those with no prior cosmetic experience. Social media keeps those aspirations continuously refreshed.

**How to Make a Smart Decision When Social Media Is Your Starting Point**

Social media is a reasonable place to discover what's possible. It's a poor place to set your expectations. Here's how to close that gap.

Bring screenshots, not ultimatums. Using social media images as inspiration is fine. Arriving with a filtered photo and asking your dentist to replicate it precisely is a setup for disappointment. Share your inspiration, then let your dentist explain what's realistic for your specific anatomy.

Ask about conservative options first. Before committing to veneers, ask whether whitening, bonding, or contouring could achieve a comparable result. The less tooth structure altered, the better your long-term dental health.

Get a proper consultation—not just a quote. A thorough cosmetic dental consultation includes a full smile evaluation, a discussion of your oral health baseline, and an honest assessment of what each procedure involves. If a provider skips this and moves straight to pricing, look elsewhere.

Separate the filter from the feeling. Sometimes the discomfort isn't about a specific flaw—it's about general confidence. Cosmetic dentistry can genuinely improve self-esteem, but it works best when it addresses real concerns rather than chasing an algorithmically ideal version of yourself.

**Your Smile, Your Standards**

Social media has made cosmetic dentistry more visible, more accessible, and more demanded than at any point in its history. That's not entirely a bad thing. More awareness means more people seeking care, more innovation in treatment options, and a broader conversation about what patients actually want from their smiles.

The most empowering thing you can do is approach that conversation with clear eyes. Social media can show you what's possible. A qualified cosmetic dentist can show you what's right for you. Those two things don't always match—and when they diverge, the dentist's assessment is the one worth trusting.

If you're considering cosmetic dental work and want to understand your options, book a consultation with our team. We'll give you an honest, thorough evaluation and help you build a treatment plan grounded in your actual smile—not a filtered version of it.

**Frequently Asked Questions**

What is Snapchat dysmorphia in the context of cosmetic dentistry?

Snapchat dysmorphia refers to a pattern in which patients seek cosmetic procedures to look like the filtered or edited version of themselves—rather than a celebrity or abstract ideal. In dentistry, this means patients requesting treatments to replicate the teeth they see in their own edited selfies. Researchers at Boston Medical Center have linked this phenomenon to body dysmorphic disorder in some cases.

How has social media changed what patients ask for at cosmetic dental consultations?

According to industry data, 72% of aesthetic professionals now report patients requesting specific procedures to look better in selfies. Patients are arriving with more visual references, greater awareness of available treatments, and—in some cases—expectations shaped more by filters than clinical realities. This has prompted the profession to place greater emphasis on expectation management and conservative treatment approaches.

Which cosmetic dental procedures have grown most due to social media influence?

Teeth whitening, porcelain veneers, clear aligners, and dental bonding have all seen demand increases linked to social media. Veneers have experienced a 250% increase in procedure volume in recent years, while professional whitening is now the most common cosmetic dental procedure, with 19% of US adults having undergone treatment (URBN Dental, 2026).

Is it wrong to want cosmetic dental work because of what I've seen on social media?

No. Social media is a legitimate source of inspiration and awareness. The key is working with a qualified dentist to distinguish between realistic goals and filter-driven expectations. Many patients with genuine cosmetic concerns—discoloration, chips, gaps—find the confidence to seek help through social media. The concern arises when expectations are based on unattainable, digitally altered images.

How do I know if a cosmetic dental procedure is right for me?

The starting point is a comprehensive consultation with an experienced cosmetic dentist. A proper evaluation covers your oral health baseline, your specific aesthetic concerns, and the least invasive treatment options that can address them. If a provider doesn't take this approach, seek a second opinion.

args.summary:
This article examines how social media platforms like Instagram, TikTok, and Snapchat are reshaping cosmetic dentistry. Key findings include: 90.7% of cosmetic dental practitioners attribute rising aesthetic demand to social media, and 72% report patients requesting procedures specifically to look better in selfies. The global cosmetic dentistry market exceeded $31 billion in 2026. A systematic review of 15 studies covering over 10,000 participants found that 72% of patients were motivated by influencer posts when choosing cosmetic dental treatment. Nearly half of Americans report social media has damaged their smile confidence.

The article introduces "Snapchat dysmorphia" — a term describing patients seeking cosmetic procedures to look like filtered versions of themselves rather than celebrities or ideals. Boston Medical Center researchers warn this can trigger body dysmorphic disorder. Millennials aged 25-40 are the primary consumers of cosmetic dentistry, with 82.2% of people with low self-esteem expressing interest in procedures. Veneers have seen a 250% increase in recent years, with 600,000 Americans receiving them annually. Other popular procedures include teeth whitening (19% of US adults), clear aligners (18 million patients worldwide), and dental bonding.

The article notes clinical division on this trend: social media has democratized access to information, but raises concerns about tooth structure conservation, especially in younger patients. 84.3% of people who have had one cosmetic procedure express interest in further treatment. The article advises patients to bring screenshots as inspiration rather than ultimatums, ask about conservative options first, seek proper consultations, and separate filtered expectations from genuine confidence concerns.

# Social media impact on students’ decision-making regarding aesthetic dental treatments based on cross-sectional survey data

* [Yolanda Freire](#auth-Yolanda-Freire-Aff1)[1](#Aff1)[na1](#na1),
* [Margarita Gómez Sánchez](#auth-Margarita-G_mez_S_nchez-Aff1)[1](#Aff1)[na1](#na1),

[Save article](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8/save-research?_csrf=SMOv44osyWielEeYxOnC9hm7keKjgD3P)

## Abstract

This study investigated the influence of social media on patients regarding aesthetic dental treatments according to sex, type of treatment, and time since their last treatment. A cross-sectional study was conducted using a web-based survey. Participants were students over 18 years of age who were social media users and had undergone aesthetic dental treatment. 504 responses were included. Data evaluation was made using Pearson chi-square test. The level of significance was set at *p* < .05. 29.37% of the respondents indicated that social media influenced their decision to have their aesthetic treatment. Regarding the influence of social media, no differences were observed between males and females, nor by type of aesthetic treatment. Participants who had undergone an aesthetic dental treatment within the last year were more influenced by social media than those who had undergone it more than two years ago. Posts from dental clinics or dentists were the type of content that most influenced participants. Social media can influence some patients' decision to undergo aesthetic dental treatment, thus dental practices and dentists should consider the increasing importance of social media in their daily practice.

## Introduction

Web 1.0 initially emerged as a space for companies to disseminate information to the public[1](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR1 "Aghaei, S., Nematbakhsh, M. A. & Farsani, H. K. Evolution of the world wide Web: from WEB 1.0 to WEB 4.0. Int. J. Web Semant. Technol. 3, 1–10. 
                  https://doi.org/10.5121/IJWEST.2012.3101
                  
                 (2012).") and it was characterized by its limited scope for interactive communication with users[2](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR2 "Tennant, B. et al. eHealth literacy and Web 2.0 health information seeking behaviors among baby boomers and older adults. J. Med. Int. Res. 17, e70. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2196/jmir.3992
                  
                 (2015)."), as it only allowed searching and reading information[1](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR1 "Aghaei, S., Nematbakhsh, M. A. & Farsani, H. K. Evolution of the world wide Web: from WEB 1.0 to WEB 4.0. Int. J. Web Semant. Technol. 3, 1–10. 
                  https://doi.org/10.5121/IJWEST.2012.3101
                  
                 (2012)."). However, the evolution of web technologies and user interfaces has significantly changed the way users interact with information[3](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR3 "Eysenbach, G. Medicine 2.0: Social networking, collaboration, participation, apomediation, and openness. J. Med. Int. Res. 10, e22. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2196/jmir.1030
                  
                 (2008)."). This development has led to dynamic and interactive websites with user-oriented features, also referred to as Web 2.0[4](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR4 "Vandelanotte, C. et al. Effectiveness of a web 2.0 intervention to increase physical activity in real-world settings: randomized ecological trial. J. Med. Int. Res. 19, e390. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2196/jmir.8484
                  
                 (2017)."), which encompasses a range of Internet applications that have fostered increased participation, collaboration, openness, and social networking[2](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR2 "Tennant, B. et al. eHealth literacy and Web 2.0 health information seeking behaviors among baby boomers and older adults. J. Med. Int. Res. 17, e70. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2196/jmir.3992
                  
                 (2015)."). These Web 2.0 applications include blogs, social networking platforms, and social media[5](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR5 "Bardus, M. et al. The use of social media to increase the impact of health research: Systematic review. J. Med. Int. Res. 22, e15607. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2196/15607
                  
                 (2020)."). According to the Cambridge Dictionary, social media refers to `websites and computer programs that allow people to communicate and share information over the Internet using a computer or mobile phone[6](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR6 "Cambridge Dictionary. Cambridge University Press & Assessment; 2023 [cited 2023 Apr 28]. social media; [one page]. 
                  https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/social-media
                  
                "). Examples of social media include blogs, wikis, podcasts, Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, or LinkedIn[6](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR6 "Cambridge Dictionary. Cambridge University Press & Assessment; 2023 [cited 2023 Apr 28]. social media; [one page]. 
                  https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/social-media
                  
                "),[7](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR7 "Gholami-Kordkheili, F., Wild, V. & Strech, D. The impact of social media on medical professionalism: A systematic qualitative review of challenges and opportunities. J. Med. Int. Res. 15, e184. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2196/jmir.2708
                  
                 (2013).").

In recent years, there has been a significant increase in the use of social media[8](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR8 "eurostat. Digital economy and society statistics - households and individuals. 
                  https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Digital_economy_and_society_statistics_-_households_and_individuals
                  
                 (2022)."). Originally designed for personal use, they are now widely used by businesses to promote products or services and engage with consumers[9](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR9 "Nelson, K. L., Shroff, B., Best, A. M. & Lindauer, S. J. Orthodontic marketing through social media networks: The patient and practitioner’s perspective. Angle Orthod. 85, 1035–1041. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2319/110714-797.1
                  
                 (2015)."). In the health sector, social media play a crucial role in various areas such as health promotion, research, recruitment, and marketing[10](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR10 "Farsi, D. Social media and health care, part I: Literature review of social media use by health care providers. J. Med. Int. Res. 23, e23205. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2196/23205
                  
                 (2022)."). Specifically, in the field of dentistry, marketing has emerged as an additional facet to the clinical practice of dentists[11](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR11 "McGuigan, P. J. & Eisner, A. B. Marketing the dental practice: eight steps toward success. J. Am. Dent. Assoc. 137, 31–38. 
                  https://doi.org/10.14219/jada.archive.2006.0056
                  
                 (2006)."). Consequently, this has led to a proliferation of oral health-related information on certain websites, aimed at promoting specific products[12](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR12 "Ruiz, M., Kabani, F. & Cotter, J. A review of the effects of oral health media hype on clients’ perception of treatment. Can. J. Dent. Hyg. 56, 31–38 (2022).").

Dental websites sometimes contain posts with promotional content, often accompanied by before and after photographs[13](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR13 "Rosenstiel, S. F., Pappas, M., Pulido, M. T. & Rashid, R. G. Quantification of the esthetics of dentists’ before and after photographs. J. Dent. 37, e64–e69. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jdent.2009.05.003
                  
                 (2009)."). These photographs have been found to be effective in encouraging some people to seek treatment[14](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR14 "Baik, K. M., Anbar, G., Alshaikh, A. & Banjar, A. Effect of social media on patient’s perception of dental aesthetics in Saudi Arabia. Int. J. Dent. 27, 4794497. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1155/2022/4794497
                  
                 (2022)."). In addition, advertisements related to cosmetic dentistry[15](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR15 "Salim, N. A., Jubair, F., Hassona, Y. M., Izriqi, S. & Al-Fuqaha’a, D. Esthetic dentistry on twitter: benefits and dangers. Int. J. Dent. 8, 5077886. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1155/2021/5077886
                  
                 (2021).") or specific publications on treatments such as tooth whitening[16](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR16 "Simsek, H., Buyuk, S. K., Cetinkaya, E., Tural, M. & Koseoglu, M. S. “How I whiten my teeth”: YouTube™ as a patient information resource for teeth whitening. BMC Oral Health 20, 183. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1186/s12903-020-01172-w
                  
                 (2020)."). As a result, social media platforms have facilitated direct access to such content, contributing to an increased demand for cosmetic dentistry[17](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR17 "Abbasi, M. S. et al. Impact of social media on aesthetic dentistry: general practitioners’ perspectives. Healthcare (Basel) 10, 2055. 
                  https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare10102055
                  
                 (2022)."). However, the content published is not always developed by oral health professionals, but rather by users or individuals commonly referred to as influencers. In recent years, the figure of the influencer has grown as a communication method to engage directly with consumers[18](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR18 "Willis, E. & Delbaere, M. Patient influencers: The next frontier in direct-to-consumer pharmaceutical marketing. J. Med. Int. Res. 24, e29422. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2196/29422
                  
                 (2022)."). For example, influencers are individuals with a large number of followers and interactions on social media[19](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR19 "Dhanesh, G. S. & Duthler, G. Relationship management through social media influencers: Effects of followers’ awareness of paid endorsement. Public Relat. Rev. 45, 101765. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pubrev.2019.03.002
                  
                 (2019).") who sometimes post content related to dentistry. It is therefore relevant to investigate the potential influence of social media in relation to aesthetic dental treatments, especially given the increasing demand for such treatments[17](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR17 "Abbasi, M. S. et al. Impact of social media on aesthetic dentistry: general practitioners’ perspectives. Healthcare (Basel) 10, 2055. 
                  https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare10102055
                  
                 (2022).") and the impact of website advertising on customer perceptions of oral healthcare[12](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR12 "Ruiz, M., Kabani, F. & Cotter, J. A review of the effects of oral health media hype on clients’ perception of treatment. Can. J. Dent. Hyg. 56, 31–38 (2022)."). This aspect is of particular importance in the young adult population, as they have a higher use of social media[20](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR20 "Eurostat. Do you participate in social networks? 
                  https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-eurostat-news/-/edn-20210630-1
                  
                 (2022)."). Therefore, the rationale for the study is that there is lack of scientific evidence analyzing the impact of social media on aesthetic dentistry. It is important for dentists to be aware of the impact of social media on the demand for aesthetic treatments so that they can take it into account in their daily practice. Thus, the aim of this study was to describe the influence of social media on students who had undergone aesthetic dental treatment according to sex, type of aesthetic dental treatment received and time when it was performed to explore whether social media have influenced the performance of these treatments. The null hypothesis was that there would be no significant differences in the influence of social media on young patients in terms of sex, type of aesthetic dental treatment received and when it was performed.

## Methods

### Study design

To conduct this cross-sectional study, the web-based questionnaire (WBQ) survey method was chosen. WBQs are self-administered questionnaires that users can access through a browser on several devices, such as computers, mobiles, or tablets[21](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR21 "Callegaro L, Manfreda KL, Vehovar V. Web Survey Methodology (ed. Metzler, K.) 4–9 (SAGE Publications, 2015)."). With the increasing use of the Internet, WBQ questionnaires represent an alternative to traditional paper questionnaires[22](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR22 "Hohwü, L. et al. Web-based versus traditional paper questionnaires: A mixed-mode survey with a Nordic perspective. J. Med. Int. Res. 15, e173. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2196/jmir.2595
                  
                 (2013)."). It has been observed that this type of questionnaire is completed to a greater extent and with fewer missing items compared to paper-based questionnaires[23](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR23 "Zazpe, I. et al. Paper-based versus web-based versions of self-administered questionnaires, including food-frequency questionnaires: Prospective cohort study. JMIR Public Health Surveill. 5, e11997. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2196/11997
                  
                 (2019)."). At present, the WBQ questionnaires have been used in various research studies[24](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR24 "Swanston, E., Pulman, A., Dogan, H., Murphy, J. & Bitters, F. Scoping the need for a tailored mHealth app to improve health and well-being behavioral transformation in the police: Exploring the views of UK police workers via web-based surveys and client meetings. JMIR Form Res. 5, e28075. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2196/28075
                  
                 (2021)."),[25](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR25 "Lee, Y. H., Jang, Y. J. & Lee, S. K. Obstacles to health big data utilization based on the perceptions and demands of health care workers in South Korea: Web-based survey study. JMIR Form Res. 7, e45913. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2196/45913
                  
                 (2023)."). Access to the survey was facilitated by a QR code. This study was conducted in accordance with the principles of the World Medical Association's Declaration of Helsinki and was registered in Clinical Trials under ID NCT05850403 in May 2023.

### Ethics committee approval

This study was approved by the Ethics Committee of the Universidad Europea de Madrid (CIPI/22.022). Data handling was carried out in accordance with the regulations (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament, and of the European Council 27th April 2016 on the protection of personal data, its processing and free movement. Participation in the study was voluntary and no financial compensation was provided for participation in the study.

### Sample recruitment

It was calculated that a minimum of 395 surveys were required to estimate the proportion of people who reported being influenced by social media in their last aesthetic dental treatment (expected proportion: 50%) with a precision margin of 5%, a confidence level of 95% and assuming a 5% loss rate.

The target population were young social media users who had previously undergone aesthetic dental treatment. Therefore, the inclusion criteria were students over 18 years of age that accepted the informed consent. Exclusion criteria were not having social media or not having previously undergone esthetic dental treatment. The sampling method used was non-probability sampling. Participants were recruited during the celebration of an Oral Health campaign, framed within the IX Oral Health and Healthy Habits campaign of the First Region Official College of Dentists and Stomatologists on 22 and 23 March 2023. Recruitment was carried out by some volunteer students of the fourth year of the Degree in Dentistry of the Universidad Europea de Madrid, as well as by the authors of the study. A link was shared via a QR code that was displayed by volunteers and available on posters at the event.

### Questionnaire

The Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) checklist[26](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR26 "Von Elm, E. et al. The strengthening the reporting of observational studies in epidemiology (STROBE) Statement: Guidelines for reporting observational studies. BMJ 335, 806–808. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.39335.541782.AD
                  
                 (2007).") was used to design the questionnaire. The study was conducted using the Microsoft Forms platform (Microsoft Inc., Seattle, WA, USA), which did not require registration for access. For validation purposes, a first version of the questionnaire was created in Spanish, consisting of 19 questions distributed over four pages and divided into three sections. The final questionnaire was available in both Spanish and English, allowing participants to choose their preferred language.

Informed consent section. This section provided information about the aims of the study, explained that data collection would be anonymous, informed participants of their right to withdraw from the study at any time, information about the principal investigator was provided (Y.F) as well as information about the location and method of storage of the data collected. Consent was obtained through a dichotomous question (yes/no). Only participants who responded affirmatively to this question were included in the study.

Sociodemographic characteristics section. First, an open question asked for a nickname. Then, age was asked with a closed polytomous question (18–25; 26–35; > 36) and sex (male, female), being a student (yes/no) and having had aesthetic dental treatment (yes/no) were asked with dichotomous questions. Participants were then asked about the most recent dental treatment (orthodontic treatment; invisible orthodontic treatment; teeth whitening; veneers or crowns; other treatment) and when it was received (less than one year ago; within the last two to five years; more than six years ago) using two closed polytomous questions.

Participants' social media behavior section. Participants were asked if they had a social media account (response: yes/no). If they answered yes, they were asked about their general use of social media through four closed, polytomous questions:

* Social media platforms on which they had an account (response: Facebook; Instagram; Twitter; LinkedIn; TikTok; Snapchat)
* Most frequently used social media (response: Facebook; Instagram; Twitter; LinkedIn; TikTok; Snapchat)
* Frequency of their use (response: daily; weekly; monthly; occasionally)
* Preferred time of day (response: morning; afternoon/evening; night).

Then, participants were asked whether they had sought information about their most recent dental treatment on social media (response: yes/no). If the answer was yes, participants were asked if social media had influenced their decision to undergo an aesthetic dental treatment (response: yes/no). If the participant responded affirmatively, the questionnaire proceeded to explore the influence of different content displayed on social media in the performance of the last aesthetic dental treatment through 5 questions based on a 3-point Likert scale (agree, neutral, disagree):

* Aesthetic dental treatments social media posts from dental clinics or dentists.
* Aesthetic dental treatments advertised on social media.
* Influencers who have undergone the aesthetic dental treatment.
* Collaborations with influencers.
* The perception that it is a common aesthetic dental treatment.

The questionnaire was tested for validity[17](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR17 "Abbasi, M. S. et al. Impact of social media on aesthetic dentistry: general practitioners’ perspectives. Healthcare (Basel) 10, 2055. 
                  https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare10102055
                  
                 (2022)."),[27](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR27 "Alalawi, A., Aljuaid, H. & Natto, Z. S. The effect of social media on the choice of dental patients: A cross-sectional study in the city of Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Patient Prefer Adherence 13, 1685–1692. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2147/PPA.S213704
                  
                 (2019).") for this purpose. 30 participants were recruited to evaluate the clarity of the questions (0 = no; 1 = unsure; 2 = yes), if they would include the questions (0 = no; 1 = unsure; 2 = yes) and to rate the importance of the questions using a 3-point Likert scale (1 = very important, 2 = important, 3 = not very important). Based on the results, the questionnaire was adapted, and a pilot study was conducted. 40 individuals were then asked to complete the questionnaire and to repeat the process one week later to analyze internal consistency, obtaining scores considered to be highly consistent.

The final questionnaire was on the Microsoft Forms platform. Results were only recorded if the participant completed the questionnaire and selected the submit option. The questionnaire data were only accessible to the principal investigator (Y.F). Upon completion of data collection, the data were downloaded in Excel format and the survey was then deleted to protect data security.

### Data processing

A total of 964 responses were collected. 457 responses were excluded as they did not meet the inclusion and exclusion criteria: 21 did not provide informed consent; 18 were from participants under the age of 18; 129 were from participants who were not students; 245 were from participants who had not received aesthetic dental treatment; and 44 were from participants who were not social media users. 507 responses that met the eligibility criteria were evaluated to identify possible duplicate responses. For this purpose, responses with the same nickname were analyzed, looking at gender and age group. Responses from a later time period were excluded, following the methodology described in the literature, which suggests that first impressions are more reliable[28](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR28 "Fang, H., Lv, Y., Chen, L., Zhang, X. & Hu, Y. The current knowledge, attitudes, and practices of the neglected methodology of web-based questionnaires among chinese health workers: Web-based questionnaire study. J. Med. Int. Res. 25, e41591. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2196/41591
                  
                 (2023)."). Thus, 3 responses were excluded.

### Statistical analysis

Data analysis was performed using SPSS software (IBM SPSS Statistics, v.22, 2013). Sociodemographic characteristics of participants and variables related to social media use were subjected to descriptive analysis. The Pearson chi-square test was used to assess the relationship between variables. The significance level was set at *p* < .05.

## Results

The response rate was 72.22% and the completion rate was 100% as all questionnaires were correctly completed. Finally, 504 responses were included in the data analysis. The average response time was 4 min 17 s. The sociodemographic characteristics of the participants are shown in Table [1](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#Tab1). 68.65% of the participants were female and most participants were aged 18–25 years (84.52%). Most participants reported having undergone an aesthetic dental treatment in the last 5 years, with orthodontic treatment being the most common.

### Participant behavior with respect to social media

### Participant social media behavior with respect to their last aesthetic dental treatment

33.33% of participants indicated that they had used social media to find information about their last aesthetic dental treatment. In addition, 29.37% of participants indicated that social media influenced their decision to have their last aesthetic dental treatment.

No differences were observed between males and females regarding the influence of social media on the last aesthetic dental treatment received or the type of aesthetic treatment received. However, respondents who had undergone an aesthetic dental treatment in the last year were more influenced by social media than those who had undergone an aesthetic dental treatment more than two years ago (*p* < .05) (Table [3](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#Tab3)).

## Discussion

This study assessed the behavior of students in relation to the influence of social media on the last aesthetic dental treatment. The null hypothesis was partially accepted, as significant differences were observed in terms of the time since the last aesthetic dental treatment, but no differences were observed in terms of sex or type of aesthetic dental treatment. Dental aesthetics play an important role in the perception of a visually pleasing face[29](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR29 "Aldaij, M. et al. Patient satisfaction with dental appearance and treatment desire to improve esthetics. J. Oral Health Community Dent. 12, 90–95. 
                  https://doi.org/10.5005/jp-journals-10062-0033
                  
                 (2018)."), with the younger population showing a greater awareness of dental aesthetics[30](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR30 "Alsurayyi, M. A. et al. A cross-sectional online survey on knowledge, awareness, and perceptions of Hollywood smile among the Saudi Arabia population. Open Dent. J. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2174/18742106-v16-e2111261
                  
                 (2022)."). Recently, there has been an increase in the demand for dental treatment for aesthetic purposes[30](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR30 "Alsurayyi, M. A. et al. A cross-sectional online survey on knowledge, awareness, and perceptions of Hollywood smile among the Saudi Arabia population. Open Dent. J. 
                  https://doi.org/10.2174/18742106-v16-e2111261
                  
                 (2022)."),[31](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR31 "Parrini, S. et al. Laypeople’s perceptions of frontal smile esthetics: A systematic review. Am. J. Orthod. Dentofacial. Orthop. 150, 740–750. 
                  https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ajodo.2016.06.022
                  
                 (2016)."), mainly influenced by the appearance of public figures and social media[30](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR30 "Alsurayyi, M. A. et al. S. et al. Impact of social media on aesthetic dentistry: general practitioners’ perspectives. Healthcare (Basel) 10, 2055. 
                  https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare10102055
                  
                 (2022)."). However, it is also important to consider the influence of social media from the patients' perspective. Therefore, this study explored the influence that social media have had on the demand for aesthetic treatments.

In relation to the use of social media to obtain information about aesthetic treatments,. 33.33% of the participants stated that they had used social media for this purpose. These results are in line with previous studies that examined the interaction between dental patients and social media. Previous studies showed that 30% of participants used social media to obtain information about orthodontic treatment[32](/articles/s41598-024-72442-8#ref-CR32 "Siddiqui, N., Chia, M. & Sharif, M. O. There are a few limitations to this study. First, it was conducted in a single country, which means that when extrapolating the results, it is important to consider differences in internet and social media use across countries. Second, the study population consisted of a university population, thus, the results do not reflect the influence of social media on dental treatment in other age groups. Therefore, future research evaluating the impact of social media on other age groups would be necessary. Third, the use of Microsoft Forms allows individuals to complete the survey multiple times. However, the use of a nickname and cross-referencing of demographic data was implemented to minimise this risk.

29.37% of participants indicated that social media had influenced their aesthetic treatment. No significant differences were found between male and female participants or by type of treatment. However, social media was found to have a greater influence on those participants who had undergone an aesthetic dental treatment in the last year. While various factors might influence the decision to undergo cosmetic dental treatment, it is worth noting that social media is increasingly becoming a factor to be considered.

args.summary: This study investigates the influence of social media on students' decision-making regarding aesthetic dental treatments. A cross-sectional web-based survey was conducted with 504 participants (students over 18 who were social media users and had undergone aesthetic dental treatment). Key findings: 29.37% of respondents indicated social media influenced their decision to undergo aesthetic dental treatment. 33.33% used social media to find information about their last treatment. No significant differences were observed between males and females regarding social media influence, nor by type of aesthetic treatment. However, participants who had undergone treatment within the last year were more influenced by social media than those treated more than two years ago (p < .05). Posts from dental clinics or dentists were the most influential type of content, while influencer collaborations were the least influential. The study concludes that social media can influence some patients' decisions to undergo aesthetic dental treatment, and dental practices should consider the increasing importance of social media in their daily practice. The null hypothesis was partially accepted—significant differences were found based on time since treatment but not by sex or treatment type.

# The Role of Social Media in Orthodontics: An Evidence-Based Perspective

* [Dr Mo Almuzian](https://www.orthodonticacademy.co.uk/profile/zl1omar6504732/profile)
* Mar 10, 2025
* 4 min read

Social media platforms like Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, and YouTube allow orthodontists to engage with patients and peers, but misinformation, ethical concerns, and unrealistic expectations remain challenges (Zhu et al., 2022).

**1. Social Media as a Patient Education Tool**

*A. Access to Orthodontic Information*

Studies show that 70% of orthodontic patients use social media for treatment-related information, but 40% of this content is inaccurate (Alsalem et al., 2020; Rossouw et al., 2021). TikTok and Instagram provide insights into fixed appliance, aligners, and oral hygiene, yet often exaggerate treatment outcomes (Gottlieb et al., 2023).

*B. The Role of Orthodontists*

Orthodontists who produce educational content enhance patient knowledge and compliance (Patel et al., 2022). A study by Mason et al. (2023) confirmed that patients who follow orthodontic pages demonstrate better oral hygiene and treatment adherence (Afsharpour et al., 2021).

**2. Social Media in Practice Growth & Marketing**

*A. Branding and Patient Acquisition*

Social media marketing is more cost-effective than traditional advertising, with higher patient engagement rates (Bennett et al., 2021). Facebook and Instagram ads increase consultation bookings, particularly when featuring before-and-after photos (Hassan et al., 2022).

*B. Managing Patient Expectations*

While social media raises awareness, it also fosters unrealistic treatment expectations. Over 60% of patients influenced by social media expect shorter treatment durations (Chung et al., 2023). Misleading influencer content often promotes aligners as a solution for all malocclusions, causing dissatisfaction when results do not match expectations (Johnson et al., 2022).

**3. Professional Networking & Education**

*A. Connecting with Orthodontists Worldwide*

Facebook groups, LinkedIn, and Twitter (X) allow orthodontists to share clinical cases, discuss treatment strategies, and stay updated on innovations (Evans et al., 2020). A study by Wong et al. (2021) found that orthodontists who engage in online discussions improve their clinical decision-making.

*B. E-Learning & Webinars*

Post-pandemic, social media has become an integral part of virtual orthodontic education. Platforms like YouTube, Facebook and Instagram host live case discussions, enhancing knowledge sharing (Park et al., 2022). Webinars hosted by leading orthodontists provide updated research and clinical techniques (Almuzian, 2022, Jones et al., 2023).

**4. Social Media & Orthodontic Research**

*A. Rapid Dissemination of Findings*

Orthodontic journals like AJODO and EJO now utilise Twitter and LinkedIn for research updates, accelerating knowledge translation from academia to practice (Garcia et al., 2021).

*B. Crowdsourcing in Research*

Social media facilitates data collection and study recruitment. A study by Mitchell et al. (2022) reported that Twitter-based surveys increase participant engagement and diversity in orthodontic research.

**5. Risks, Ethics & Professional Boundaries**

*A. Spread of Misinformation*

A 2021 review in the Journal of Health Communications found that 40% of orthodontic-related content on social media was inaccurate, with influencers promoting unverified treatments (Lee et al., 2021).

*B. Privacy, Ethical Boundaries & Professional Conduct*

Orthodontists face increasing challenges in maintaining professional boundaries, patient confidentiality, and ethical marketing on social media. The General Dental Council (GDC, 2023) outlines specific guidelines for dental professionals, emphasising the need to:

• Uphold patient confidentiality – Orthodontists must not discuss clinical cases on public forums or share patient images without explicit consent.

• Maintain professional integrity – Misleading claims, exaggerated treatment outcomes, and undisclosed sponsorships violate ethical standards.

• Avoid private clinical advice online – Social media interactions should not replace professional consultations (AAO, 2022).

The American Association of Orthodontists (AAO, 2022) reinforces that orthodontists must ensure transparency in online communications, particularly in marketing. According to a 2023 GDC report, orthodontists should:

• Keep professional and personal accounts separate to maintain professional credibility.

• Clearly disclose sponsorships or paid promotions to avoid misleading content.

• Refrain from engaging in online disputes with patients or colleagues, as this may lead to legal consequences.

*Additionally, defamation, cyberbullying, or unprofessional online behaviour can damage reputations and lead to GDC investigations or regulatory actions (Dent et al., 2023). The ADA (2023) warns that any breach of online professionalism may compromise a clinician’s registration or practice license.*

**6. Future Trends in Social Media & Orthodontics**

• AI-driven virtual consultations (Smith et al., 2023)

• Augmented reality (AR) treatment previews (Thompson et al., 2024)

• Blockchain for secure patient data sharing (Gonzalez et al., 2023)

• More personalised patient education via AI-powered chatbots (Davies et al., 2023)

A 2023 study predicts that over 80% of patient interactions will begin online by 2030, making social media an indispensable part of orthodontic practice (Brown et al., 2023).

Conclusion

Social media is reshaping orthodontics, enhancing patient education, practice marketing, professional networking, and research dissemination. However, misinformation, unrealistic expectations, ethical challenges, and privacy concerns require careful management. By maintaining an evidence-based, ethical, and professional online presence, orthodontists can leverage social media for the benefit of both patients and the profession.

Key References

• Alsalem et al. (2020) – Social media misinformation in orthodontics

• Bennett et al. (2021) – Social media marketing for orthodontists

• Chung et al. (2023) – Patient expectations and social media influence

• Garcia et al. (2021) – Research dissemination via social media

• GDC (2023) – Professional and ethical guidance on social media use

• Hassan et al. (2022) – Effectiveness of social media ads in orthodontics

• Mason et al. (2023) – Patient engagement with orthodontic education

• Smith et al. (2024) – Ethical challenges in orthodontic social media use

• AAO (2022) – Social media guidelines for orthodontists

Would you like any further refinements or additional references?

Dr Mo Almuzian, 2025

## 市场定义

该市场涉及通过各种治疗解决方案和服务来诊断、预防和矫正牙齿和颌骨不齐。它包括固定牙套、可移动牙套、保持器和正畸配件等产品领域，所有这些产品都旨在牙齿矫正。

市场按年龄组细分，同时满足儿童、青少年和成人的需求，反映出不同生命阶段对正畸治疗的需求不断增长。该报告重点介绍了关键市场驱动因素、主要趋势、监管框架以及影响行业增长的竞争格局。

**正畸市场****概述**

2023年全球正畸市场规模为80.9亿美元，预计将从2024年的89.6亿美元增长到2031年的202.6亿美元，预测期内复合年增长率为12.36%。

口腔健康意识的增强推动了市场的增长。人们越来越认识到牙齿排列在口腔卫生中的作用，这增加了对正畸治疗的需求。

强调早期干预咬合不正和其他牙科问题的长期益处的教育举措促进了预防性护理和整容手术的增加。此外，人们对美观和自我保健的日益关注促使更多成年人寻求正畸治疗，从而推动了市场增长。

正畸行业的主要公司有 Ultradent Products Inc.、Dentsply Sirona、Henry Schein Orthodontics、3M、T.P. Orthodontics、Envista Holdings、Rocky Mountain Orthodontics、Align Technology, Inc.、JJ Orthodontics Pvt.Ltd.、MATT ORTHODONTICS, LLC、Great Lakes Dental Technologies.、American Orthodontics、Institut Straumann AG、G&H Orthodontics. 和 DENTAURUM GmbH & Co. KG

此外，3D打印等正畸技术的突破正在重塑市场格局。这些创新可以实现高度准确的治疗计划以及个性化矫正器和牙套的生产，从而改善治疗效果并减少患者在正畸医生办公室的时间。

3D 打印系统的使用简化了正畸设备的制造，提高了精度、舒适度和效率。这些技术进步通过提供卓越的结果和优化患者护理来促进市场增长。

* *2024 年 4 月，KLOwen Orthodontics 在 AAO 上推出了业界唯一的定制金属自锁 (SL) 解决方案，并荣获 2024 年 Ortho Innovator 荣誉奖。该解决方案将低摩擦结扎与定制处方相结合，提供更短的结扎预约、更快的初始对齐并增强对牙齿定位的控制。*

**主要亮点：**

1. 2023 年，正畸行业规模达到 80.9 亿美元。
2. 预计2024年至2031年该市场将以12.36%的复合年增长率增长。
3. 2023年北美市场份额为36.12%，价值29.2亿美元。
4. 2023 年，固定牙套细分市场的收入为 30.8 亿美元。
5. 到 2031 年，儿童和青少年市场预计将达到 116.6 亿美元。
6. 到 2031 年，牙科诊所市场预计将达到 113.3 亿美元。
7. 预计到 2031 年，直销部门将产生 89.97 亿美元的收入。
8. 预计亚太地区在预测期内将以 13.95% 的复合年增长率强劲增长。

**市场驱动力**

**“越来越关注牙齿健康”**

由于人们对牙齿健康的日益关注，正畸市场正在经历显着增长。随着人们对保持适当口腔卫生的重要性和牙齿排列的长期益处的认识不断提高，越来越多的人正在寻求正畸治疗。

正确的排列可以改善美观并降低出现牙龈疾病、蛀牙和不均匀磨损等牙齿问题的风险。关于错位对整体健康影响的教育的增加进一步推动了人们对口腔健康的日益关注，从而导致更多的人投资于正畸解决方案。

这种优先考虑牙齿健康的转变正在刺激需求。此外，正畸技术和定制选项的进步使治疗更加有效和方便。

* *2025 年 3 月，世界卫生组织 (WHO) 强调，口腔疾病影响着近 37 亿人，构成了重大的全球健康负担。继 2024 年 11 月世界卫生组织全球口腔健康会议之后，通过了《曼谷宣言——没有口腔健康就没有健康》。该宣言强调将口腔健康纳入更广泛的公共卫生目标，包括非传染性疾病、全民健康覆盖和环境可持续性。*

**市场挑战**

**“治疗费用高”**

阻碍正畸市场扩张的一个主要挑战是治疗成本高昂，特别是对于先进的解决方案，例如[透明矫正器](https://www.kingsresearch.com/clear-aligners-market-826)和定制牙套。

许多患者发现这些治疗费用昂贵，这可能会限制获得正畸护理的机会，特别是在发展中地区或没有足够保险覆盖的地区。成本障碍影响患者的采用并限制市场增长。

为了应对这一挑战，市场参与者正在开发技术驱动的解决方案，例如 3D 打印和数字治疗规划，这些解决方案可以简化生产并降低治疗成本。

通过提高效率和减少材料浪费，这些技术可以使正畸治疗变得更加经济实惠和容易获得，从而促进市场扩张并提供优质护理。

**市场趋势**

**“3D技术的进步”**

在 3D 打印系统进步的推动下，全球正畸市场正在经历大幅增长。 3D 打印技术的集成正在彻底改变正畸治疗，可以根据患者的个人需求创建高度定制的矫正器和牙套。

该技术可确保精确贴合，改善治疗效果并提高患者舒适度。此外，3D 打印系统可以更快地生产正畸设备，缩短交货时间并简化治疗流程。

3D 打印可以实现更复杂、更准确的设计，显着提高正畸治疗的效率、灵活性和整体效果。

* *2023 年 9 月，Align Technology, Inc. 推出了 Invisalign 腭扩张器系统，这是其首款基于专有专利技术的直接 3D 打印设备。 Invisalign 隐适美腭扩张器设计用于在乳牙列、混合牙列或恒牙列成长患者的治疗过程中快速扩张并随后固定狭窄的上颌骨（上颌）。它为传统金属腭扩张器提供了安全、舒适且临床有效的替代方案。*

**市场细分：**

* 副产品（固定牙套、活动牙套、保持器、正畸配件）：由于固定牙套在长期正畸治疗中的广泛使用以及在复杂牙齿矫正中的高效性，固定牙套细分市场在 2023 年的收入为 30.8 亿美元。
* 按年龄组（儿童和青少年、成人）：由于早期干预方法和年轻人群中咬合不正患病率的上升，2023 年儿童和青少年占据了 62.09% 的市场份额。

## 正畸市场区域分析

按地区划分，市场分为北美、欧洲、亚太地区、中东和非洲以及拉丁美洲。

2023年北美正畸市场份额约为36.12%，价值29.2亿美元。该地区完善的医疗基础设施、对牙齿美学的高度认识以及正畸专业人员的高度集中，进一步巩固了这一主导地位。

人工智能驱动的治疗计划、正畸矫治器 3D 打印和数字口腔内扫描等尖端技术的采用进一步推动了区域市场的增长。

此外，优惠的报销政策、广泛的牙科保险覆盖范围和高水平的可支配收入使患者能够投资于正畸治疗。隐形正畸选择的日益普及，尤其是在成年人中，促进了区域市场的扩张。

随着牙齿拥挤、畸形、牙齿缺损和牙齿间距不均匀等牙齿问题的日益普遍，对正畸服务的需求也在增加。正畸服务在各种环境中提供，包括医院和牙科诊所。固定正畸器具可以更好地控制牙齿移动。此外，固定牙套需要特殊的维护和基本的口腔卫生才能保持良好状态。根据世界卫生组织 (WHO) 的数据，2022 年全球约有 35 亿人患有口腔疾病。国际美容整形外科协会 (ISAPS) 2022 年的一项调查指出，美国、巴西、墨西哥、德国和印度是进行整容手术最多的前 5 个国家。2022 年，美国和巴西占全球所有整容手术（手术和非手术）的 28.4%。此外，牙医提供的各种优惠和折扣可能有利于正畸服务市场的增长。

### 牙科实验室对 CAD/CAM 的投资创造了丰厚的利润机会

在过去的 25 年里，计算机辅助设计 (CAD) 和计算机辅助制造 (CAM) 已成为牙科领域越来越受欢迎的一部分。这些技术可用于在牙科实验室和牙科诊所制造透明矫正器、定制托槽、种植体基台和全口重建产品。CAD 和 CAM 技术的开发是为了解决三个挑战。第一个挑战是确保修复体具有足够的强度，尤其是后牙。第二个挑战是在保留功能性修复体的同时保留自然外观。第三个挑战是使牙齿修复更容易、更快、更准确。在一些情况下，CAD 和 CAM 技术的运用可为患者提供当天修复。修复体核和框架中使用的高强度结构材料，如氧化铝和氧化锆基陶瓷，只能通过 CAD/CAM 系统来成型，因为这些系统可以延长修复体的寿命。因此，随着对安全且美观的牙科材料的需求不断增加，牙科界可用的 CAD/CAM 系统数量在过去几年中大幅增加。此外，新的高强度陶瓷材料已被引入用于制造牙科设备。由于这些材料与传统牙科加工技术的兼容性有限，CAD 和 CAM 在牙科领域获得了极大的关注。

- **市场规模：** 2023年市场规模为52.4亿美元，预计到2031年将增长至139.7亿美元。
- **复合年增长率 (CAGR)：** 2023-2031年预测期内为13.0%。
- **历史数据：** 2021-2022年；**基准年：** 2023年；**预测期：** 2024-2031年。
- **报告代码：** TIPRE00012149
- **类别：** 生命科学
- **页数：** 150页
- **最后更新日期：** 2025年2月15日

**市场驱动因素和机遇：**
1. **主要驱动因素：** 全球牙科疾病（尤其是错颌畸形）发病率激增；人们对美容牙科的需求和认识增加；牙科保险的扩大；新产品推出；对预防保健日益重视。
2. **关键机遇：** 牙科实验室对CAD/CAM（计算机辅助设计和制造）技术的投资，这些技术用于制造透明矫正器、定制托槽和种植体等产品，提高了修复体的强度、美观度和制作效率。

**市场细分：**
- **按类型：** 固定（牙套）和可拆卸（隐形矫正器）。2023年可拆卸部分占据更大市场份额。
- **按最终用户：** 医院和牙科诊所。2023年牙科诊所占据显著份额。

**区域分析：**
- **北美：** 占据主导市场份额，得益于牙科技术进步和正畸产品获批增加。
- **亚太地区：** 预计实现最高增长率，因口腔疾病患病率上升和人口意识增强，且市场参与者正积极进行地域扩张。
- **其他地区：** 欧洲、中东和非洲、南美和中美洲。

**主要市场参与者（公司）：**
登士柏西诺德公司、3M、Straumann AG研究所、Q and M 牙科集团、武汉大众口腔医疗有限公司、大连美尔牙科、新月牙科保健、对齐正畸、海岸牙科、阿巴诺医疗集团有限公司。

**近期市场动态/新闻：**
- Ormco Corp 推出 Spark On-Demand 计划（2024年5月）。
- Candid 推出正畸平台 CandidPro（2023年2月）。
- Align Technology 将 CBCT 功能集成到 ClinCheck 软件中（2022年3月）。

**报告范围：** 涵盖全球及区域（北美、欧洲、亚太、南美、中东和非洲）层面的市场规模、份额、趋势、PEST/波特五力分析、SWOT分析、竞争格局和公司简介。

## **市场动态**

### **市场驱动因素**

***全球范围内不断增加的牙科疾病负担，尤其是咬合不正，将推动市场增长***

个人的口腔和牙齿健康被认为是全球主要的公共卫生问题。成年人口中牙齿疾病的患病率正在上升，例如咬合不正、牙周病、牙齿严重脱落或腐烂等。咬合不正是牙齿排列不齐，大部分是遗传性的，但有时是由某些疾病引起的，例如颌骨肿瘤和其他牙齿问题。它也可能是由于面部受伤和童年习惯（例如吮拇指）引起的。牙齿咬合不正的特征是一种形态变异，可能与其他疾病和病理状况无关。

全球牙齿咬合不正的高发病率是推动全球正畸市场增长的主要因素之一。患有成骨不全症的患者数量的增加预计将增加全球错牙合畸形的患病率，因为患有遗传性疾病（例如成骨不全症）的患者的患病率更高。

### **市场限制**

***与长期正畸治疗相关的副作用限制了市场扩张***

限制市场增长的因素之一包括与长期正畸治疗相关的不良事件。正畸治疗过程中执行不当可能会导致多种不良反应，例如剧烈疼痛、牙周病、颞下颌功能障碍（TMD）和其他严重影响。正畸托槽在青少年中广泛使用来矫正牙齿排列。尽管如此，托槽仍存在有据可查的缺点，例如牙龈疾病、过敏反应、强直、软组织损伤或口腔溃疡。

所有上述因素的综合作用预计将阻碍正畸产品的采用，进而限制市场增长。

### **市场机会**

***患者群体未满足的需求预计将对市场增长产生积极影响***

咬合不正、反咬合、牙齿歪斜和咬合问题等牙科疾病的日益流行，以及高昂的治疗费用造成了巨大的缺口，导致患者群体的需求得不到满足。一些制造商和组织已开始采取举措，通过合作伙伴关系、服务扩展和其他政策来填补这些空白，以满足未得到满足的患者群体的需求。

与此同时，政府举措的增加和市场参与者之间不断加强的合作伙伴关系预计将为未来的市场增长提供长期机会。

### **市场挑战**

***正畸治疗成本高昂限制市场扩张***

尽管市场正在快速增长，但某些因素在一定程度上限制了市场的增长。治疗成本高昂是阻碍市场增长的因素之一。与治疗相关的成本，加上治疗持续时间长，预计将限制未来几年的市场。

因此，如此高的产品成本限制了接受此类治疗的患者数量，进而阻碍了市场增长。

### **其他挑战**

***有限保险范围***

在许多地区，正畸治疗并未完全纳入保险范围，这给寻求治疗的患者带来了经济挑战。尽管大多数保险公司承保这些治疗，但这样做有一定的条件。在某些情况下，医疗保险承保[正畸牙套](../orthodontic-braces-market-110166)仅当它们被认为具有医疗必要性时。

#### **劳动力短缺**

正畸行业面临人员配置和保留挑战，影响满足不断增长的患者需求的能力。

#### **监管障碍**

应对医疗器械和治疗的复杂监管环境可能会延迟产品发布和市场进入。

## **正畸市场趋势**

***越来越多地采用技术先进的工具被认为是重要的市场趋势***

该领域越来越多地采用人工智能 (AI) 和 3D 打印等数字工具，是市场出现的趋势之一。人工智能自诞生以来已经取得了显着的进步，并具有广泛的解决问题的能力，可以应用于正畸。市场的一个突出趋势是数字工具的使用，包括机器学习（ML）和[人工智能（AI）](../industry-reports/artificial-intelligence-market-100114)，用于诊断和治疗。

因此，结合机器学习和人工智能的 3D 打印牙套和透明矫正器的进步提高了治疗计划和结果的效率，进而推动了整体市场的增长。因此，这被认为是全球正畸市场的重要趋势。

### **其他趋势**

***增加成人患者基础***

由于对改善牙齿美观的渴望以及透明矫正器等谨慎治疗方案的可用性，寻求正畸治疗的成年患者数量显着增加。

### **直接面向消费者 (DTC) 对准器**

DTC 矫治器套件的出现为消费者提供了无需传统去诊所就诊的正畸解决方案，对那些寻求经济高效且便捷治疗的人来说很有吸引力。然而，这种趋势引发了有关治疗质量和结果的争论。运营商采取了各种策略来维持其市场地位。

### **注重美学**

人们对牙齿美学的日益重视导致对兼具功能矫正和美容美化功能的正畸治疗的需求激增。由于卓越的舒适度和更高的美观度，人们倾向于比传统的金属丝矫正器更喜欢透明的矫正器。

## **COVID-19 的影响**

COVID-19大流行的爆发对全球市场产生了负面影响。受疫情影响，领先企业的收入也出现下降。这主要是由于封锁措施、旅行限制和正畸诊所暂时关闭所致。然而，由于数字工具或远程牙科的采用增加，市场出现了显着反弹。这导致在大流行期间越来越多地采用正畸产品，尤其是家用正畸产品，并且预计这种增长将在预计的几年内持续下去。

随着病例数量恢复到大流行前的水平，预计市场在不久的将来将出现显着增长。

## **细分分析**

### **按产品类型**

***透明对准器的广泛采用支撑了耗材领域的主导地位***

根据产品类型，市场分为用品和仪器。

供应部分进一步研究了固定供应和可移动供应。可摘除部分又分为矫正器、保持器等。此外，固定节段分为托槽、带和颊管、弓丝等。此外，固定段可分为常规段和定制段。到 2026 年，供应品领域预计将以 98.21% 的份额引领市场。

到 2025 年，耗材细分市场将在全球正畸市场中占据更高的份额。促进该细分市场增长的关键因素包括新产品推出的增加、透明矫正器的日益普及以及定制牙套等技术进步。此外，医疗保健提供者和制造商之间的合作预计将增加对透明矫正器的需求以及市场上先进产品的推出。   
• 例如，2023 年 7 月，时代天使科技推出了定制透明矫正器，以加强其在美国市场的影响力。

另一方面，仪器仪表领域预计在未来几年将稳定增长。这些是正畸医生在手术过程中使用的工具。印度和澳大利亚等新兴国家的临床就诊和牙齿矫正手术数量的增加预计将在预计几年内推动该细分市场的增长。

### **按年龄段**

***正畸治疗的日益转变促进了成人市场的增长***

根据年龄组，市场分为成人和青少年。

成人细分市场在 2024 年占据了主要份额。这种主导地位可归因于以下因素：寻求日常牙科护理的成年人口不断增长、对各种治疗方法的认识以及成年患者转诊至正畸医生的人数增加。预计到 2026 年，牙医和正畸医生拥有的诊所部门将以 89.68% 的份额主导市场。

相比之下，青少年细分市场也有望在整个预测期内出现显着增长。传统上，青少年是正畸护理的主要接受者。牙齿不齐、颌骨问题、牙齿歪斜和其他牙齿问题在青少年中很常见。而青少年咬合不正的早期发现也增加了透明矫正器和正畸产品的采用。因此，该细分市场正在全球范围内增长。在预测期内（2026-2034 年），该细分市场的复合年增长率可能高达 17.2%。

### **按最终用户**

***牙医和正畸医生自有诊所的正畸治疗患者流量较高，以促进细分市场增长***

根据最终用户，对牙医和正畸医生拥有的诊所及其他诊所的市场进行了研究。

到 2025 年，牙医和正畸医生拥有的诊所细分市场将占据全球市场的最高份额。牙科诊所数量的增加以及全球到牙医和正畸医生拥有的诊所就诊的患者人数不断增长，正在推动对牙齿矫正产品的需求。此外，诊所中易于使用的定制矫治器以及制造商和服务提供商之间的合作伙伴关系进一步推动了该细分市场的增长。预计到 2026 年，该细分市场将占据 89.5% 的市场份额。

另一方面，其他细分市场预计在不久的将来将大幅增长。多专科医院和牙科诊所的出现、报销和牙科保险的改善以及采用牙科保险的人数的增加可能会推动该细分市场的增长。预计其他细分市场在预测期内（2025-2032 年）将以 15.4% 的复合年增长率大幅增长。

The webpage provides a comprehensive market research report on the global orthodontics market by Fortune Business Insights. As of 2025, the market is valued at $8.54 billion, and is projected to grow from $9.5 billion in 2026 to $38.43 billion by 2034, at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 19.10%. North America dominated the market in 2025 with a 42.90% share ($3.66 billion), followed by Asia-Pacific at 24.70% ($2.1 billion) and Europe at 23.00% ($1.96 billion).

**Key Market Drivers:** Rising prevalence of dental diseases such as malocclusion (misaligned teeth), increasing demand for dental aesthetics, and growing adult patient base seeking orthodontic treatment—especially clear aligners.

**Market Restraints:** High treatment costs, limited insurance coverage, adverse effects from long-term orthodontic treatments (e.g., pain, periodontal disease), and labor shortages.

**Market Trends:** Adoption of AI and 3D printing for diagnostics and treatment planning, rise of direct-to-consumer (DTC) aligners, and increasing focus on aesthetics over traditional metal braces.

**COVID-19 Impact:** The pandemic initially hurt the market due to lockdowns and clinic closures, but recovery was driven by increased adoption of digital tools and teledentistry.

**Segmentation:**
- **By Product Type:** The supplies segment (including fixed supplies like brackets, bands, archwires, and removable supplies like aligners and retainers) leads with 98.21% share in 2026. Clear aligners are a major driver.
- **By Age Group:** Adults held the dominant share in 2024, while the adolescent segment is projected to grow at 17.2% CAGR.
- **By End User:** Dentist- and orthodontist-owned clinics dominate with 89.5% market share in 2026.
- **By Region:** The U.S. market alone is expected to reach $3.53 billion in 2026; China $740 million; India $390 million; Japan $460 million; Germany $460 million.

**Key Players:** Align Technology, Inc. (Invisalign), Ormco Corporation (Envista), Institut Straumann AG, Dentsply Sirona, 3M (Solventum), and Henry Schein Inc. dominate the competitive landscape.

# 德勤中国联合艾尔建美学、中国整形美容协会发布《中国医美行业2024年度洞悉报告》

## 中国医美消费新动向

德勤中国携手艾尔建美学和中国整形美容协会发布*[**《中国医美行业2024年度洞悉报告》**](/content/dam/assets-zone1/cn/zh/docs/services/consulting/2025/deloitte-cn-consulting-dtt-china-medical-aesthetic-industry-outlook-2024-zh-240624.pdf)*（以下简称“报告”），本报告旨在深度解读当下中国医美行业需求者的个性化品质医美需求，为行业如何持续提供优质、安全的治疗体验及为需求者创造长期价值，提供基于全新视角的解题思路。

报告通过案头研究、医美行业专家深度访谈，以及针对两千余名中高收入医美需求者（家庭年收入大于30万）和超过600家医美机构（涉及超过100个城市）的调研，总结概括中国医美行业发展的最新洞见、前瞻思考与趋势研判。

**中国整形美容协会会长张斌**表示：“作为医美高品质发展理念的行业倡导者，中整协一直积极推进创新和行业健康发展，联动追求品质医美的上下游合作伙伴，并时刻关注从宏观环境到微观体感的变化。此次与德勤和艾尔建美学共同推出《中国医美行业2024年度洞悉报告》，希望有助于与上下游合作伙伴共同得出具有实用价值的品质经营启示，为医美需求者提供优质、可靠、个性化的服务和治疗体验。”

**德勤中国生命科学与医疗行业主管合伙人简思华**表示：“2023年，医美行业站在了新的发展节点上，不仅见证了行业的自我革新，也映射出需求者对医美品质日益增长的期待。我们希望洞察报告能够为行业决策者提供新的视角和思路，促进行业健康有序发展。我们坚信通过不断创新和服务升级，医美行业能够更好地满足需求者对美好生活的追求，成为经济发展中的一支新动力。”

**艾尔建美学中国总经理丘汉华**表示：“无论医美行业的内涵外延如何拓展，技术理念更迭如何迅速，商业模式如何演进，以创新和品质为驱动的内核从未改变。艾尔建美学将凭借自身产品研发和创新能力、对医美市场和需求者的洞察能力以及专业人才的储备能力等，一如既往紧密携手行业伙伴，助力中国医美行业全面的品质升级之路。”

***医美市场增速稳健，注射及能量源类治疗前景乐观***

2024年是推动消费从企稳恢复转向持续扩大的一年，也是医美行业提质升级的关键一年。医美行业作为兼具医疗属性和情绪消费特点的“新质消费力”之一，在这一年充分见证了医美需求者悦己诉求以及对医美行业信心的进一步提升。

报告显示，2024年服务型消费修复，预计中国医美市场增速可达10%左右；受医美渗透率不断提升和多元化品质医美需求驱动，中国医美市场预计在未来几年内仍可保持10%至15%的快速增长。

其中，注射类医美治疗因其效果相对更显著，能够满足成熟需求者进阶需求等特性，预计在未来五年内保持20%至30%的复合增长率；能量源类医美治疗因其非侵入式特点，需求者接受度更高等因素，预计同期复合增长率在15%至20%。

医美行业资深人士表示，上游厂商不断通过高品质产品和服务的获批交付，助力行业迈向品质医美新阶段；同时，合规监管趋严和自律自治不断促使行业回归医疗本质，为行业高品质时代持续创造内生动力。

***医美需求侧趋向理性，愿意为品质买单***

报告发现，在医美需求K型分化的趋势下，追求品质医美的中高收入群体仍强势增长。医美需求者在追求性价比医美的同时，更加追求优质安全与个性化兼具的品质医美服务和治疗体验。

数据显示，2023年，91%中高收入医美需求者的医美支出较上年稳中有升，增加的主要原因是项目升级或增加项目种类；展望2024年，绝大多数中高收入医美需求者将继续维持或增加医美消费金额，尤其青睐光电和注射类项目的持续消费。

***医美机构专业性备受关注，治疗从面部向身体拓展***

报告显示，过去一年医美消费额超过5万元的需求者更注重医美机构的专业性，会根据不同机构或医生擅长的项目做出治疗选择。他们对注射类项目仍然愿意持续高投入，而身体塑形作为蓝海项目，将是未来的增长引擎。

管中窥豹：从口腔和体检看消费医疗行业的2024

2025-04-09 09:00  [查看原文](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s?__biz=Mzg3NTU0OTkyNg==&mid=2247498045&idx=1&sn=509310c2b11e1fb6bbd85799375c3e44)

收藏

**引言：**

1. 消费医疗行业因为兼具消费与医疗的双重属性，一直以来被视为投资的优质赛道，其核心优势在于融合了消费行业的高增长潜力与医疗领域的高专业壁垒，多个细分领域都在过去的很多年里受到热捧。具体来说，消费属性赋予该行业直接面向消费者的市场活力，依托居民健康意识提升与城市化/老龄化趋势，多个消费医疗细分赛道都享有了较高的行业增速；而医疗属性则通过技术门槛、资质审批及服务严肃性表现出强需求粘性与品牌溢价空间，为行业的长期稳定发展提供保障。

2. 然而，消费医疗行业在过去享有双重红利的同时，近年来也面临了双重挑战：消费端受经济消费降级影响，消费者对非必需医疗服务的支出趋于谨慎，支付意愿与客单价承压；医疗端则因政策监管持续收紧，合规成本攀升，例如广告限制、集采政策等倒逼企业调整经营模式，部分中小玩家面临淘汰。

3. 尽管短期阵痛可能难以避免，但是行业长期发展逻辑依然稳固。我们坚信，技术创新将推动产品、服务价值升级；政策规范化虽加剧竞争，但也为头部企业创造整合机遇，加速行业集中度提升；总体而言，我们相信消费医疗行业具备穿越周期的韧性，未来在大环境实现回暖复苏之后，行业的繁荣很值得期待。

PART 1

**口腔行业**

**口腔医疗服务的基本情况**

中国口腔医疗服务市场规模在2023年大约有2700亿元，其中正畸服务和种植服务是最大的两块市场，分别有约540亿和610亿元的市场规模。

中国口腔医疗服务市场在过去多年来保持增长，但是增速呈现逐步下滑的趋势。在15-19年，行业的年化增速可以在15%左右，19-22年增速低于10%，22-24年可能在5%左右。渗透率的逐步提升+市场竞争的加剧+一些特定事件（集采，消费降级）是导致市场增速放缓的原因。

种植服务市场在2016-2021年年均增速15-20%。2023年种植牙集采落地后至2024年，行业增速回落至10%。种植牙属于刚需医疗消费，行业长期增长逻辑受益于人口老龄化趋势，推动缺失牙修复需求持续释放。然而，消费降级趋势对市场产生一定冲击，高端种植需求可能受抑制。种植牙集采政策的实施有效降低终端支付成本，在一定程度上缓解消费者价格敏感度，有助于维持市场需求韧性并推动行业规范化发展。

正畸服务市场在2014年左右开始蓬勃发展，2014-2022年年均复合增长率约15%。2022-2024年市场增长趋于停滞。正畸服务属于相对非刚需医疗消费，市场需求受宏观经济环境及居民可支配收入变化影响较大。在消费降级趋势下，消费者对高价隐形正畸的支付意愿下降，推动市场向性价比更高的传统正畸方案倾斜。此外，出生率下降对青少年正畸市场形成长期压力，导致新增需求放缓。

**我们区别于市场的观点**

1. 消费降级对于消费医疗赛道的冲击超出预期。新冠结束以来，在经济增速放缓+未来收入预期不理想的情况下，各行各业出现了普遍的消费降级潮，对于消费医疗各赛道的波及更是显著。具体而言，越是刚需性弱、越是不符合消费者心理的消费医疗行为，衰退的速度越是明显。此外，针对男性、青年人等群体的消费行为，受到的影响更大于针对女性、儿童、老年的消费行为。

2. 回到口腔行业，尽管种植牙经历了集采，但是由于治疗刚需性较强+以价换量效应明显，在集采降价+渗透率提升的叠加影响下，种植服务未来3-5年依旧会有增长，高端种植体的增速可能会更高。放眼10年后，在老龄化进程中，65后到80后这一代“有更强自我消费力”的人群开始步入老龄，种植牙需求提升，将会带来种植牙赛道的另一波高速增长潮。

3. 口腔服务行业处于产能过剩，陆续出清的阶段，所以盈利能力大幅下降，大量民营口腔医院为了生存开始忽视质量，选择低价产品，这可能使得口腔上游行业陷入一段时间的严重价格竞争，带动上游行业也进行产能淘汰，有成熟海外渠道的企业更有可能成为成功者。

**口腔上游行业的分析**

**01 口腔上游的产品分类**

口腔耗材设备赛道是口腔医疗服务的上游，涵盖了口腔诊疗过程中所必需的各类器耗材与设备。按照我们的分类方法，可以按照齿科不同治疗场景对赛道进行分类，包括预防材料、填充修复材料、根管材料、义齿材料、种植牙材料、正畸材料等耗材，以及口腔综合治疗台、CT、口扫设备、其他口腔设备等各个细分赛道。

资料来源：GL研究，专家介绍

**02 口腔上游行业的过往市场情况**

在市场规模上，上述所有赛道合计的市场规模在2023年约为252亿，整体上由于口腔医疗的低渗透率，整个赛道在过往5年有较好的增长（年均增速13%），但是拆分来看，不同赛道的过往增速有较大的差异。

简单而言，可以把不同过往增速的赛道归成三类：

1. 增速跟随口腔行业服务量增长而增长的耗材：如预防材料、充填修复材料等。

2. 由于中国vs海外有低渗透率低基数，且治疗效果明确，消费者意识快速提升，外加医疗服务机构重点耕耘这些业务，因此过往增速较快，是整个口腔上游赛道的“扛把子”：如种植牙材料、前几年的正畸材料等。

3. 由于被其他产品或者技术取代，增速低于整体行业增速，甚至出现衰退：如活动牙、传统印模材料等。

资料来源：综合专家访谈、机构研报、上市公司招股书

**03 种植牙与正畸的分析对比**

对于种植和正畸这两个最大的细分单品，我们首先回顾了这两个行业在2024年的表现，并逐个分析了集采、消费降级、老龄化、低出生率等中长期因素的影响。综合来看放眼未来，种植牙行业的基本面可能要好于正畸行业。

资料来源：GL Analysis

**04 口腔上游的未来市场预判**

结合过往赛道增速情况和未来发展因素分析预测，在理想情况下，行业未来增速可以达到10%左右。对于各个赛道的增速，由于受到耗材集采+老龄化趋势+低生育率+消费降级等多个因素的叠加影响，不同赛道的增速有较大差异，具体分析请见下表。

资料来源：综合GL过往研究、行业专家访谈、上市公司招股书

PART 2

**体检行业**

**体检中心赛道基本面分析**

2019-2022年，中国体检中心市场年均增速6.1%，其中民营体检中心市场增速达15.5%，表现优于整体行业。2023年初疫情防控政策调整后，前期积压的体检需求集中释放，叠加“阳康”群体健康关注度提升，推动市场短期增长。然而，2023年至今，受宏观经济环境变化及消费端支出收缩影响，行业增速显著放缓甚至趋于停滞。

体检服务整体刚需属性一般，需求受宏观经济环境及消费能力影响较大。在消费降级背景下，消费者更倾向于选择毛利率较低的基础体检套餐，对高端体检服务需求有所收缩。行业长期增长逻辑与人口老龄化趋势及国家鼓励疾病早筛早诊政策相契合，但短期内宏观经济下行压力，特别是民营企业经营困难，对行业增长形成显著冲击。

**我们区别于市场的观点**

1. 体检服务行业的高速增长时期（2010年-新冠前）已经过去，过去几年的市场整体增速已经较低，且部分头部玩家的经营表现不佳，站在目前的节点看，行业的可盈利性有一些挑战。放眼未来3-5年，如果宏观经济持续下行，会继续影响行业的发展，这种影响不仅仅落到个人的消费意愿降低上，也落到了企业对于员工体检支出的收紧上，因此体检市场未来衰退的概率不低。此外，客单价的下滑和头部玩家的价格战大概率会拓展到所有玩家，内卷的程度会进一步加剧。

2. 企业客户的资源、体检机构的品牌、机构数量及便利性是大玩家之间竞争的核心要素，头部企业通过多年累积的品牌背书和高投入的销售费用来拓展业务，在全国范围内树立了优势。但是部分区域性中小体检机构的经营表现，特别是利润率表现可能优于这些头部大机构。核心原因是这些区域性机构主要通过地方性人脉关系，以较低的费用投入带来更多的客户资源，同时在当地聘请具有强大社会资源和人脉资源的员工，确保了其在当地市场的强劲表现，这些“区域龙头玩家”可以享受较高的毛利率（~60%）。

3. 尽管如此，地方中小体检机构资本规模与稳定性弱于头部企业，整体利润被限制在几百到几千万左右，在重资产和头部效应集中的背景下，中小企业又局限于地方资源优势的依赖，一旦遇到全国性巨头的针对性竞争，或者宏观经济持续下行风险未来不会消除，那么资本投资这些区域性巨头的风险较高，且这类投资的退出的难度与不稳定性也较高。

**行业整体回顾**

2019年中国健康体检行业（包括民营机构和公立医院）的市场规模为2280亿元，到2022年这一数字为2720亿元，CAGR=6.1%。如果只关注民营机构，那么民营机构2019年的市场规模为388亿元，2022年这一数字为598亿元，CAGR=15.5%。

2022-2023年，整体市场和民营机构的增速我们预估分别在10%和20%左右，但其增长的驱动因素来自疫情封闭导致的正常体检需求在被积压后快速释放，外加一部分新冠康复患者的“阳康后体检需求”，因此这一增长并不可持续。

数据来源：综合专家访谈、前瞻产业研究院研报、上市公司年报

往前追溯，体检行业的爆发期开始在2010年前后，这一行业从2010年到2019年之前享有较高的增速，部分年份的增长速度甚至达到了25%。而这一市场增速在2019年前后开始放缓的主要原因我们认为并不是新冠疫情，而是在经过了低渗透率的早期发展后，体检需求增速的自然放缓导致。

行业需求情况健康体检行业的客户群体可以大致分为三类：民营企业、国企和公务员单位、个人。

按照收入拆分，公务员和国企单位占比约为40%，民营企业占比约为30%，个人体检占比约为30%，但是每类客户群体的收入占比存在地区差异。

* 民营企业：在四线、五线城市，民营企业的体检占比在20%以下；在一线城市（如北上广深），民营企业的体检需求占比较高，通常在30%至40%之间；
* 国企和公务员单位：在内地，尤其是四线、五线城市，国企和公务员单位的体检需求占比较高，可能达到60%-70%，在一线城市约占30%-40%；
* 个人体检：各地均保持20%-30%的占比。

从毛利率的角度看，个人业务的毛利率最高，随后是国企和公务员单位，最后是民企。

在经济大环境收紧的背景下，2024年行业的发展有所衰退：

* 国企和公务员单位的体检需求量没有减少，但由于政策变化，一些体检项目转向公立三甲医院；
* 民营企业客户在降本增效的背景下，体检需求减少，体检的套餐标准也降低，引发各体检机构价格战争抢市场份额，整体净利率下降；
* 个人体检市场虽然也受到个人消费降级的影响，但是电商平台的体检套餐售卖热度增长，这两个事件的影响对冲，这部分市场没有明显衰退。

**行业竞争情况**

市场集中度方面，2023年民营机构体检人次约1.18亿人次。而根据各企业财报显示，2023年头部3家民营体检中心体检人次共4063万人次，在客单价接近相同的假设下，市场集中度CR3约为34.4%。

经济下行背景导致消费者对健康体检服务的价格敏感度提高，行业卷价格现象加剧。在头部玩家中，有企业通过降价策略来吸引客户，甚至以最低折扣以保本运营；而有企业选择保持较高的利润率，这使得其营业额在24年有一定下滑；也有龙头企业打算逐步提高单价，并取消不符合预期利润的体检项目。整体而言，随着市场需求增速下滑+宏观经济承压，行业的竞争格局趋于激烈，各家企业如果希望继续扩大营收和保持利润率，则需要采取更多的措施。

**赛道历史融资情况**

2020-2021年健康体检行业投融资事件数量分别为19起、18起，2023年行业共发生投融资事件4起，2024年1-6月发生2起。融资规模方面，2020年行业融资规模达21.8亿元，为近5年峰值，2023年融资规模仅1.6亿元，2019-2024年我国健康体检行业投融资活跃度整体呈下降趋势，市场对于体检赛道热情度有所下降。

数据来源：IT桔子

**未来展望**

**01 行业发展有利因素**

1. 人口老龄化和慢性病患病率的上升，主动健康管理和定期体检的需求日益增长，同时健康体检的需求呈现多元化趋势，拓宽了市场空间。

2. 电商平台的普及，越来越多的消费者通过互联网渠道购买体检服务，美团、抖音、快手等平台上品牌宣传力度和个人体检需求持续增长。

3. 健康体检行业与健康管理、保险、养老等增值服务的深度融合，催生了新的商业模式和市场机会。体检后的健康定制管理业务（如减肥，控糖计划）虽然规模较小，但毛利远高于传统体检服务，成为各大体检中心拓宽业务的新发力点。

**02 行业发展不利因素**

1. 在经济下行周期，可能导致对健康体检服务的需求下降，企业经营不善会降低对于员工体检的支出，个人消费降级也会影响参加体检的意愿，尤其是高端体检套餐受到的冲击会更大。

2. 行业进入门槛一般，主要壁垒为资金与资源渠道而非技术与专利。不同于眼科医疗服务（需要较高的CAPEX壁垒）、齿科医疗服务（依赖医生的专业技术），体检服务行业的门槛可能低于其他这些医疗服务赛道。

3. 健康体检行业毛利率一般（45%左右），外加医疗服务行业的销售费用天然较高，导致行业的净利率较低，大量企业的净利率低于10%，甚至近1年来出现亏损。较低的毛利率使得行业的盈利能力受到较大的挑战。

This article from 医药魔方ByDrug (published April 9, 2025) provides a detailed analysis of the consumer medical industry in 2024, focusing on two key sectors: **oral/dental care** and **health checkup (physical examination) services**.

**General Context:** The consumer medical industry faces dual pressures from economic consumption downgrades and tightening healthcare policy regulations. While short-term pain is expected, long-term growth drivers remain intact due to technological innovation, aging demographics, and industry consolidation.

**Part 1: Oral/Dental Industry**
- China's oral medical service market was ~270 billion RMB in 2023, with orthodontics (~540 billion) and dental implants (~610 billion) as the largest segments.
- Growth has slowed: 15% CAGR (2015-2019), under 10% (2019-2022), ~5% (2022-2024). Causes include penetration rate increases, competition, and specific events (collective procurement, consumption downgrade).
- **Dental implants:** Growth slowed from 15-20% (2016-2021) to ~10% post-collective procurement (2023-2024). Long-term growth is supported by aging demographics, though high-end demand may be suppressed.
- **Orthodontics:** Growth stalled from 2022-2024. As a non-essential service, demand is highly sensitive to disposable income. Birth rate decline pressures the youth market.
- **Key divergent views:** Consumption downgrade impact is stronger than expected; non-essential services for men and young adults are hit hardest. Dental implants will still grow due to price-volume effects. The dental service industry is in a phase of overcapacity and price competition, with upstream players possessing mature overseas channels likely to succeed.
- **Upstream market:** ~25.2 billion RMB in 2023, growing at 13% CAGR. Growth varies by sub-segment: preventive/filling materials follow service volume; implants and orthodontics were high-growth leaders; older products (e.g., removable dentures) are declining.
- **Future outlook:** Implant fundamentals are stronger than orthodontics. Ideal industry growth rate is ~10%, but varies significantly by sub-sector.

**Part 2: Health Checkup Industry**
- Market size: 228 billion RMB (2019) → 272 billion (2022), CAGR 6.1%. Private sector grew faster at 15.5% CAGR (2019-2022).
- Post-COVID demand surge was temporary. Growth has slowed/stagnated since 2023 due to macroeconomic pressures.
- **Key divergent views:** The high-growth era is over. Profitability is challenged. Customer segmentation: state-owned/social insurance (40%), private enterprises (30%), individual (30%). Economic downturn is reducing enterprise spending on employee checkups. Price wars are intensifying.
- **Regional dynamics:** Private enterprises dominate checkup demand in first-tier cities (30-40%), while state-owned units dominate in lower-tier cities (60-70%). Regional small-to-medium players may have better profit margins (~60%) than national giants due to lower customer acquisition costs.
- **Competition:** CR3 (top 3 private players) ~34.4% of 1.18 billion checkup visits in 2023. Price competition is severe. Net profit margins are low (most below 10%, some losses).
- **Financing:** Active investment in 2020-2021 (19-18 deals, 21.8 billion RMB peak) declined sharply in 2023-2024 (4-2 deals, 1.6 billion RMB).
- **Future outlook:** Favorable factors: aging population, e-commerce channel growth, integration with health management/insurance. Unfavorable factors: economic downturn, low entry barriers (capital/resources vs. technology), low net margins (~45% gross margin, <10% net margin).
